Daiki Hakono (箱はこ野の大だい希さ, Hakono Daiki?) was a boy who became trapped in the world of Danmara at a young age after receiving the cursed trunk keeping the Fairy-Tale Card locked up.

Appearance

Daiki's most notable features are his circular eyes and snout-like nose, which are features he retains throughout all his appearances. As a child, Daiki had a bowl cut and wore light clothing, but as he grew into an adult he grew a much more scruffy appearance, now donning a moustache and beard. Attire-wise he was clad in a pair of underwear and a light button-up shirt, as well as the helmet that all Danmara players wore during their first task.

Upon rapidly aging, his hair had grown both longer and white, with his beard now connecting and reaching his chest. He has also switched out his bicycle helmet for a simple bucket hat, and he now wears a varsity jacket emblazoned with a "B".
Personality

Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Danmara Arc

After visiting Unji Zuma's empty house, Momo and Okarun hear screaming when suddenly Daiki shows up, half naked and holding a sword. The two start running and Momo is able to immobilize him while Okarun calls the police, but Daiki was being followed by a gang who demand to hand him over. After activating his Turbo Granny powers, the gang realizes Okarun is just like Unji. Daiki starts bawling as he doesn't want to go back after he just got out of there, but the duo resolves the fight and the three of them are brought to their hideout where a diorama is located.

Tension rises when the gang reveals that they want to throw Daiki back inside the cursed object to get Unji out, as he was the one living inside in the first place. Daiki reveals that the cursed trunk was given to him when he was a 4th grader as a birthday gift, but when he touched it, he was transported inside Danmara. He survived for many years, avoiding monsters and eating sweets, but when he decided to take his own life, a girl from the hideout approached him. As soon as he touched her hands, he was sent back to the real world and was offered to live inside Unji's home to figure how to return to a normal life. Unji swapped places with the girl to destroy the world and prohibited anyone from accessing the diorama. However it has been more than a week since he entered with the Golden Ball given to him by a mysterious figure, so they once again try to send Daiki inside. He tries to fend off the teenagers by swinging his sword, but Momo accidentally falls back and touches the diorama, disappearing.

He listens to Okarun and the gang discussing on what to do before he turns into his Turbo Granny form to run towards the Ayase residence. After the final boss is defeated and the final seal is broken, Fairy Tale Card gets freed inside the Danmara. He explains how he freed the old man and the girl since they didn't want to play the game, but in the meanwhile they could tell everyone what they had seen and bring more people in the cursed trunk. Daiki and two girls are shown talking together, hoping to bring as many people as possible inside the diorama to make the rescue easier. Okarun recruits Turbo Granny, Rin and Mai to bring everyone out of Danmara and Daiki is there assisting them. He gets scared when Mai turns into an eldritch form and surrounds Rin to put her inside her idol clothes. When the hip hop duo turns on the music and Rin starts singing, Daiki and the others start cheering her on.

Everybody gets brought out by Rin, but Fairy Tale Card is also able to escape by using Zuma's Umbrella Boy form. Later in the fight, the yokai begins possessing the teenagers with his powers, so Daiki and other still conscious members try to protect Rin from the attacks. Thanks to the efforts of Okarun, Count Saint-Germain, Rokuro and Masamichi Bega, the Fairy Tale Card is defeated and Daiki gets helped by the gang members after he got injured in the brawl and lost his helmet. In the following days Daiki, along with the hideout's friend group, together visit Unji in the hospital, begging for his help. Unji is surprised to see all of them safe, but insists to keep quiet to avoid disturbing the other patients.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Outside of Kami High, Renjaku's students start guarding the school's gate, intimidating anyone who tries to leave. The girls of the school ask Okarun to talk to them, so along with Bamora and Momo, he approaches them. Unji recognizes Okarun and walks to him, demanding to see the girl he adventured Danmara with. After he discovers that she has turned small, he brings out a really old Daiki with a full grown white beard, explaining that he has been aging unnaturally since the whole Danmara incident. Thanks to his dad Bega they were able to find his parents, though they treated it as a sick joke due to Daiki disappearing just four years ago. Upon hearing his story, Zuma felt sad for him and wanted to help him out. Momo agrees and asks him to come to her house, but the conversation is cut short when Jiji and Aira attack Zuma and retrieve Momo, believing he's one of the power users with the task of stealing Momo's powers just like Kouki.

The group walks towards the Ayase residence with Unji carrying Daiki on his shoulder, however the tension is still high. Once there, Seiko brings good news as they might be able to turn Momo back to normal and they all prepare to depart to Shimane. Seiko notices the trio so Momo introduces them and asks her to examine Daiki because he too was stuck in the cursed trunk. Unji also adds that he was in seventh grade when he entered and he's now aging at an incredible speed. Seiko theorizes on a quick glance that it must be the same curse placed on Momo and orders them to come, even covering their travelling expenses. When Kinta arrives to inform the group of the blackmailer who approached Kouki, Okarun and Aira decide to remain in Kamigoe City and they rush to the gym to assist Rin.

At the airport, Momo's curse seems to have accelerated as Bamora and Seiko cannot remember her anymore, but also Unji's, who's now blind, and Daiki's, now unable to walk on his own. Raiya picked him up on his shoulders and asked someone to accompany Unji so Seiko orders Bamora to hold his hand. Raiya tells Daiki to be patient a little longer so they can remove his curse, but Daiki wonders why he's going out of his way to help him, considering that the first time they met, he was trying to beat him up with a stick. Raiya admits that he thought he was the one responsible for Unji's disappearance and Daiki is surprised he would go that far for him and asks why. Raiya points out that Unji helped both of them and he reveals how he was bullied when he was younger and Unji came to his rescue, but he also cared about his friends deeply and never left anyone behind. Daiki listens while Raiya explains how the world moves too fast and they try to keep up but they can't, even when trying their best, so they just wanted to be forgiven and be told that they were okay, which Unji did and they'll thus do anything for his sake.

On the plane, Daiki quietly sits between Raiya and Seiko, too tired to mutter a word, even when Seiko is sweating profusely. Because of the attack of the subterraneans, Bamora is forced to summon empty space to protect the civilians by using her suit's heart-pounding hidden mode, teleporting everyone in the pocket dimension other than Unji and Daiki, supposedly because of their curse getting in the way.

The Dark Knight (暗黒騎土, Ankoku Kishi?) was one of the three guardian deities in Danmara keeping the Fairy-Tale Card locked away. In accordance with the functionality of the dimension, his defeat led to not only the yokai's seal being broken but also players acquiring the Carmine (カーマイン, Kāmain?) card where they could utilize his skills.

In Dandadan, he serves as a minor antagonist during the Danmara Arc.

Appearance

The Dark Knight has the appearance of a gigantic medieval knight at least 15 meters tall.
Personality

The Dark Knight was silent and programmed to attack anyone that entered National Border Hill.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Danmara Arc

Following Momo's unsuccessful efforts to scale the wall of National Border Hill, the Dark Knight breaches the wall of the border and casts a threatening gaze in her direction. He then initiates his assault on the player, employing his shield to unleash a cascade of debris from the shattered wall while wielding his sword to strike at her. Soon after, Unji Zuma arrives just in time to defend Momo from the giant's sword attack and unleashes a shockwave from one of his umbrellas after it meets the tip of the Dark Knight's sword, resulting in the Dark Knight being destroyed. As a result, Momo and Unji acquire the Dark Knight card, which they later discover after defeating the Death Pâtissier, enabling them to progress through the subsequent stages of Danmara.

Natural Abilities

Physical Prowess

Immense Strength: As a giant, the Dark Knight possessed a large amount of physical power.

Skill Set

Equipment

Sword [v · e]
The Dark Knight wielded a giant sword, employing it to deliver a variety of devastating slashes to players who ventured into National Border Hill.
Dark Knight Sword

Along with his massive sword, the Dark Knight wielded a massive shield with the Danmara symbol for defense.

The Death Pâtissier (デスパティシエ, Desupatishie?) was one of the three guardian deities in Danmara keeping the Fairy-Tale Card locked away. In accordance with the functionality of the dimension, his defeat led to not only the yokai's seal being broken but also players acquiring the Nom Nom Bongo (モグモグボンゴ, Mogumogubongo?) card where they could utilize his skills.

In Dandadan, he serves as a minor antagonist during the Danmara Arc.

Appearance

The Death Pâtissier was an enormous figure, towering at least 15 meters in height, with a cartoon face; having large, round eyes with lifted up thin eyebrows, a mustache, a curled beard, and lacked a mouth. As implied by his name, he donned the attire of a pastry chef.
Personality

The Death Pâtissier was programmed to play a game of candy based-color tag, attacking anyone in the National Border Hill obstacle who was not in contact with the specified candy he called out.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Danmara Arc

Upon Momo and Unji's entrance in the National Border Hill obstacle course to recover the kintama that accidently fell from Unji's pants, the Death Pâtissier commences his candy-themed color tag game by calling out for chocolate. As Momo is the sole individual in contact with the specified candy, the Death Pâtissier directs his assault towards Unji and the frog shikigami. As the game progresses, Momo, Unji, and the frog shikigami are compelled to navigate the obstacle course in search of the designated candy for each round, all while attempting to recover the kintama. Just as he ends the game after four rounds, the Death Pâtissier notices Momo utilizing her psychic power to latch onto his rolling pin to reach hum and with her Moe Moe Tri-Beam, resulting in the guardian being destroyed and Momo and Unji acquiring the Nom Nom Bongo card.

Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Physical Prowess

Immense Strength: As a giant, the Death Pâtissier possessed a large amount of physical power.

Equipment

The Death Pâtissier wields a giant rolling pin, employing it to deliver a variety of devastating slams to players who fail to listen to his orders while playing a game of color tag based on candy.

Along with his massive rolling pin, the Death Pâtissier wields a massive whisk which uses to attack and stir the players caught inside.

The Earthbound Spirit Crab (地縛霊蟹, Jibakurei Kani?) is an earthbound spirit that was previously bound to a tunnel in Shono City.

Appearance

The earthbound spirit took on the form of a giant freshwater crab. On the back of its shell were the faces of the girls who were previously murdered within the tunnel. On its belly side, the earthbound spirit had four rows of mouths with noses and two large eyes.
Personality

After being comforted by the Turbo Granny, the Earthbound Spirit Crab became very protective of her.[1]
Background

The earthbound spirit came to be after several girls were murdered within a tunnel in Shono City. Some time ago, the Turbo Granny entered the tunnel to console the earthbound spirit, since the spirit comprised of girls who died horribly, and the two came to fuse their beings together.[1]
Synopsis

Turbo Granny Arc

After Momo and Okarun manage to capture the Turbo Granny, the Earthbound Spirit Crab chases after them to free her before they could leave Shono City.[2] While on the pursuit, the Earthbound Spirit Crab is led to a bathhouse at an inn and falls for Momo's trap in being boiled in hot water, causing it to be slowed down as planned.[3] Using the spirits from a nearby cemetery to take control of the citizens, the Earthbound Spirit Crab and the Turbo Granny manage to corner Momo and Okarun and fuse together to put an end to them.[4] However, after Momo uses her psychokinesis to grab on to a moving train heading towards Kamigoe City, the Turbo Granny-fused Earthbound Spirit Crab continues with their chase but soon realize that they were being led to a trap set up by Seiko, resulting in the earthbound spirit being exorcised.

The Fairy-Tale Card (メルへンカルタ, Meruhen Karuta?) is a yokai sealed within Danmara and the creator of the cursed trunk's inner world.

In Dandadan, he serves as the main antagonist during the Danmara Arc.

Appearance

Fairy-Tale Card (Depowered Form)
The Fairy-Tale Card in his depowered form.
The Fairy-Tale Card is a large size yokai whose body is made up of multiple black tendrils with buds that are connected to four cards: a face, an ear, a mouth with a nose, and an eyeball looking up. He speaks through his face card.

After being defeated by Okarun, Rokuro, Unji, and Count Saint-Germain, the Fairy-Tale Card was reduced to a tiny head creature with a hairy beard and tiny thin legs.

Personality

As the creator of the world Danmara, the Fairy-Tale Card views it as a wonderful place he made for humans who are sent. As part of his creation process, he took human necessities into account by having certain parts of the world be made out of sweets, though his knowledge about humans seems to be limited as he assumed that they depend on this substance alone. It can be implied that he is rather patient with players when relying on them to free him, having chosen to keep a little boy player in Danmara until he reached old age. On the other hand, this also gives evidence that the Fairy-Tale Card is self-centered and has no sympathy or remorse for players, as he did not allow the Old Man Player to leave Danmara even though his time spent caused him to fall into despair, which almost caused him to commit suicide. Despite catering to human needs with sweets, the Fairy-Tale Card sees players as pawns to do his bidding and is only willing to allow them to exit Danmara if he deems them to be useless by not participating in the game. Even after allowing them to be free, he views them as being useful enough to act as bait to draw in more players to the cursed trunk once they relay their experience being trapped in Danmara. He also did not adhere to Momo's request to have her and the others leave Danmara even after being freed and tried being manipulative in preventing the band of delinquent players from wanting to return to the real world.
Background

At an unknown point in time, the Fairy-Tale Card came to be after a European sorcerer sealed the evil of this world within Japanese playing cards and had him locked away in a cursed trunk.[1] Unable to break the seals keeping him imprisoned himself, the Fairy-Tale Card targeted humans to do his bidding by creating a realm within the Danmara and turning the cursed trunk into a portal that would send anyone to his world if they were to come in contact with it.

Following a young boy being sent to Danmara and becoming trapped there until he reached old age, the Fairy-Tale Card decides to release him the moment he came encounter a young girl also sent, having viewed him as being useless in his hopes to be released. This sequentially leads to the old man encountering Unji Zuma and him being the new owner of the cursed trunk. Upon Count Saint-Germain's arrival on Earth, the Fairy-Tale Card strikes a bargain with him, offering his powers in return for liberation from the cursed trunk. He then becomes aware of his plan to dispatch Unji to the inner world to break the cursed trunk's seals and have him possess his body to utilize his Umbrella Boy powers to flee. After Unji is sent, the Fairy-Tale Card chose to exit out the young girl who was from Unji's gang, deeming her as useless much like the old man he previously released.
Synopsis

Danmara Arc

Fairy-Tale Card unsealed
The Fairy-Tale Card is released.
Following the destruction of the final seal by Unji, the Fairy-Tale Card is finally liberated, as he had been misled into thinking that destroying the item would result in his return to the real world. Expressing gratitude to all players involved in his freedom, the Fairy-Tale Card notices Turbo Granny in the crowd, acknowledging her new appearance and questioning her allegiance to humans after she warns against making eye contact to avoid being possessed. When Momo asks about leaving Danmara, the Fairy-Tale Card denies the possibility of escape and explains the circumstances surrounding the Old Man Player and the young girl's departure from Danmara. Upon being confronted with Momo's request to set her and the others free, he firmly denies, convinced that the world he has designed fulfills its purpose of providing delight to humans. He is also of the opinion that the delinquent players would rather remain in his world than face rejection in the outside world. When the Fairy-Tale Card hints that the delinquents would prefer it that they cause chaos in the real world, one of Unji's followers falls prey to the yokai's manipulation and turns against Unji. This chain of events leads to the Fairy-Tale Card seizing control of Unji, while also harnessing the full potential of Umbrella Boy's power.

Umbrella Boy awakens
The Fairy-Tale Card takes control of Umbrella Boy Unji.
With the power of Umbrella Boy reaching its zenith, the Fairy-Tale Card identifies it as the crucial element for his liberation from the cursed trunk and bring about chaos to the world. Wanting to have Unji live out his destructive impulses, the Fairy-Tale Card employs Umbrella Boy's shockwave blasts to wreak havoc, which results in Momo losing consciousness. Following Rokuro and Bega's appearance, the Fairy-Tale Card has Umbrella Boy Unji engage the two in battle while airborne using the yokai's propulsion. However, when Okarun devises a strategy to ground him by creating a tornado with a heater made from Rokuro's nanoskin, the Fairy-Tale Card engages them in close combat and loses the second kintama to Okarun. With the kintama now in his possession, Okarun becomes able to activate his Turbo Granny form and fight an even battle against the Fairy-Tale Card. The Fairy-Tale Card is then defeated by Okarun after Unji's body takes a hit from a dropkick that sends him crashing back into the stage platform.

Fairy-Tale Card using Unji's body
The Fairy-Tale Card using Umbrella Boy Unji's powers to escape Danmara.
Following Umbrella Boy Unji's defeat at the hands of Okarun, the Fairy-Tale Card reprimands him, Rokuro, and Bega for hindering Unji's destructive ambitions. He then merges with Unji's body, harnessing Umbrella Boy Unji's powers to launch skyward in an attempt to escape the cursed trunk. As he nearly escapes, the Fairy-Tale Card is taken aback upon encountering the Renjaku high schoolers and Unji's followers, following Rin's use of Mai's Onbusuman gravity manipulation to lift the trapped victims of Danmara out of the cursed trunk.

Upon finally being set free into the real world, the Fairy-Tale Card rejoices and, while Unji is unconscious, expresses his gratitude, vowing that his sacrifice will not be in vain. He then turns to Rin, perceiving her as a potential threat to the world, and tries to take control of her mind. However, his attempt is thwarted by Mai who pushes him back towards a wall. Before Rin has a chance to sing, the Fairy-Tale Card employs its mouth card to have her mouth disappear and proceeds use his powers to prevent the delinquents from attacking him. He soon finds himself confronted by Count Saint-Germain who puts a stop to his mind control over the delinquents using the talismans used for the cursed trunks black cloth to immobilize them. The Fairy-Tale Card immediately recognizes the man and inquires as to why he is getting in his way since he knew all about his plan to send Umbrella Boy to help him escape from the cursed trunk. The Fairy-Tale receives no response from Count Saint-Germain, except for a question in return, inquiring about his identity, much to the yokai's annoyance.

Black Haircutter
The Fairy-Tale Card attacked by Count Saint-Germain.
After using his eye vanishing power to blind Count Saint-Germain, the Fairy-Tale Card commences his attack using his buds. However, Count Saint-Germain deflects the buds and uses his powers to reach the yokai and destroy his mouth card with his sword. The Fairy-Tale Card regenerates the mouth card with one of its buds, declaring it futile for any attempt at defeat due to its capacity for repeated regrowth, and demands an answer to his previous question. Count Saint-Germain instead responds telling him that his arrogance in the midst of their battle will lead to a costly defeat and reveals his strategy to triumph by simultaneously destroying two or all of his cards. As the Fairy-Tale Card becomes doubtful of his ability to accomplish this feat alone, Okarun, Rokuro, and Bega are freed from the cursed trunk and are turned to Count Saint-Germain for assistance in defeating their enemy.

The Fairy-Tale Card defeated
The Fairy-Tale Card defeated by the combined efforts of Okarun, Rokuro, Unji, and Count Saint-Germain.
Finding it disgraceful to be outnumbered, the Fairy-Tale Card brands Okarun, Rokuro, and Bega as cowards and attacks the as they run away. The Fairy-Tale Car's eyeball card is then struck by a particle beam fired by Rokuro, only to have it quickly regenerate. This prompts Count Saint-Germain to disclose to Rokuro and Okarun that the yokai can only be defeated if its cards are targeted in pairs. Surprised to find Unji alive and armed with one of his umbrellas to attack, the Fairy-Tale Card tries to dominate him once again with his mind control. However, this attempt is futile as Unji remains unconvinced by the corrupted words has to say about his mother. As he becomes frustrated by this, the Fairy-Tale Card meets his defeat as his cards are obliterated by a coordinated assault from Okarun, Rokuro, Unji, and Count Saint-Germain.

Defeated, the Fairy-Tale Card is reduced to a powerless state and tries to escape. However, Count Saint-Germain discovers him and insists he acknowledge his defeat, thus preserving his life in accordance with their agreement. Comforted by this resolution, the Fairy-Tale Card concedes and delights in his new liberty. However, Count Saint-Germain's stabbing of the yokai with a small blade to seize its power provokes intense pain and fury in the Fairy-Tale Card. As he demands for the return of his powers while lying on the ground wounded, he listens as Count Saint-Germain reveals his ambition to solve all worldly enigmas and possess all supernatural entities, including the significant Dandadan, and queries the yokai's knowledge of it.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Adachi, who managed to steal Murakami's power, contacted the Orchestrator. At the rendezvous point, she met a strange looking businessman who held out his hand towards her. The Orchestrator then called her and informed her that because she acted on her own and caused trouble for their schemes, she must return all the powers she has. She refuses for her mother's sake and the businessman assaults her but she's quickly rescued by Bega. The businessman manifests the Fairy-Tale Card, however he remembers his emotional fierceness from the Renjaku apartments incident. Because he cannot control his will, he resorts to brainwashing Adachi, sending her towards Bega. The latter easily puts her down, although this gives the Fairy-Tale Card power user enough time to flee the scene.

Former Abilities and Powers

Physical Abilities

Buds: The Fairy-Tale Card fights offensively using his buds as blunt objects, which are strong enough to cause surface damage.

Yokai Abilities

Body Manipulation [v · e]
The Fairy-Tale Card possesses the ability to take control over any human in his presence, with each card having a unique application.
Mind Control
Fairy-Tale Card Body Manipulation - Mind
The face card of the Fairy-Tale Card has the ability to corrupt the minds of humans to take control of them.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The main strength of this power is that it allows the Fairy-Tale Card to control his victims' bodies against their will by forcing them to face their innermost trauma in an effort to mentally break their spirit. He can also bring out the full potential of his victim to use as his strength, however, as a consequence to them, the victim will die as a result of repeated stress to their body. There seems to be no limit to the number of humans he can keep under control at once.

As stated by the Turbo Granny, the power of the Fairy-Tale Card is contingent upon its targets making eye contact; should the enemy shut their eyes, they remain unaffected. Additionally, it holds no sway over yokai. The card's control over an individual's mind can be disrupted if the Fairy-Tale Card is attacked during the process of subjugation, or if the face card is destroyed.
Usage
The Fairy-Tale Card employs mind control to compel allies among foes to battle and even slay one another.
Mouth Erase
Fairy-Tale Card Body Manipulation - Mouth
The mouth card of the Fairy-Tale Card possesses the body manipulation ability to erase a human's mouth.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The main strength of this power is that it allows the Fairy-Tale Card to conceal the mouths of his enemies if he deems that their speech or voice to be a hindrance.

Like with the other cards, this power can be nullified if the card that casted it (in this case, the mouth card) is destroyed.
Usage
So far, this ability has proven effective in preventing Rin from utilizing Mai's Onbusuman ability for gravity manipulation through her singing.
Eye Erase
Fairy-Tale Card Body Manipulation - Eyes
The eye card of the Fairy-Tale Card possesses the body manipulation ability to erase a human's eyes.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The main strength of this power is that it allows the Fairy-Tale Card to induce blindness to a human. With this handicap, the Fairy-Tale Card's victim becomes vulnerable to attacks.

An individual bestowed with extrasensory perception can overcome this power, as they would be capable of evading and countering any assaults launched by the Fairy-Tale Card. Like with the other cards, this power can be nullified if the card that casted it (in this case, the eye card) is destroyed.
Usage
The Fairy-Tale Card employs this ability in combat to secure an advantage over adversaries, who are then unable to discern his location or anticipate his attacks.
Ear Disruption
Fairy-Tale Card Body Manipulation - Ears
The ear card of the Fairy-Tale Card possesses the body manipulation ability to release a potent sound to a human's ears.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The main strength of this power is that it allows the Fairy-Tale Card to disrupt human hearing by emitting a deafening sound that induces dizziness.

Like with the other cards, this power can be nullified if the card that casted it (in this case, the ear card) is destroyed.
Usage
The Fairy-Tale Card utilizes its ability in combat to halt any enemies attempting to attack, stopping them in their tracks.
Possession
Fairy-Tale Card Body Manipulation
The Fairy-Tale Card's body manipulation includes him being able to enter a human's body and take control of them from within.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The primary advantage of this power is its ability to enable the Fairy-Tale Card to possess a human's body, thereby commandeering their motor functions and serving as an auxiliary body. In addition, he can control the human's abilities. The victim still maintains their consciousness and senses when being controlled, though the latter is not shared with the Fairy-Tale Card, as shown when the yokai took control of Unji who was coughing up blood being forced to use Umbrella Boy's propulsion power.
Usage
The Fairy-Tale Card used this power to take over Unji's body and use Umbrella Boy's propulsion power to fly out of the cursed trunk.
Regeneration
Fairy-Tale Card regeneration
The Fairy-Tale Card has the ability to regenerate through its buds, enabling it to restore any one of his four cards that have been destroyed.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The main strength of this power is that it allows the Fairy-Tale Card to restore his cards multiple times if his enemy destroys one of them. As discovered by Count Saint-Germain, who perceived the yokai's even number cards as being similar to the pairings of karuta cards, the Fairy-Tale Card's regeneration will be rendered nullified if two or all of his cards are destroyed simultaneously. Therefore, the collaboration of two or more people is required to accomplish this task.
Pocket Dimension Creation
Danmara's Dimension
The Fairy-Tale Card possesses the power to create pocket dimensions.

She is gang member of Unji Zuma who entered the world of Danmara as its second player.

Appearance

She sports dark hair styled into two buns on her head, with her right bangs dyed. She seemingly wears mascara that highlights her eye. She dons a jacket over her school uniform, which includes a collared shirt with a bow tie, a dark skirt, and long dark socks. After being sent to Danmara, she started wearing a helmet and kept it on until the defeat of the Fairy-Tale Card.
Personality

Synopsis

After surviving many years in the Danmara dimension, Daiki Hakono decides to end his life when he suddenly meets the girl and grabs her hands, sending him back to reality. Zuma later enters the cursed trunk and swaps places with her.

The girl explains how they are all deeply indebted to Unji since he protects them from shady people and allows them to happily hangout in the Renjaku Apartment Complex. She's shocked when Momo is accidentally pushed into the diorama and listens to the boys scrambling for a plan to save Zuma and Ayase.

She later stands outside of the cursed trunk along with Rin, Mai and others. Turbo Granny instructs the outside squad to slowly lower the object on top of the black cloth and the girl attempts to lift it by using a couple of sticks. At the same time, Turbo Granny instructs to not do exactly that, but she's already transported inside the Danmara.

Using the Onbusuman's gravitational powers, she escapes the alternate reality along with all the other Renjaku High School's students and hides behind Rin with other girls.

After the whole Renjaku Apartments Incident, she's part of the friend group who visit Unji and Masamichi Bega in the hospital, who he orders to keep quiet to avoid disturbing the other patients.

The Flatwoods Monster (フラットウッズ・モンスター, Furattouzzu Monsutā?) was an alien and a UMA who was an associate of the Serpos.[1]

In Dandadan, it serves as a minor antagonist during the Turbo Granny Arc.

Appearance

The Flatwoods Monster was a massive, heavily built 3-metre-tall alien (10 feet) with a build similar to a sumo wrestler, with a large belly and bulky, muscular arms and legs which it uses in combat. Its body is grey in color and has numerous lines that run down its sides. Its face that has circular eyes with prominent pupils, a rectangular mouth and an angular nose. Its overall head is not unlike that of a nutcracker. Its head was also adorned by a stocky helmet. Most notably, it possesses a strange hood that surrounds its head. In terms of clothing, it only wore a patterned tsuna. When its arms were destroyed, the Flatwoods Monster grew a pair of extra legs with a polka dot pattern on them.
Gallery

The Flatwoods Monster's color scheme.
The Flatwoods Monster's color scheme.
The Flatwoods Monster's anime concept art.
The Flatwoods Monster's anime concept art.
The Flatwoods Monster's full appearance.
The Flatwoods Monster's full appearance.
Personality

As a subordinate to the Serpos, the Flatwoods Monster executed the tasks assigned to it. It was particularly tenacious in attempting to retrieve Momo and Okarun's 'banana organs,' deeming them dishonorable humans for not fulfilling their "promise" to the Serpos. In addition to its resemblance to a sumo wrestler, the alien also imitated the movements of one, and interestingly, its weakness for touching the ground with its hands aligns with the same sumo rule that dictates a sumo wrestler's defeat. Despite this, however, it did not respect the rules of the game, as it pretended like it was still in the game after Momo and Okarun made its hand touch the ground.
Background

The alien was first sighted in the town of Flatwoods in Braxton County, West Virginia and went on to become known as the "Flatwoods Monster". At some point, the alien came to Japan and had been reported to have been sighted in the Yamanashi Prefecture.[1]
Synopsis

Turbo Granny Arc

The Flatwoods Monster defeated (Anime)
The Flatwoods Monster defeated by Momo and Okarun.
Following Momo and Okarun's escape from the Serpos, the Flatwoods Monster was tasked with retrieving their banana organs. With Momo removing the protective talisman on the torii gate earlier to let Okarun into her house, the Flatwoods Monster becomes able to enter as well and rings the doorbell, which sounds the ominous chime for evil spirits, alerting Momo and Okarun of its ominous presence. Along with Empty Space being erected with a wall to block their escape, the Flatwoods Monster releases its harmful mist to envelope the area and commences its assault on Momo and Okarun, demanding for them to give their banana organs to it. Okarun, after transforming and gaining Turbo Granny's extraordinary speed with the assistance of Momo using her psychic power to suppress his curse from his head, confronts the colossal alien and manages to bite off all the fingers from its left hand. The Flatwoods Monster then takes damage to its right leg after Okarun launches himself, and loses his right arm after it disintegrates from Momo forcing his body to drop down with her psychokinesis, with the girl having figured out its weakness to touching the ground with its hands based on its sumo appearance. Nevertheless, the Flatwoods Monster manages to stabilize itself by sprouting legs from its back. It then retaliates by seizing Momo, slamming her against the wall near the torii gate, and unleashes a flurry of punches. Despite her injuries, Momo reveals that she deliberately let the colossal alien pummel her against the wall in order to have it create a hole deep enough for her and Okarun to end up outside the torii gate, enabling her to use her psychic power to lure him to her location and place the talisman back on the gate, resulting in the Flatwoods Monster's defeat as its body begins to burn to ash from the talisman's effects.[2]

Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Physical Prowess

Enhanced Strength: Befitting its immense size, the Flatwoods Monster had incredibly physical strength, being able to unleash shockwaves with a stomp of its feet and create craters with its punches.

Skill Set

Sumo Wrestling: The Flatwoods Monster unleashed its brute strength by using sumo style foot stomps. Since it fought in such a way, the Flatwoods Monster had the weakness of disintegrating if its hands were to touch the ground, being align with the sport's indication of a wrestler's defeat.

Fūta Zuma (頭ず間ま風ふう太た, Zuma Fūta?) was the younger brother of Unji Zuma. Following his death, his spirit went on to become a yokai known as Umbrella Boy (アンブレラボーイ, Anburera Bōi?, Viz: 'Brella Boy), whose powers is shared with Unji.

Appearance

Human

Futa was a young boy with a shaved head who wore a simple long sleeve shirt and shorts. Gifted by his mother, he wore rain boots as his sole choice of footwear and consistently had an umbrella at his side.

Yokai

Umbrella Boy True form
Umbrella Boy's full appearance.
Umbrella Boy has the appearance of a cyclops; having a large bulging eye with large, exposed teeth. This shadowy head is connected to an abnormally large leg wearing a geta sandal. Most noticeably, and befitting his namesake, Umbrella Boy's body is obstructed by a large, frayed umbrella that has an opening at the front for the yokai to peek through.

Personality

Futa was a genuinely happy child who cherished the umbrella and rainboots his mother gave him.

According to the Turbo Granny, Umbrella Boy is said to be a "sweet yokai" by nature but becomes unstoppable when he is forced to fight.
Background

Having grown up in poverty, Futa treasured the rainboots and umbrella his mother had given him, making a vow to always take them with him wherever he went.[1] After the death of their father, Futa was protected by his older brother Unji as their mother struggled to raise them by herself. On a rainy day, while heading home, Futa ran after his umbrella after it from flew out of his hands, leading to him to a nearby river where he tragically drowned.[2]

Following his death, Futa's spirit went on to become an Umbrella Boy yokai. Years later, at the location of Futa's accident, Umbrella Boy met Unji, who was rushing to rescue Bega and a boy from drowning in the river, and chose to offer his power to assist in their salvation.[3]
Etymology

Futa's first name means "large wind."
Chapter Appearances

Kintama Hunt Saga

[v · e · ?]
Danmara Arc
Current Saga

[v · e · ?]
Kozuka Knives Arc
Trivia

Umbrella Boy takes its design from a classic Japanese yokai called the Kasa-obake, an old umbrella that became a spirit, notable for its singular eye and one leg. Kasa-obake are also called Karakasa-kozo, which literally translates into Umbrella Boy.
Kasa-obake are often depicted as having one leg, but the reason for Dandadan's Umbrella Boy to have one leg seems to stem from the fact that Futa lost one of his boots when he drowned, and as a yokai he ends up only having one geta to stand on.
Futa's name containing the kanji for "wind" is similar to how his older brother's name contains the kanji for "cloud.

Hana (花) is an anthropomorphized anatomical model that resides at the Ayase residence.

Appearance

Hana Anime Concept Art
Hana's anime concept art.
Hana is an anatomical model who's right-side makes up her exposed muscle while her left compromises of her skin half. On her skin half, she is given a tied back hair and has a closed left eye. Unlike her partner Taro, she possesses no limbs to move about and can only be held upright with a round base stand connected to her torso.

After moving into the Ayase residence, Hana is given a beanie and a shirt to cover herself.
Personality

Hana has a very lovey-dovey relationship with her partner, Taro. While interactive towards him, Hana remains completely quiet around others, presumably either because she is too shy or is limited to only communicating with Taro since they are both anatomical models.
Background

Hana developed a relationship with fellow anatomical model Taro during their time at Kami High. At some point, the two became separated after Hana was thrown away for being deemed an obsolete model.
Synopsis

Cursed House Arc

At the junkyard, Hana is found by Taro who was in a rush to reunite with her, which resulted in him catching the attention of Momo, Okarun and Jiji who tracked him down. Hana begs Taro to forget about her since she has accepted her fate but becomes moved to hear Taro's feelings towards her.

Wanting to help her, Hana is offered by Momo to stay at the Ayase residence so that she and Taro may continue their relationship. The next day in the morning, Hana waits outside with Momo to meet with Taro, who ends up running late after getting run over by a truck.

Evil Eye Arc

Hana silently participates in the family dinner. She only reappears while Okarun fights the Evil Eye and gets carried by Momo. Along with Momo and Aira, she gets turned around when the Evil Eye decides to remove his underwear which does not agree with Okarun's deal. Seiko is too tired to deal with their destroyed home and so Hana, Turbo Granny, Momo and her go rest inside a bathhouse.

Momo carries her again back to the Ayase residence when they suddenly discover an alien staring them down. Okarun and Aira secretly called for Mantis Shrimp's aid, who recruited his alien friend Ludris to help rebuild the house. Hana is last seen inside the under-construction Ayase residence.

Etymology

The name Hana means "flower, blossom" (花).
Similarly to her lover, Hana is a generic female name in Japanese, with Yamada Hanako being the Japanese equivalent of Jane Doe.

Hase (ハセー, Hasē?) is a student at Kami High who was a bully to Okarun in Class 2-C.

In Dandadan, he had no significant role during the Kintama Hunt Saga but soon reemerged in the Current Saga during the Kozuka Knives Arc as a major antagonist, having been given Jumping Crone's power by an unknown individual to exact his petty revenge on Okarun for inadvertently ridiculing him at school.

Appearance

Hase has medium-length brown hair that's parted in the middle and falls to the sides of his face. For attire, he wears his school's gakuran outfit.
Gallery

Hase's full appearance.
Hase's full appearance.
Hase´s face with Jumping Crone Form
Hase´s face with Jumping Crone Form
Personality

Hase is a mean student at Kami High who favors bullying his classmate Okarun. However, he has shown himself to be quite cowardly, as he stopped his bullying when confronted by Momo's intimidating glare. Much like Aira's character at the beginning of the series, Hase projects an air of confidence, arrogance, and bravado, largely stemming from his former popularity with the female students. He felt emboldened to approach two girls, brazenly flipping their hair and interrupting their conversation. His inflated ego also drove him to wanting to assert his dominance during gym class by eagerly selecting Okarun as his partner, perceiving him as a weakling who could make him look good. However, after Okarun outperformed him and took away his popularity as a result, Hase became a resentful individual and prone to violent bursts of anger.
Background

Since the beginning, Hase made fun of Okarun's passion for the occult and stole his magazine while mocking him, saying that people who believe stupid conspiracies like those should just die. Okarun quietly submitted to the bully so Hase and his friends kept making fun of him every single day, until Momo showed up in her classroom and made them stop with an intimidating glance.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Turbo Granny Arc

Hase picks on Okarun with his friends by throwing paper balls at him but stops after Momo Ayase sits in front of Okarun and glares at the boys.

Cursed House Arc

Hase, a boy and two girls sneak in Kami High at night to have a séance with the school spirits and he teases the girls by making up fake noises. Suddenly they hear somebody running towards them and they flash the hallway, revealing Taro approaching them at full speed. Frightened, they escape outside and Hase stumbles and falls while the others manage to get away, even though the anatomical model wasn't chasing them and only wanted to go reunite with Hana at the Ayase Residence.

Space Globalists Arc

Hase quietly watches with the rest of the class the new transfer student Bamora, who it's said to come from India, being taught their language by Okarun and Kinta.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

During gym class, Hase asks Okarun to be his partner for physical fitness, confident that he can outrun Okarun easily due to his impressive track time of 6 seconds. However, Okarun quickly outruns him, even beating his record by 0.2 seconds, much to Hase's shock. Following this, Okarun surprisingly manages to outperform the rest of his classmates, causing Hase to wonder aloud how Okarun suddenly became athletic. Later, Hase hears a mysterious voice tempting him to get revenge on Okarun, claiming that Okarun has special abilities and that he can acquire power too and steal Okarun's by using the Asura knives in front of him. Following this, Hase goes about his day as normal while remaining uncertain whether he should heed the voice's instructions. However, when he discovers that two girls are attracted to Okarun upon his approach and is treated as a reject by them and fellow students, Hase becomes prompted to test the voice's claims by cutting himself with the Asura. When he experiences no immediate effects, he initially dismisses the voice as deceitful, only to later sense a presence behind him, signaling the emergence of his newfound powers.

Later, Hase allies with the alien survivor of the Kur's Advance Unit after learning that she too has also been assigned with the task of stealing Okarun's powers. At the entrance to the Kami High gymnasium, Hase uses the Crone's powers to attack Okarun and Kinta after they arrived, along with Aira, to help Rin and Kouki. He and the exosuit alien then confront and chase after the duo around the building. After landing a strong kick to Okarun, who deploys the airbag gauntlets given to him by Kinta to cushion his crash, Hase deactivates his yokai form, taking note at how exhausting it is for him to maintain it and the discomfort it causes to his feet. Hase expresses his frustration to the exosuit alien, stating that her movements are obstructing his efforts to confront Okarun and demands for her to target Kinta instead. While the exosuit alien disregards his request to fine-tune her exosuit, Hase emphasizes their shared mission but, as he re-activates his yokai form, reveals that his primary goal is revenge against Okarun and cautions her to avoid interfering or she might become his enemy as well. After the exosuit alien proceeds to target Okarun, refusing to comply to Hase's orders, Hase is left no choice but to fight against Kinta who is now wearing a miniature Great Kinta as a combat suit.

Noticing his ally almost killing Okarun, he gets enraged and leaves Kinta behind to stop her in her tracks. He again declares that he would be the one to hurt Takakura, but because the lady doesn't seem to back down, he states that he will kill her if she attempts to get in his way again. He kicks her upwards before getting above her and jumping downwards, crushing her to the ground. She's immobilized while Hase continues to plummel her with yokai powered jumps until she's beat to a pulp. Kinta and Okarun see this opportunity to merge in one singular robot and combine their strengths, although the suit is obviously constructed for the former's better control. Hase launches her down the field and mocks her after she's unable to get up due to the series of attacks he gave her, again stating that she mustn't interfere. Hase is suddenly ambushed by the ridiculous robot of the two boys and he weaves their punch, baffled by Okarun's behavior as he thinks he's ridiculing him. Hase uses the Crone powers to blast them away but Kinta orders Okarun to use the verniers and he does just so, successfully parrying his attack. Kinta even performs a Blast Wind, Thrust Attack, however Hase is just too fast to land a hit and the latter insults Okarun since it appears to him that he's holding back his powers against him and rushes him to manifest them. Hase makes quick work of them, leading Okarun to realize that merging was a bad move because of the added weight and nanoskin, flabbergasting Kinta since he always believed the contrary due to the mecha series he loved watching growing up.

The Hastur Kur is the leader of the Kur's Advance Unit who wielded the Hastur.

In Dandadan, he serves as one of the two primary antagonists during the Space Globalists Arc, alongside Reiko Kashima.

Appearance

Hastur Kur (True Form)
The Hastur Kur's full appearance.
The Kur has a very distinct appearance that differs from his race's octopus physiology. He has a large head with a veined forehead and bulbous eyes that are closed. Unlike his brethren, he possesses more tentacle-like appendages connected to his head that are thinner and longer and a small mouth. Overall, he resembles more like a jellyfish than an octopus.

Personality

The Hastur Kur has a very greedy and possessive personality, claiming that everything he comes across are his and his alone, and takes action by stealing whatever catches his interest. To this extent, he does not take it lightly when others destroy his possessions. He is shown to be cold-hearted and sadistic when carrying out his people's objective of conquering planets, which he describes as "hunting". After Bamora had escaped from Sumer with Banga's help, the Hastur Kur declared to Banga that he would be persistent enough to track her daughter down to the ends of the cosmos to kill her and would use her head to adorn the top of the Sumer pyramid. His remorseless behavior also includes the use of psychological warfare to get his enemies to submit, as he was sure of himself that Banga would comply to open a portal to Earth for his team by torturing Aja right in front of her. The Hastur Kur views his race as a superior species and deems all life within the galaxy to be "lower lifeforms". As such, he arrogantly believes that all organisms should at least understand that it is a futile effort to try and resist him and the invading army, having failed to comprehend why Kinta wouldn't give up in trying to reconstruct his mecha as the former began crushing the pilot core. Despite this view, he has good judgement in identify lifeforms who are strong, which, like his teammates, fuels his interests in operating powerful battle suits that can be crafted from their essence.
Background

For many years, the Hastur Kur had orchestrated a series of Kur invasions across various planets in the universe. During the invasion of Sumer, he and his team caught the Sumerian woman Banga using the Sumerian pyramid to transport the sole surviving Sumerian child Bamora to Earth. Having realized that only a Sumerian is capable of activating the portal, the Hastur Kur threatened to torture Banga's colleague Aja if she did not comply with him in sending them to Earth to track down Bamora.
Synopsis

Space Globalists Arc

After arriving on Earth, the Hastur Kur and his team encountered and launched an attack on the Serpo and defeated them, resulting in them being rewarded with their data, which included their findings on Okarun's kintama, and technology. At the same time, he receives a signal from Bamora's exosuit that was accidentally triggered by Jiji.

Later, the Hastur Kur and his team confront Okarun to acquire his kintama that they plan to use as a battery to summon their main force. Using his suit's spatial carving ability, the Hastur Kur deals a devastating blow to Okarun that results in him losing conscious. With the kintama acquired, the Hastur Kur and his team prepare to leave the area through a portal and decide to also take Okarun with them to perform an investigation on his internal anatomy. However, their exit is interrupted by Mr. Mantis Shrimp who arrives to save Okarun. The Hastur Kur stops the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur from fighting him, telling his teammate that they don't have the time, and leaves with his team without Okarun in their possession, but not before threatening to target Mr. Mantis Shrimp the next time they meet.

A few days later, the Advance Unit activates their warp gate to allow passage for their main force's battleships. The Hastur Kur, along with the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur and Ta Koshin Jo Kur, confront Momo, Rokuro, and Bamora as they attempt to close the gate. After Bamora defeats the Ta Koshin Jo Kur, the Hastur Kur gives the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur a weapon that electrically restrains her. He then takes Bamora out of her suit, claiming it for himself, and pierces her abdomen with his tail, much to Momo's horror. After Rokuro saves Bamora with a healing syringe, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur holds up Bamora by the neck as the Hastur Kur gives credit to her for helping the Kur find a new planet to conquer. Momo sends a tree towards the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur to have him release Bamora and prepares to fight the two Kur members. The Hastur Kur puts Momo on the defense as he sends her psychic rubble attacks back at her and clashes with her Moe-Moe Tri Beam, resulting in both of their attacks to repel each other, which confirmed to him that Momo was a strong opponent to face. The Hastur Kur then receives reinforcements from the Kur members who had passed through the gate, causing Momo and Bamora to be overwhelmed. However, the two girls are saved by Okarun, Aira, Mr. Mantis Shrimp, and the Evil Eye who prepare to face the Kur together.

The Hastur Kur supports the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur with his spatial power as he fights Okarun. Momo prevents Okarun from falling for his tricks and informs him of how the Kur's ability works. After the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur is blown away by an attack from Okarun, the Hastur Kur fights Momo and Okarun alone and manages to render their attacks useless. Seeing Momo heading his way with a ton of controlled rubble, the Hastur Kur sends them away to his dimension, along with Momo who jumps at him. This results in the Kur's battle suit being destroyed with a Moe Moe Tri-Beam projecting out, as Momo tricked him into sending her to his dimension to unleash her attack that is capable of transcending dimensions. Refusing to allow her to get the best of him, the Hastur Kur prepares to attack Momo as she jumps out from his damaged suit. However, the Hastur Kur is defeated by Okarun after he uses a powerful charging attack to completely destroy his suit and save Momo.

Furious that his battle suit had been destroyed, the Kur chooses to steal Bamora's and activates its Slaughter Mode after becoming its new pilot. After ejecting her out, the Kur finds himself facing against Kinta, who saves Bamora from falling, after he constructs a mecha using the nanoskin the Ayase house is made of. In response to being attacked with the Tokyo Tower by Kinta as a swinging weapon, the Kur does the same using the Tokyo Skytree, pointing out that his tower is longer than his, but loses the exchange as Kinta points out how his tower is more superior. Despite this, the Kur states to Kinta that his attacks have done no damage to his suit, which he becomes impressed by its resilience, and uses its horns to destroy the mecha. He then proceeds to extract the pilot core out of the mecha that is holding Kinta and Bamora inside. As he starts to crush it with his hand, the Kur declares the Earth to be his race's property once more battleships have passed through the gate and tells Kinta to give up as he tries to resist by controlling the nanoskin. The Kur crushes the pod but realizes too late that Kinta and Bamora had secretly ejected onto his back to form a jetpack that they control to send him soaring up in the sky and rocketing down with a devastating powerbomb technique. With the suit returning to normal from taking too much damage, the Kur leaves out of it while feeling dizzy from the impact. Yet as of now, it’s unclear if Hastur Kur managed to escape and is hiding despite Earth’s gravity or was also imprisoned within Reiko Kashima’s mirror and promptly eradicated by the Yokai.

Most Head Exosuits worn by other Kur lacked the stick arms and metal piece attachment though more than one is seen possessing them. Considering that the Advance Unit was already formed during the invasion of Sumer, it's likely that the Head Exosuit Kur was the one defending the Big Mama inside the forest while she was being fed the captured Sumerian soldiers to produce exosuits.

The Imotako Kur was a Kur of the Advance Unit who wielded the Imotako.

In Dandadan, he serves as a major antagonist during the Space Globalists Arc.

Appearance

Imotako Kur has a mask-like face with spiral eyes, a hollow circular mouth. His elongated arms are massive. Swirling, wood-like textures cover his body, blending him into a dark, chaotic background. The spine-like structure behind his head adds a skeletal, otherworldly aura, evoking a cosmic, malevolent presence.
Personality

Background

Synopsis

Space Globalists Arc

At Moe Moe Kikoho, Imotako Kur emerges amidst the chaos instigated by Serpo and numerous alien clones. He attacks by using his power to transform the Serpo aliens into creatures with facial features resembling his own, thereby turning them into his underlings. Momo Ayase and a Serpo use ironings to smash the clone aliens in the face, causing them to revert to their original Serpo forms. This cycle continues and the Serpo clones are overwhelmed. To end the battle, the Serpo tells Momo to defeat Imotako Kur, yet she struggles due to his ability to phase through objects, as his true body exists in a different dimension. Ultimately, remembering a lesson from her grandmother, Momo harnesses the power to turn impossible thoughts into reality, unleashing a Moe Moe Tri-Beam that disintegrates Imotako Kur, resulting in his death.

He's briefly seen attached to the side of the Warp Gate Pyramid during the Invasion of Sumer.

Abilities and Powers

Imotako Kur's true body exists in a different dimension, granting him the ability to phase through objects without harm. While his attacks successfully connect, those of others simply miss him. He possesses the ability to manipulate his body, extending parts of it like sharp tentacles to pierce his enemies. When his tentacles penetrate the heads of the Serpo aliens, their faces morph, transforming them into his underlings.

The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur refers to the conscripted alien affiliated with the Kur of the Advance Unit who wielded a jet booster exosuit.

In Dandadan, she serves as a major antagonist during the Space Globalists Arc and a supporting antagonist during the Kozuka Knives Arc.

Appearance

She is a female alien with a humanoid body, while possessing a very lean, muscular and athletic build with straight shoulder-length, light-colored hair that is parted in the middle, with a few strands gently falling over her forehead and pointy ears. Her entire body is covered in scars, all of which were inflicted by the Kur during their invasion of her home planet. Her most prominent ones are the two on her face; a diagonal cut on her right cheek and a vertical one on her left. Along with her scars, she lost her left eye and has it replaced with an artificial crosshair pupil. She is mainly seen wearing her exosuit, which helps her to survive the gravity on foreign planets.

In the past, before the Kur invaded her planet, she was more slender, her hair was longer, and her body showed no signs of damage.

The alien wearing her second exosuit.

The alien wearing her original exosuit.
The alien wearing her original exosuit.
Personality

This alien woman is an extremely vengeful individual, having gone to great lengths to get her chance to bring justice to her destroyed home world by assassinating the emperor of the invaders responsible for taking everything away from her. After infiltrating the Kur army, she meticulously portrayed herself as the ideal soldier to gain enough trust to receive an audience with the emperor, demonstrating a cold, unflinching attitude toward the Kur's targets in pursuit of her goal. This facade was apparent during her confrontation with Okarun and during the invasion with Momo and Bamora, where she forcefully kicked Momo away from Bamora and seized the Suemrian girl by the neck while registering her survival after being killed by the Hastur Kur.

With years of continuous war, conquest, horrific acts of genocide, and endurance climbing up the ranks to gain the trust of her enemies and complete her quest for vengeance rendered meaningless following the Family's triumph over the Kur invasion, the alien's spirit became consumed by sorrow and frustration, leading to a decision to give up on living. However, as both a final act of vengeance and a prelude to her own self-destruction, she became fixated on killing Okarun, whom she held responsible for her plan's collapse following her defeat at his hands during the invasion. Her relentless focus was apparent as she ignored Hase's attempts to dissuade her from interfering with his own vendetta against Okarun.
Background

She once lived a serene life on her home planet with her partner. However, it was soon destroyed following the Kur's arrival on her world to conquer and forcibly integrate it into their empire like many others. Driven by the devastation of her world, she survived the upheaval and infiltrated the alien army. Over the course of more than a century, she played a pivotal role in countless invasions and genocides, methodically climbing the ranks to achieve her ultimate goal of getting close to the Kur emperor and exact her revenge for the destruction of her planet. Her efforts proved to be fruitful as she eventually became the right hand of Hastur, the leader of the Advance Unit.

Among the invasions, the alien took part in the conquest of Sumer. During this time, she and her team caught Banga using the Sumerian pyramid to transport Bamora to Earth in the midst of a rebellion between the enslaved male Sumerians and the Kur. Refusing to allow her to escape, the Advance Unit later departed for Earth to capture Bamora.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Space Globalists Arc

After the Advance Unit arrived on Earth to track down Bamora, the team launched an attack on the Serpos at their base and separated to ambush Momo, Okarun, Aira, and Jiji who were affiliated with their target. The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur, along with five other members, approach Okarun just as he was departing from the Ayase residency and engaging him in battle. After the Hastur Kur knocks Okarun unconscious with his spatial carving attack, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur uses a Serpo apparatus to extract Okarun's single kintama from his crotch. As the team prepares to leave through a portal with both Okarun and his kintama, Mr. Mantis Shrimp arrives to stop them from abducting Okarun. The Jet booster Exosuit Kur gets herself ready to fight him. However, the Hastur Kur stops her, telling his ally that they did not have the time to focus on him, and has his team depart without Okarun in their possession.

As the Kur activate their warp gate using Okarun's kintama to gradually summon their main fleet, the Advance Unit stands guard, ready to fend off any intruders. They soon find themselves clashing with the Family. The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur and the Ta Koshin Jo Kur launch a surprise attack on Momo and Rokuro as they race to close the warp gate. In the midst of this confrontation, Bamora, wielding her kaiju exosuit, swiftly joins the fray after attack the Ta Koshin Jo Kur. With the defeat of the Ta Koshin Jo Kur by the Sumerian girl, the Hastur Kur hands an electrical restraining device to the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur to bind Bamora. This opens a window for the Hastur Kur to extract Bamora from her exosuit and pierce her abdomen with his tail. As Momo desperately tries to heal Bamora's fatal wound, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur relentlessly attacks Rokuro's psychic barrier protecting Momo. When Rokuro's barrier finally falls, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur kicks Momo aside and seizes the now-healed Bamora by the neck. Observing Bamora's survival, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur interprets it as luck being on her side. Momo, using her powers, hurls a tree at the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur, causing her to lose her grip on Bamora.

The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur engages in battle alongside Hastur Kur against Momo; however, she is swiftly neutralized when Momo encases her in a sphere of debris. The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur then escapes from her trap just as Kur reinforcements arrive. Following this, Okarun, Aira, Mr. Mantis Shrimp, and the Evil Eye arrive to fight alongside Momo. As the Evil Eye confronts Okarun to have him make good on his word to fight him every Tuesday, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur comes in to interrupt the two with an attack and fight Okarun herself, with assistance from the Hastur Kur using his spatial carving. Just as she gets close enough to strike Okarun, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur is struck in the face by a chuck of debris by Momo assisting Okarun in battle. The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur meets a swift defeat when Okarun, using Turbo Granny's telephone wire ejection speed, delivers a powerful kick that sends her crashing into a building and then into a canal, leaving her exosuit heavily damaged and putting her out of commission for the rest of the invasion. Her unconscious body gets transported away through a small canal and she gets brought by Count Saint-Germain to the Kamigoe Ruins.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

At some point after the invasion, the wielder of the Jet Booster Exosuit awakens to find herself out of her suit in the Kamigoe City's ruined area. Spotting Count Saint-Germain standing before her after he speaks, she instinctively adopts a defensive stance. The man gestures towards her damaged exosuit beside her, suggesting that if it is indeed hers, she will need a replacement as it is no longer fully operational. Curious about his intentions, she asks what he wants from her. Count Saint-Germain explains that he requires her assistance, which is to steal Okarun's power on his behalf. Although he reassures her that she has the right to refuse, he highlights that rejecting his offer and permitting him to leave would compel her to face the challenges of Earth's heavy gravity on her own, a reality that becomes apparent as he notices her difficulty in remaining upright while they speak despite not being a Kur alien. With her plans to assassinate the Kur emperor brought down by the Family, the alien accepts Count Saint-Germain's assignment and is given a new exosuit for the job.

At Kami High, the alien ambushes Okarun and Kinta as they rush to assist Rin and Kouki, who has met up with her blackmailer. While pursuing the duo, Hase, a Kami High student who has been given the same task as her, voices his frustration with her getting in his way of confronting Okarun and instructs her to target Kinta instead. However, she disregards his orders as she becomes engrossed in recalibrating her newly upgraded suit. With the modifications finished, the alien proceeds to charge forward, swiftly evades Kinta's attack as he operates a miniature Great Kinta suit, and lands a strong kick on Okarun wearing a nanoskin plate armor crafted by his ally. As Hase shifts his focus to targeting Kinta, Okarun confronts the alien directly, demanding to know why she is attacking him. The alien accuses him of stealing everything from her, revealing how her personal mission to assassinate the Kur emperor was ruined by the Family, and demands for him to recognize the years of struggle she endured. Okarun dismisses her frustrations as meaningless to him and counters with a forceful attack, activating his verniers to propel himself forward. She parries the strike and readies a punch, only for Okarun to surprise her by activating his pile bunkers, landing a heavy blow that sends both combatants tumbling to the ground. Desperate to de-escalate the situation, Okarun implores her to stop, arguing that he isn’t her true enemy. However, she remains resolute in her intentions, affirming her singular focus, killing him and then herself.

As glimpses of her tragic past scroll through her mind, the alien rushes forward and barrages Okarun's armor with a series of kicks, forcing him to boost into her. She opens up the exosuit's face and bites with rage Okarun's arm, hurting him and he uses his pile bunkers to gain distance. Just then, he sees the furious alien's humanoid face and realizes she's not one of the Kurs. She dives and lands a powerful kick that slams the boy's hand onto the nanoskin arm, causing it to lose the properties of steel imagined by Kinta. She activates a mechanism in her hip which forms a ring of light that travels onto her back and gets released as a devastating beam when she extends her leg forward, completely wrecking Okarun's armor. Hase notices her deadly intent and shifts focus from Kinta to block her path, declaring that he'll be the one to kill Okarun. Despite her rage, Hase doesn't hold back and flings her skyward before jumping above her and slamming her down into the ground, repeating this multiple times. Okarun and Kinta take this window of time to merge while Hase finishes her and throws her aside, telling her to stay out of his way. Barely lifeless on the ground, she spectates Hase duel the boys and lose. With her armor now damaged and her revenge still unfinished, she recovers and departs in the skies.

Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Skill Set

Master Hand-to-Hand Combatant: The alien possesses extraordinary skill in hand-to-hand combat, having held her own against Okarun in his Turbo Granny form, an opponent whose fighting prowess are great enough to match the likes of the fighting oriented Evil Eye.

Equipment

Jet Booster Exosuit [v · e]
The alien wielded an exosuit during her affiliation with the Kur. Following her battle against Okarun, the exosuit sustained major damage and was declared inoperable by Count Saint-Germain.
Jet Booster Exosuit
Capabilities
Jets
Jet Booster Exosuit's Jets
The exosuit features a pair of jets on its back that serve to enhance the wearer's hand-to-hand combat skills.
Usage
Jet Booster Exosuit's enhanced strength
Like all exosuits, the alien donned hers primarily for combat and to withstand the brutal gravity of foreign planets. Her fighting style, centered on hand-to-hand combat, was significantly enhanced by the jets of her exosuit, allowing her greater mobility and amplifying the force behind her powerful strikes.
Aviate Exosuit
After her original exosuit was damaged by Okarun, the alien was given a new one that was combat oriented much like her old one by Count Saint-Germain. At first, the alien found it difficult to wield when first put to use and had to make a few recalibrations in the middle of her confrontation with Okarun and Kinta.
Aviate Exosuit Infobox
Capabilities
Heads-Up Display
Like all exosuits, this model features a heads-up display integrated into the helmet, enabling the user to evaluate their surroundings.
Recalibration
Aviate Exosuit's Recalibration
The exosuit is able to be adjusted or fine-tuned by the wearer to ensure it functions effectively for them. The reconfiguration settings are located on the right arm.
Flight
Jet Booster Exosuit 2
The defining feature of this exosuit is its sole propulsion mechanism located on the back, enabling the wearer to take flight. Unlike the select few flying-type exosuits that are built for long-range assaults—such as those equipped with weapons for aerial bombardment or sniping—this particular model's flight capabilities is specifically tailored for close-range engagements.
Enhanced Durability
Verniers Okarun
The exosuit is shown to be quite durable, being able to withstand heavy melee attacks from Okarun who was equipped with steel-hardened nanoskin armor.
Usage
Similar to her previous exosuit, the alien utilizes this version for hand-to-hand combat during battle. With its propulsion system, she adeptly maneuvers across the battlefield, allowing her to approach her target while benefiting from improved agility, evasive capabilities, and increased power in her melee attacks.

Kashimoto is a man with moderately long hair and a goatee. He wears a pair of rectangular glasses and a black bucket hat, and his attire consists of a tracksuit shirt and dark pants. On the back of his shirt is a symbol that resembles the Eye of Providence, albeit with a multi-ringed pupil. He also wears a pair of loop earrings.

ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

Compared to his business partner, Kashimoto is a lot more level-headed and serious. He tends to be the go-to source of knowledge in the duo, with mythology and ways to lift curses being his forte. Despite his seriousness, he is more than happy to share some banter with his business partner.
Synopsis

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Kashimoto and Payase meet up with Seiko Ayase at a restaurant after the spirit medium seeks their help. While Payase is given entrusted by Seiko to look after a cursed trunk, Kashimoto is asked by Seiko if he has any knowledge on how to turn a pygmy to normal size, being informed that her granddaughter was shrunken down after she had escaped from the cursed trunk. Kashimoto answers yes and that the key is the Uchide-no-kozuchi that is in the possession of the deity Daikokuten. He further explains that Daikokuten and the other god Okuninushi are one and the same and recommends that Seiko visit the Izumo Grand Shrine. Grateful for the advice, Seiko gets ready to leave. As Kashimoto expresses his willingness to help her, he is unexpectedly kicked aside by a jiangshi amidst a group of similar beings.[1]

After Seiko is taken down by the Minotaur, Kashimoto and Payase include themselves in the battle by punching the Minotaur away together with their power. Kashimoto voices his displeasure being kicked out of nowhere earlier and unleashes his power, along with Payase, in preparation to face the Minotaur and the jiangshi.[2] Seiko rises to her feet after enduring injuries inflicted by the Minotaur, likening her ordeal to that of the most excruciating osteopathy clinic imaginable, a remark that strikes a chord with Kashimoto while leaving Payase perplexed. After being informed by Seiko that the Minotaur's body is made of iron, and his strength increases every time he is hit, Kashimoto and Payase are instructed by her to handle fighting the Minotaur while she goes to retrieve her bag. As the jiangshi charge in, Kashimoto uses Aphoom-Zhah to knock them back. After Payase is thrown by the Minotaur, Kashimoto tells Seiko as he comes in to attack the Minotaur with Aphoom-Zhah. He briefly stands his ground but is soon punch to the wall by the Minotaur. Kashimoto and Payase then try again to attack the Minotaur as Seiko attempts to reclaim her bag but are overpowered after the Minotaurs claims to have reached his peak. As the Minotaur takes hold of Seiko and begins crushing her with his tough musculature, Kashimoto comes to attack him with Aphoom-Zhah and continues as Seiko instructed in light of the attack also affecting her. With the Minotaur's body cooled down by Kashimoto's Aphoom-Zhah, Payase manages to free Seiko by extending his arms through the Minotaur's arms, causing them to break. As the Minotaur becomes confused by how this has happened, Kashimoto explains to him that his inability to feel pain led to his downfall and reveals that his Ice Flames can reach absolute zero, resulting in his iron body being susceptible to hydrogen penetration. In the end, Seiko finishes the bull off with the use of the talisman in her purse.[3]

ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Powers

Supernatural Abilities

Guardian Spirit [v · e]
Kashimoto is capable of calling on the spiritual power of a guardian spirit.
Kashimoto's power

(氷ひょう炎えん, Hyōen?)
The spiritual power of the guardian spirit is the conjuration of flames with freezing properties, capable of dropping down to absolute zero. The flames take on the form of a spiral with a phoneix-like bird head on one side and a wing of feathers on the other.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The primary advantage of this spiritual power lies in its ability to enable Kashimoto to freeze his targets directly. Additionally, it enhances his physical strength, permitting him to strike an iron minotaur with sufficient force to propel him a considerable distance without inflicting any injury to his hand, as well as damage a portion of a jiangshi's face.
Usage
Kashimoto employs this power in combat, using it to amplify his punches, which results in both freezing his opponents and delivering damage.
Techniques
