Kinta Sakata (坂田金太, Sakata Kinta?) is one of the main characters of the manga series Dandadan.

He is a student at Kami High who later became one of Momo and Okarun's main allies whenever the two are faced with the paranormal.

Appearance

Volume 10 Color Page 2
Kinta's color scheme.
Kinta is a young man with a rotund build, short-trimmed middle-parting dark hair and wears glasses. For attire, he wears his school's gakuran outfit.

Personality

Kinta acts vain and prideful, particularly towards young men around his age who he has no interest in interacting with. After Okarun and Jiji carried the defeated Bamora to the Ayase house, Kinta immediately stepped out with a condescending attitude, calling them out as useless for being late and brushing off any flattery from them. He is also an attention seeker, having wanted to present himself at school as an important person to Momo, Okarun, and the others by putting on an eyepatch and wrapping himself in bandages, with the false story behind his appearance being injuries from a battle against an alien that he won single-handedly. Kinta often tries to act cool and strong in front of people, often making eccentric statements and poses. Additionally, he is too proud to admit his own shortcomings and will justify his failures with an excuse.

However, this personality is admitted by Kinta to be a façade. Fully aware that he is an individual who can't amount to anything, Kinta tried masking his insecurities by finding fault in others and making attempts at being acknowledged by his peers. In light of him having nothing to be proud, Kinta declares to be a person who remains true to himself. With his love for robots and girls driving him, Kinta refused to give up and leave behind the Great Kinta and Bamora out of fear of being crushed inside the cockpit by the Spatial Suit Exosuit Kur, stating that he would regret it for the rest of his life, and persisted on with trying to defeat the Kur.

Despite his prideful and awkward traits, Kinta has more than a bit of bravery. He is eager to help the Family face the unknown, as he was visibly excited to have a chance to rush into the fray after finding an SOS note attached to the Ayase house. Even when hurt in a fight and facing possible death, he was able to keep his cool, protect Bamora, and find a way to come out on top against the Hastur Kur. Even during his first battle, when he was largely helpless and incapable of fighting, he rushed into danger to discover the secret of the enemy's invisibility rather than flee to save himself. His bravery is overshadowed by his irritating way of communicating to people, yet he refuses to back down when confronted with the unknown and consistently seeks solutions whenever feasible.

When it comes to the opposite sex, Kinta desires to be seen as being charming to girls but ends up failing from getting the wrong idea analyzing relationships between young men and women. He is also perverted, as he hoped to lock lips with Momo as he was sent flying towards her by Bamora and wanted to end his fight with the Spatial Exosuit Kur quickly to have a "lovey-dovey thunder break" with Bamora.

Along with wanting to be liked by girls, Kinta's other prominent personality is his passion for mechas. While having a hobby of collecting mecha figurines called Dandams and watching mecha genre anime, Kinta dreamed of one day piloting a mecha and committed himself to preparing for the momentous occasion by riding amusement rides to avoid robot sickness. Come the battle against Bamora's out of control exosuit, Kinta's dream came to fruition as he exercised his knowledge of mechas to construct one of the nanoskin the Ayase house is made of and was overjoyed in the end.
Background

Equipment

Nanoskin [v · e]
Kinta carries around a cube fragment of nanoskin from the Ayase residence.
Kinta's nanoskin
Capabilities
Shapeshifting
Nanoskin functions like clay, capable of shapeshifting into various forms and objects, from clothing and tools to vehicles and even complex structures like houses or robots. Mastery of nanoskin offers exceptional adaptability, enabling solutions for nearly any scenario. It can also autonomously restore itself when damaged and adheres to both the visualized form and functionality, allowing it to support features like energy beams or propulsion systems.

The creation of an object requires an exact amount of nanoskin based on its size and complexity, limiting the user to the available quantity. Though nanoskin can self-restore after damage, its fragility poses challenges in combat. To counter this, Kinta enabled nanoskin to mimic the density of hardened materials like steel, improving durability but making it heavier and less agile for the user when worn.
Usage
Great Kinta
(グレートキンタ, Gurēto Kinta?)
Great Kinta Kaiju Zeta Version - First Form
 Great Kinta Bodhisattva, Zeta Version - Second Form
 Great Kinta Bodhisattva, Zeta Version - First Form
Utilizing the nanoskin the Ayase household is made of and his passion for mechas, Kinta is able to construct a colossal robot that he can pilot to battle enormous foes. This robot was originally designed by Kinta to take on Bamora when she lost control of her kaiju suit. It was later reconstructed to face the Hastur Kur, who had seized control of Bamora's kaiju suit in its Slaughter Mode.
When piloted by Kinta, the mecha proved to be very formidable, as its physical strength is great enough to damage the kaiju and leave a path of destruction in an Empty Space Kamigoe City. Since the mecha was composed entirely of nanoskin, which is a fragile material, its durability was considerably weak and could easily be damaged. However, by continuously applying his imagination to the nanoskin, he could have the mecha repair itself to give it a form of regeneration.
Techniques

Kinta can use his nanoskin to craft various tools. To find out Kouki's blackmailer, Kinta crafted a surveillance camera that acts as a hairpin for Kouki to wear. In addition, he crafted himself a replica of his glasses with HUD features and had it sync to the hairpin to watch the recorded footage.
Battle Suits
A battle suit version of the Great Kinta.
The Great Kinta battle suit merged with Okarun.
During his and Okarun's fight against Hase and the alien of the Kur's Advance Unit, Kinta used his nanoskin to craft a battle suit model of the Great Kinta with harden density to provide durability. However, the battle suit proved to be cumbersome for him to operate. Later, he had the suit "merge" with Okarun as a second pilot operating the lower half to make use of his combat prowess.

Kouki Yukishiro (雪白幸姬, Yukishiro Kōki?) is a student at Kami High and a skilled pianist.

In Dandadan, she started out as a main antagonist during the first half of the Kozuka Knives Arc, having been threatened with blackmail by Murakami if she did not do his bidding in stealing Momo Ayase's powers.

Appearance

Kouki is a slender young girl with long hair that obscures most of her face and her round eyes have large pupils. As a student, she wears the Kami High uniform; a dark buttoned up blazer with her school emblem located around the left breast, a collared shirt, a bow, long socks and sandals. Similar to Rin Sawaki, she wears a long dark skirt instead of the standard short skirt.

She later does her hair up, revealing that her eyes are naturally almond shaped, as well that she has rather small eyebrows.

Personality

Kouki is a timid and dispirited girl. As a child, she took pride in her recognition as a talented pianist. After her time in the spotlight was replaced by a life of isolation from her peers, Kouki longed to once again be acknowledged, even if the means were improper.
Background

As a child, Kouki received accolades for her skills in playing the piano, distinguishing her as a prodigy to many. However, after losing to Aira Shiratori in the junior piano competition, she believed she had no talent and quit playing the piano.[1] By the time Kouki reached high school, she found herself as an outcast by her classmates and even her own family with her younger sister Alice overshadowing her in talent.[2]

In an act of desperation to once again be acknowledged, Kouki chose to post to her account an anonymous picture of herself undressed. Later, she was approached by an individual who recognized her as the girl in the photograph. Kouki was then coerced by the person to do their bidding in locating Momo Ayase to usurp her powers using a small knife if she desired their silence.[3] After she consented to their terms, she was cut with a knife, which allowed her to see the pygmies, who accompanied Kouki to ensure that she fulfilled her mission.
Synopsis

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Momo being pursued by a female student
Kouki targeting Momo for her power.
After one pygmy locates Momo Ayase in the library, Kouki makes her move to search for her and steal her power once her friends have left the room. However, she ultimately runs out of time to complete her task after the school bell rings and makes a hasty retreat.[4] While alone, Kouki is told by a mystery person in a locker that her approach was wrong since she did not make Momo yield first and is urged by them to give in to her desires to become the person she wants to be.[5]

Later, Kouki finds herself locking eyes with Momo as the History and Culture Research Club tries searching for her after the shrunken girl informs them about what happened in the library. She then flees from the group and manages to hide herself inside an Empty Space classroom using a cloak that has her blend in with the environment.[6] Eventually, she is found and attacked by Momo using her psychic power to hurl a desk at her.[7] Following Momo's attack that renders her unconscious, the pygmies carry Kouki out of the classroom in their escape. When they arrive at Queen's infirmary, where the nurse is also present in Empty Space, Kouki tries to win Queen over by wrongfully accusing Jiji and the others of being the attackers. However, as the story Kouki tells Queen begins to unravel, and upon the nurse's insistence on honesty, Kouki admits to her misdeeds of attacking Momo. This then leads to Kouki being angrily slapped by Queen for pretending to be the victim.[8]

Later, Kouki explains to the History and Culture Research Club and Queen her reason for attacking Momo, revealing she had been blackmailed into doing so, but is unable to recall the identity of her blackmailer. She then suddenly experiences dizziness and inability to remember those conditions to respond to Aira's inquiry. Momo theorizes that Kouki may simply be a pawn manipulated by the sinister teacher who sent her, suggesting that the teacher could have altered her memory to keep any information from surfacing. Kouki elaborates that the teacher enabled her to perceive the pygmies by wounding her with one of his numerous knives. She then brushes the pygmies off her arm as they try to bandage her wound. Even though Momo clarifies that the pygmies genuinely want to help, Kouki remains unwilling to acknowledge them or allow them to follow her, longing for a return to her ordinary life. As Kouki becomes increasingly disheartened by her unfortunate situation, Queen discloses her research on the pygmies, explaining that these marginalized individuals have retreated underground, yearning for recognition and offering their allegiance to those who acknowledge them. Touched by this revelation and contemplating her own isolation, Kouki becomes moved to tears, leading the pygmies to sew the phrase "Hang in there, Kouki" as a sign of encouragement. Aira and Momo advises everyone to stick together to prevent the enemy from exploiting any vulnerabilities and to keep an eye on Kouki in case the enemy targets her again, presenting an opportunity to ambush their foe and erase Kouki's image. After Kouki gives out her name to Aira as requested, Aira realizes she knows Kouki, remembering that she lost to her in a childhood piano competition—an event that motivated her to work hard and eventually win. Kouki also recognizes Aira and becomes shocked and frustrated to learn from her that she quit the piano due to finding it tedious.

Kouki voices her discomfort about needing to change out of her school uniform, which has become unwearable after being doused in white from the fire extinguisher. When Aira comments on her consistently sorrowful demeanor, Kouki retorts, asking Aira to be quiet. While wearing a nanoskin surveillance camera made by Kinta as a hair ornament, Kouki is monitored by the History and Culture Research Club and comes into contact with at least three teachers as suspects — Queen, Adachi, and Sanjome. After school, Kouki reunites with Murakami and follows him to the school gym where he has the Severed Head Dribblers convert her, along with Rin spying on them, into floating heads, having caught onto their trap.

After Aira arrives with Okarun and Kinta to help the girls, Kouki has her body returned to her thanks to Mai and the pygmies. Kouki then reveals that the identity of her blackmailer is Murakami. As the situation becomes worse with the Severed Head Dribblers growing gigantic, the gym walls closing in, and Rin's power gradually weakening, Kouki turns to the pygmies for help in finding Murakami to end the chaos, while also apologizing to them for her previous mistreatment. After their search, she learns from the pygmies that Murakami is not inside the gym and informs Aira. Just as she starts to feel powerless not being able to help Aira and Rin fight the Severed Head Dribblers, Kouki is presented with a piano instantly constructed by the pygmies and is urged by Aira, Rin, and Mai to play, believing that Rin's power can be amplified if she does so. Kouki finds herself unable to play properly due to the memories of her mother's teachings resurfacing and the piano being one she is not accustomed to. However, after Aira reveals her past admiration for Kouki and wish for her to reignite her passion she once had, Kouki becomes able to play a melody that summons a swarm of flies ominously gathering over Kamigoe City.

Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Skill Set

Perfect Pitch: Kouki is a gifted pianist in that she can recognize the pitch of sounds and reproduce musical notes accurately without needing any reference. She characterizes her talent as the ability to visualize sounds.

Supernatural Abilities

Pygmy Awareness [v · e]
Kouki is able to clearly see the miniscule creatures known as pygmies after acquiring the ability from an Asura by Murakami. As a result of being able to see them, Kouki is granted their fidelity in that they follow her wherever she goes, protect her when she is in danger, and follow her orders.
Kouki's Pygmy Awareness
Lord of the Flies
(蠅の王, Hae no ō?)
After returning to playing the piano, Kouki discovered her innate ability, which is the power to summon and subjugate small living things to her will.
Kouki summoning flies
Strengths and Weaknesses
This power allows Kouki to command small living creatures by playing the piano. Her manipulation primarily focuses on insects, with flies being the most notable subjects of her control. Rather than issuing vocal commands, Kouki's influence is conveyed through the melodies she plays, with the insects instinctively responding to her intentions in any given scenario, such as attacking her targets or tracking them down elsewhere. The range of this ability is impressively vast, as demonstrated when she summoned an entire swarm of flies across Kamigoe City to locate Murakami in a distant area.

The only known weakness to this power is that it depletes Kouki's stamina.
Usage
Kouki's first usage of this ability was to have a swarm of flies deliver Murakami over to her to defeat him and cancel out his ability to control the Severed Head Dribblers. In addition, she also summoned various insects to attack the Severed Head Dribblers, while sparing Aira, Rin, and Mai who were with her.
Equipment

Asura [v · e]
Kouki wields a black handle Asura knife given to her by Murakami for the task of robbing Momo of her psychic powers.
Kozuka Knives Arc
Capabilities
Power Absorption
Like its parent, the black handle Asuras are capable of extracting powers from individuals, under the condition that the wielder's target admits defeat before being cut.
Usage
Kouki attempted to use the Asura on Momo when she was alone in the library.

Ludris (ルドリス, Rudorisu?) is a renowned alien who travels throughout space, with a chance encounter with him being said to be considered a miracle.

Appearance

Ludris has an entirely blocky body. He has square-shaped, octad-lined eyes that resembles that of a slug and a long block mouth. He also has a upside down triangle eye marking at the center of his body.
Personality

Ludris was shown to be very irritated after being kicked by Momo and Seiko but was willing to help repair their house nonetheless as per his agreement with Mr. Mantis Shrimp.
Synopsis

Evil Eye Arc

Returning from the Spa, Ludris is found on the ruins of the Ayase residence, greeting the group. Momo and Seiko immediately send him flying with kicks, making him mad. Suddenly, Okarun and Aira appear on the scene along with Mr. Mantis Shrimp and Chiquitita hoping to help rebuilding the house. Mantis Shrimp introduced the two to Ludris, who's a construction specialist. Momo apologized to Ludris and Mr Shrimp reassures her, translating his words as him being honored to be kicked by such a beautiful woman, despite him being visibly infuriated. Seiko refuses multiple time to receive their aid, but Momo allows the three of them to gladly partecipate in the reconstruction of the house. Mr Shrimp showcases the nanoskin, a technology made by Ludris, composed of ultrahigh-density nanomachines which pick up the electrical signals of the brain and displays what they are thinking. Everyone grabs the nanoskin and together they start rebuilding the house which slowly takes form.

After the residence has been brought back to its original state, Mr Shrimp again translates to Seiko that Ludris is grateful to lend a hand to such a beautiful woman, but she suspects that he doesn't understand him at all. Momo dearly thanks everyone for their assist and sends them home.

Space Globalists Arc

As Momo asks Mr Shrimp to use his spaceship to go get Seiko in order to help defeat the Kur, he reveals that it actually belongs to Ludris and it was by pure coincidence he was on Earth at the right time. Rokuro Serpo is shocked to hear his name, since he's all knowing and powerful, constantly travelling the universe, making it difficult to encounter him even once. Momo is surprised that she got away with kicking him, so Rokuro, in disbelief, asks her if she really did that.

Abilities and Powers

Master Craftsmanship

Ludris is known as a miricle worker being the creator of the nano-skin that can respond to thoughts.

Mai Kawabanga (川かわ番ばん河が舞まい, Kawabanga Mai?) was the childhood friend of Rin Sawaki who had died from a car accident. Her spirit then went on to become an Onbusuman-type yokai that was bound to Rin until it was cleansed by the Family and became converted into a guardian spirit. Continuing to be by Rin's side, Mai makes it her goal to have her childhood friend become an idol.

Mai was a child who had short hair with front bangs that only covered the right side of her forehead and a ribbon adorning the top of her head. She wore a collared long-sleeved shirt with a sweater on top, a skirt, and black knee socks.

As an Onbusuman, Mai had the appearance of a large creature; possessing a bulbous head with an inhuman face, the body of a turtle, and a large hairy tail. After her spirit was cleansed, Mai took on the form of a teenage version of herself and wore the same clothes from when she was alive.

Currently, Mai's spirit has taken on the form of a tiny creature. She has a turtle for a head with a bow on top and an animal-like face that is located below the turtle's head. Her body is small in comparison, having tiny, stubby limbs, and wears a small dress.
Gallery

Mai Kawabanga's full appearance as a guardian spirit.
Mai Kawabanga's full appearance as a guardian spirit.
Mai's spirit after its release of its Onbusuman form.
Mai's spirit after its release of its Onbusuman form.
ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

While alive, Mai was a kind, friendly and cheerful little girl. She dreamed of becoming an idol and was very committed to achieving this goal by occasionally practicing with Rin and her friends. In addition, she did not take it lightly when others looked down on her dream, as she could no longer be friends with Rin after the latter doubted to Mai on whether being an idol held any worth, calling her out as a traitor. However, after finding out that Rin's criticism came from her having a hard life taking care of her grandmother, Mai felt empathetic and wanted to sincerely apologize to her.

After her spirit was released of her Onbusuman form, Mai chose to continue staying by Rin's side as a guardian spirit to see to it that she uses her singing talents to become an idol. As a guardian spirit, Mai has a rather blunt and stubborn personality that makes her come off as rude. In light of Rin's true goal to become a novelist, Mai did not take no for an answer and outright told her that her life has no meaning if she doesn't follow down the path of an idol. She also has a lack of respect for others that prompts her to throw insults. Although she doesn’t respect Rin's current wishes, she is quick to come to Rin's defense whenever other people insult her, showing that she still cares deeply for her friend.
ADVERTISEMENT

Background

Born with a natural talent for dancing, Mai grew up with the desire to be an idol. She would befriend likeminded girls of her age with the hopes that one day they could become an idol group together. After hearing Rin Sawaki sing during class, she asked her to join her in pursuing her idol dream. The two of them, along with the other girls, would train constantly, with Mai's outgoing nature helping Rin break out of her shell. One day, Mai learned of Junior Idol auditions and encouraged her friends to audition with her, as it could be their ticket to TV stardom. Unbeknownst to her, Rin, someone whose singing talent she relied on, had to take care of her ill grandmother while her mother was off to work.

After Rin clarified her reasons for not being able to attend, neither Mai nor their mutual friends grasped the seriousness of her circumstances, assuming that Rin was either being dishonest or that her mother was simply lazy. This led Rin to confront Mai, questioning the value of pursuing an idol career. In response, Mai accused Rin of betrayal and, along with her friends, abandoned her, confident they could proceed to the auditions without her. However, when the audition day arrived, Mai was consumed by anxiety and realized she couldn't go through with it without Rin. She then requested her mother to pick her up. Upon learning that Rin was permitted to join them, Mai asked her mother to take her along, feeling remorseful for her earlier words and wanting to apologize in person. Tragically, they were involved in a car accident en route to pick up Rin, resulting in both of their deaths. Overwhelmed by guilt and resentment for what she perceived as betrayal, Mai began to haunt Rin as an Onbusuman yokai.

Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Acrobatic Silky Arc

Around the time she discovered one of Okarun's kintama and caught sight of Okarun transforming in class, Rin began to notice Mai's presence as an Onbusuman as she started to feel weighed down.

Onbusuman Arc

After leaving the Kamigoe Police Box with Okarun in hopes of retrieving his kintama back, Rin becomes crushed under the weight of the Onbusuman, much to Okarun's shock. He takes Rin to the Ayase residence for help, where Seiko identifies the yokai and its link to Rin's past. Seiko decides that purifying Mai's spirit requires visiting her accident site and the audition venue. Knowing the Onbusuman will appear in spirit-rich areas, Seiko takes Rin, along with Momo and Okarun, to Kami High, and hires dashi carriers for transportation, and the Hayashi for protection against the awakened spirits who will be chasing them on their route. Then operation then commences upon the Onbusuman's appearance and the awakening of the school spirits.

The Onbusuman then reappears and begins to grow in size in response to Rin's singing. Upon arriving at the scene of the accident, Mai's spirit recalls her memories of departing the audition venue to seek forgiveness from Rin and becomes freed of her Onbusuman state, enabling Mai and Rin to revive their friendship as the former finally has the chance to apologize to her childhood friend. The two then join voices in a duet to defeat the Shining School Building and make their way to the audition venue. There, Rin watches as Mai's spirit starts to dissipate. Before her departure, Mai hears Rin expressing her joy singing and dancing with her to potentially become idols together. In response, Mai confesses her envy of Rin's shift in demeanor whenever she sung, admitting that her own aspiration to be an idol stemmed from wanting to meet her mother's expectations, which she believed made her the real traitor. However, Rin reassures Mai that she is mistaken about herself, emphasizing that her kindness, cheerful demeanor, and determination to fulfill expectations are what truly make her admirable and an idol in the eyes of those around her. Mai then cries feeling touched by Rin's words and completely vanishes.

Danmara Arc

The partecipants of the Onbusuman Operation reunite back in the Ayase Residence and have a celebratory dinner together, however between them Mai reappears as she couldn't pass on to the afterlife and she has turned into a weird floating spirit, with a small body and a big head formed primarily by a turtle-like creature with a bowtie on its head. Seiko reassures the kids that Mai is not dangerous and she has now become a guardian spirit. Okarun still wonders why she couldn't find peace and pass on so the spirit explains that she must first see Rin become an idol. The class rep states that it's no longer her dream but Mai insists since she has an innate talent for singing and if she doesn't, her life would have no purpose. Momo finds it harsh although she quickly gets shut off by the spirit who wants to keep Rin away from ordinary people like her. Mai demands to know her dreams and Rin embarassingly states she wants to write light novels. Mai puts her down as it's harder than it sounds like and she doesn't even have anything to write, although Rin declares she would like to write a romance story between a vampire and a girl. They keep bickering while Momo teases Okarun as she's sure that he has read her letter when he woke up during the Kur Invasion.

Rin and Mai return to the house the following day, welcomed by Bamora and by Turbo Granny to give her thanks to Momo who's unfortunately missing inside the cursed trunk. Discovering that Seiko is missing, Okarun turns to the Turbo Granny and questions her about the diorama. She demands something in return but out of nowhere Mai ticks her off by saying that she doesn't have a clue. Mai is surprised by her behavior and the Turbo Granny, offended, tries to punch her but she cannot reach her in the air. Mai and Bamora try to get them to stop and the latter states that they don't get along and they often fight. Okarun asks Mai about the cursed trunk yet this time it's the Turbo Granny who insults her memory span. They keep bickering until Okarun kneels to the ground and begs the Turbo Granny to help Momo and in exchange he will give her anything. The cat, realizing the gravity of the situation, recruits Mai and Rin to rescue everyone stuck inside the diorama.

With the unfortunate release of the Fairy-Tale Card after the breakage of the four seals, Turbo Granny contacts Rin and Mai who are standing outside and she intructs them to lower the trunk onto the black cloth to then remove all the figurines safely. Since touching it directly would transport them to Danmara, which happens to a girl who carelessly used sticks as leverage, the Turbo Granny instructs to grab strands of black cloth and have Mai transport it since she, like all spirits, has resistance to curses. However, Mai refuses to do her bidding out of spite and instead convinces Rin to save them. She reminds Rin that she's haunting her to turn into an idol and Mai transforms into pure spiritual malevolent energy which surrounds the class rep, giving her an embarassing idol outfit and Mai serves as her microphone. While she convinces everyone to cheer Rin on to strengthen her, the latter can't bear the awkwardness and doesn't understand why she has to sing. She's shocked when Mai tells her that she will be stuck like that for the rest of her life if she doesn't, so upon hearing the bystanders encouraging her, she tries to clear her mind. Meanwhile, Turbo Granny goes mad and she desperately insults Mai as they are all about to deleted from the inner world.

Suddenly, they hear someone singing and everyone other than Momo is lifted into the sky, so Turbo Granny realizes the Onbusuman controls gravity and through Rin's voice they are lifting the figurines out of the diorama without touching it. Accompanied by music produced by two band members, Rin is now determined and sings at her fullest while Mai cheers her on. Soon after, all the players inside return to Earth although between them the Fairy-Tale Card, who was using Unji Zuma's body which has Umbrella Boy's powers as a vessel, escapes. The Card immediately sets sight on Rin and attempts to manipulate her to break her mind, bringing up her complicated childhood. Thankfully, Mai blasts him away and announces he won't be able to control her because she's her producer and she won't allow him to do so. Because of this, the Fairy-Tale Card uses his mouth card to make Rin's mouth vanish, impeding her singing and thus her offensive output. Rin and Mai observe the fight and the unexpected arrival of the Count of Saint Germain who turns the tide of battle and defeats the yokai along with Okarun, Bega and Rokuro. Immediately after, Okarun begs the two to sing again as Momo and Turbo Granny are still stuck inside the Danmara. Unexpectedly, when they are brought out, Momo has shrunk down to the size of a palm.

Days later, Seiko offers to eat at every student caught in the fight at the Goro Stamina Booster restaurant. Momo promises to her friends that she's going to call them for the next paranormal occurence, however Mai bursts in and affirms that they won't be needed as her and Rin alone suffice. Aira, who has never met her before, gets tilted and she insults her beauty, to which Mai points out Aira's the ugly one and Rin is a hundred times prettier than her.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Rin was observing up close Kouki Yukishiro who was brought to the school's gym by her blackmailer when she suddenly was snuck up behind by the latter who summoned the Severed Head Dribblers that slammed Rin into the court's hoop before Mai could do anything. Aira, who came to their rescue while Okarun and Kinta got attacked, entered the gym and fought against the creatures until she saw Rin's floating head with Mai crying next to it. Mai explains what happened and the abilities of their enemies. In tears she insults Aira while asking her on how to save her, so she affirms they have to find the power user who controls them, similarly to the previous fight against Kouki. Suddenly, Rin regains consciousness despite having no body and Mai is rejoyced. However, Mai informs them that Rin is stuck between the mortal world and the afterlife, so if all of her entire life force spills out from her neck, she's going to die permanently. A Severed Head Dribbler targets Aira so Mai jumps in her way to protect her but Aira realizes she's more vulnerable than her and pushes her out of the way, unfortunately getting hurt in the process.

Mai is desperate and tries to cheer Aira on so she can continue fighting. She asks Rin if she's in a condition to sing but she exclaims that she cannot without her entire body. An headless player grabs Aira and dribbles his way to the hoop while Mai asks him to stop and gets in the way, although her small size makes it futile. Thanks to Aira's quick wits, she forces Rin's head through the hoop from the opposite direction, giving back her body and allowing Mai to turn into a microphone and activate her gravitational powers, defending the girls from the Severed Head Dribblers. She explains to Aira that Rin can control gravity although she's more focused on her embarassing outfit. They fend off the foes until Mai spots Kouki's head surrounded by Pygmies. Because the other two cannot see the creatures, Mai abandons Rin momentarily while she approaches the little men and teams up with them to bring Kouki's back. A pygmy grabs onto her ear and a chain of the creatures forms until they mimic a human player and they weave through the defenders on the court. Mai tries to slam Kouki in the hoop but she's stopped by multiple dribblers who guard it, so the pygmies create an alternative route under them and force their master's head through, returning her body. Mai returns to the powerless Rin who was being protected by Aira and starts singing again while Kouki informs them that her blackmailer is Murakami and what he has done. They decide to find him and defeat him but out of nowhere the Dribblers turn gigantic and the gym starts shrinking. Aira realizes that Rin's range of gravity is getting narrower so Mai informs them that Rin is still a novice and will only last a couple more minutes. Aira cannot defend all of them alone so they scramble to find Murakami, who's actually in the comfort of his apartment monitoring the scene.

He is an alien who attacked Momo and Okarun while they were at school after coming to Earth to collect test subjects.

In Dandadan, he serves as the main antagonist during the One-Shot Profoundly Mysterious Kick-the-Can Battle.

Appearance

The alien resembles a bipedal mandrill while outfitted with a long-sleeved shirt with two breast pockets and feautres a dark stripe extending from the collar to each sleeve. He also wears matching pants and boots.
Personality

The mandrill alien is very self-confident, assertive and narcissistic. He perceives himself as a superior being, a notion he supports with his claimed IQ of 300, which he frequently boasts about to his targets. Success in his plans also helps to inflate his massive ego. He possesses a low opinion of humans, regarding them as primitive creatures characterized by barbarism and ignorance. However, his opinion may change if he comes across one who exceeds his expectations, as he praised Momo for lasting long enough to avoid getting turned into a can by his Territory Can. Taking great pride in his intellect, he finds it intolerable for someone to label him as stupid, resulting in him exhibiting aggressive behavior towards the one who made the remark. Ironically, he also finds it offensive to be called "monkey" despite his appearance. Although he possesses a strong sense of pride, he was not so overly arrogant admitting that he couldn't comprehend how Momo avoided his first can attack directed at her, however, he did believe that the unforeseen moment must have been noteworthy if it managed to exceed someone of his intellect. He is also very persistent, as he was determined to take down Momo after she foiled his plans.

He has a unique speech pattern in which he ends almost every sentence he speaks with the word "bro" and, as his fight against Momo and Okarun drags on, he also adds "ook" to his vocabulary.
Synopsis

Profoundly Mysterious Kick-the-Can Battle!

After arriving at Kami High, the Mandrill Alien activates Empty Space and setups his Territory Can to initiate his operation of turning every human into walking cans for his plan to experiment on them later. With Momo and Okarun being the only ones not turned into a can, the Mandrill Alien targets them, starting with Momo in her class. The Mandrill Alien makes an attempt to strike Momo with a can but fails after the girl lowers her head onto her desk on time, leaving him astonished and questioning how she could foresee his move. He subsequently launches a second assault, causing her to be propelled out of the classroom. Once more, the Mandrill Alien is taken aback when Momo successfully deflects his attack. In response, he hurls several cans at her, which she blocks using her psychic hands, while insisting that he cease his littering. After Momo meets up with Okarun, who flees from the transformed can students, the Mandrill Alien reveals to them the function of his Territory Can and his intent with the humans he capture. Following Momo and Okarun's arrival at the rooftop, the Mandrill Alien tries deceiving them into destroying the Territory Can by begging them not to. Okarun comes on to the alien's game and comes between Momo and the Territory Can to block Momo from kicking it, resulting in him being transformed into a walking can after he is knocked back into the Territory Can.[1]

After leaping from the roof and using her psychic power to navigate herself into a classroom, the Mandrill Alien faces Momo once again. Disappointed that Momo didn't transform into a can as he had planned, he reveals that the Territory Can is designed to turn people into cans upon contact if they try to destroy it. He then commends Momo for not being as barbaric and foolish as he initially thought humans were, which only fuels his eagerness to dissect her. After Momo retorts, declaring that he is the real monkey lacking intelligence, while also claiming that her IQ is higher than his, the Mandrill Alien furiously launches a barrage of cans towards her after becoming enraged by her insults. He warns her that the small cans he is launching can also transform her into a can, and doubts her ability to sustain her psychic shield for long. After ceasing his assault and seeing Momo bleed from deflecting the cans, he suggests she apologize, thinking she won't survive his next attack. However, as he notices the classroom collapsing, Momo reveals she had tricked him into destroying the pillar supporting the Territory Can on the roof to let it fall and collapse the moment it hits the ground. Despite his Territory Can being destroyed, the Mandrill Alien refuses to admit defeat and comes in to attack Momo with his staff. However, he is suddenly attacked and knocked out of the school by Okarun using his headbutt attack in his Turbo Granny form.[2]

Abilities and Powers

Trivia

The design of the Space Scientist greatly resembles Dr. Gori from the Spectreman series.
The design of the Space Scientist's staff references the titular Spectreman as well.

The Mantis Exosuit Kur was a Kur of the Advance Unit who wielded the Mantis Exosuit.

In Dandadan, he serves as a major antagonist during the Space Globalists Arc.

Appearance

The Kur has never been seen outside of his Mantis Exosuit. Nonetheless, being a Kur, he is presumed to share the octopus-like physiology characteristic of his species.
Personality

He affirms that he enjoys utilizing his exosuit to the fullest during the fight with Mr. Mantis Shrimp and like many other Kurs, he considers himself above others thanks to the powers of the suit.
Background

The Mantis Exosuit Kur partecipated in the invasion of Sumer. He guarded over the Sumerian men to have them fed to Big Mama in front of the pyramid. He later entered it with the rest of the Advance Unit and threatened to torture Aja if Banga did not activate the royal slab which only sumerians can decipher.
Synopsis

Space Globalists Arc

He first appeared along with the other Advance Unit members to defeat Okarun and retrieve his Kintama to power the warp gate needed for the main Kur fleet.

At the start of the Kur Invasion, the Mantis Exosuit Kur focuses his efforts on Mr. Mantis Shrimp, utilizing his long blades to keep his distance and cause trouble to Jiji and Aira at the same time.

He briefly appears during the invasion of Sumer, guarding the male Sumerian prisoners from possible threats to have them eaten by Big Mama. Following the escape sequence, he approaches Banga along with the Advance Unit.

The Mantis is able to isolate Mr. Mantis Shrimp who throws himself into the water. The Mantis Exosuit Kur transforms in an underwater based form and reveals that he gets 100 times stronger in water before rushing towards him. He wipes the floor with him and he even pierces the Dover Demon with a venom-injecting needle, which will dissolve his inner organs. The lack of distance between the two allows Peeny Weeny to land a cataclysmic jab in his Dover Demon Strong Style Twenty-Four, its strength derived from the fact that he gets 24 times stronger when he transforms and also gets 10 times stronger underwater, surpassing the Mantis Exosuit Kur's strength by over 140 times. He can't believe it and calls his calculations absurd before being hit with a final Jet Punch, which annihilates him and makes the exosuit explode.

Masamichi Bega (部べ賀が正道, Bega Masamichi?), also known as Bega the Demon (鬼の部べ賀が, Oni no Bega?), is a police officer stationed at the Kamigoe Police Box.

Appearance

Bega is a middle-aged man with pronounced facial features and maintains a stern look that gives him an intimidating presence. He wears the standard uniform for a police officer, which includes a cap.
Personality

Bega is a serious and strict man who is fully committed in ensuring the enforcement of the law in his role as a police officer. He is shown to be extremely cautious when on the job at the Kamigoe Police Box, having been suspicious of Momo and Okarun coming into the police box claiming Turbo Granny to be a lost item, especially the latter who came to the police box earlier seeking to reclaim his second kintama, and was prompted to perform a thorough inspection for any hidden cameras within the maneki-neko doll. Along with his serious disposition, Bega is a compassionate individual, having taken Unji in as his guardian to avoid having him back out on the streets and jumped into a river without a second thought to save a boy from drowning.
Background

Bega enlisted as a police officer around the time he was married and had a daughter. After both his wife and daughter were murdered by an assailant out on the streets, Bega confronted the man responsible and learned that his hatred towards society drove him to kill his family. Though he held a grudge against him, Bega at times found himself unable to act on his urge to commit murder-suicide towards the man due to the image of his daughter appearing in his head.

Bega apprehended gang leader Unji Zuma after the delinquent instigated a fight between his gang and the police officers out on duty. Following Unji's release from juvenile detention, Bega makes the decision to become his guardian to avoid having him out on the streets again. While trying to properly raise Unji, Bega allowed him to make attempts at attacking him with an umbrella to seek payback for arresting him, though each time he was easily bested by the man. After Unji expressed curiosity about his family, Bega recounted the loss of his own family and how this led him to take in the young man and become committed to protecting him. Unji tells Bega that he cannot comprehend his perspective despite all that society has subjected him and his family to, and leaves the apartment to visit the location where his brother was discovered deceased. Upon locating him, Bega spots a boy drowning in the river and instructs Unji to alert the fire department before he leaps into the water, attempting a rescue. Just as he is about to blackout from trying to get the boy to safety, Bega and the boy are pulled out of the water by Unji using the spiritual power of Umbrella Boy after the young man encountered the yokai and was offered his umbrella abilities. The two then become relieved to see the people they tried to safe are alive.

The next day, Bega goes along with Unji to visit the latter's family grave. While traveling, Bega asks Unji how he managed to save him the other day, but Unji refuses to divulge this information, deeming Bega foolish for his reckless behavior at the time. While paying respects to Unji's late mother, father, and brother, Bega hears Unji voicing his survivor's guilt, feeling that his younger brother Futa should be alive instead of him to guarantee their mother's happiness. In response, Bega places his hand on Unji's head and solemnly counters his statement, insisting that Unji's duty is to live on.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Onbusuman Arc

At the Kamigoe Police Box, Okarun and Rin meet Bega at the front desk to retrieve the kintama that was earlier submitted as a lost item by the latter. Bega informs them that someone had already claimed it and that he can't divulge private information of who it was that took. Along with this, he also advises against trying to steal it from the person.

Danmara Arc

Momo and Okarun come up to Bega at the police box submitting Turbo Granny as a lost item. As they fill out the form, Bega grows suspicious and questions them to ascertain if the maneki-neko doll is indeed lost property as they allege. Just as he prepares to search Turbo Granny for any hidden cameras, a noise emanating from the backroom, created by Momo using her psychic powers, prompts him to remove his hands from the doll and check. Before Momo and Okarun depart, Bega instructs them to take the form and inquires if they desire a reward, which they decline.

Later, Bega goes out on patrol and comes back to the police box to find Momo and Okarun fighting with each. After walking pass them and demanding that they return home, Bega finds himself face-to-face with Rokuro disguised as a police officer and ends up getting into a fight with him. While Rokuro claims to be a police officer from a different police box, Bega calls his station for confirmation and is informed that the man in front of him is indeed who he says he is. Unbeknownst to Bega, the voice on the phone was actually Rokuro, who had used his nanoskin to secretly tap into the officer's phone. Bega then prepares to give Rokuro the lost property data he came for and recommends fighting at the station dojo the next time he is looking for a sparring match.

While patrolling, Bega spots Okarun and Rin riding their bikes at night and chases them, as it was past the curfew for high school students. His pursuit of them leads him to entering the inner world of the cursed trunk keeping the Fairy-Tale Card. After wondering if everything happening is a dream or not, Bega focuses on apprehending all those he deems as lawbreakers, beginning with the Fairy-Tale Card who has taken control of Unji. Bega also deems Rokuro as a lawbreaker as well for possessing a gun but fights alongside him regardless. With his gun out of bullets, Bega runs trying to avoid Umbrella Boy Unji's shockwaves and assists in executing Okarun's strategy to generate a tornado to ground Umbrella Boy Unji by energizing Rokuro's nanoskin heater with his own body heat. After their plan succeeds, the trio confronts Umbrella Boy Unji in a close combat showdown. Upon Umbrella Boy Unji's defeat fighting Okarun, Bega is stunned to recognize the young man beneath the cracked mask as Unji and questions why he is here after searching for him for so long.

Bega attempts to reach out to Unji, urging him to regain his senses as the Fairy-Tale Card increasingly possesses his body. However, he becomes too late, as the Fairy-Tale Card utilizes Unji's power to fly out of the cursed trunk. Shortly after, he and the other captives trapped in the cursed trunk are lifted into the air by Rin, who employs Mai's Onbusuman gravity powers to free them all from the world. He then seizes Rokuro's leg, while the alien grasps Okarun's leg to prevent further ascension, but the two are soon elevated after Momo compels Okarun to release her hand so he can return to the other side and defeat the Fairy-Tale Card. Following the conclusion of Rin's gravitational melody, Bega, Okarun, and Rokuro experience a sudden descent. In response, Rokuro activates his nanoskin to form jet booster arms, while Okarun and Bega grasp onto his legs. However, the Serpo observes that the additional weight hinders his ability to ascend further.

After managing to escape the cursed trunk, Bega immediately demands the Fairy-Tale Card to return Unji to him. Bega panics to find Unji on the brink of death and desperately tries to revive him. Upon seeing Unji regaining consciousness and asserting his determination not to die to the officer, Bega becomes relieved and informs him that they will be going home together. He then helps to support Unji as he helps Okarun, Rokuro, and Count Saint-Germain defeat the Fairy-Tale Card by firing a shockwave blast.

Following the resolution of the incidents involving the cursed trunk and the Fairy-Tale Card, Bega and Unji became hospitalized for treatment. In the hospital, Bega questions Unji about his silence regarding the cursed trunk and his umbrella powers. Unji admits that he thought Bega wouldn't have believed such an absurd story if he had told him. He then clarifies the situation with the old man the officer found in their home, explaining that he allowed him to stay out of compassion, as the man had been trapped in the cursed trunk for an extended period. Regarding his absence, Unji mentioned that he had notified Baison at the police box. Bega states that he had no prior knowledge of this, despite being aware of Unji's visit to the police box from the lost and found logs. Unji also recalled visiting the police box to collect the kintama, following advice from someone that it was essential for opening the trunk, though he couldn't recall who provided that information.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Following his and Unji's release from the hospital, the two and Unji's gang reunited Daiki with his parents. However, due to the child's elderly appearance from the cursed trunk's curse, along with the fact that he had been missing for only four years, Daiki's parents refuse to take their word that he is their son.

Later, Bega arrived at Juicy Gyoza Manufactory Dandadan to investigate reports of suspicious activity. The staff informs him of a middle-aged man who had been alone upstairs, and mentions that earlier there had been three others—a beautiful woman and two men. Spotting a trio who fit the description—Seiko, Payase and Kashimoto—Bega approaches them for questioning, only for them to disappear and leave the officer confused.

Mika Adachi (足あ立だち美み加か, Adachi Mika?) is a teacher of Class 2-E at Kami High.

In Dandadan, she serves as a minor antagonist in Kozuka Knives Arc.

Appearance

Adachi is a slender young woman of average height with straight dark hair parted in the middle. In her initial appearance, her hair was cut to a neck-length bob, but in subsequent appearances, it has grown down to reach her shoulders. Her teacher's attire consists of a scoop-neck shirt with teacher's lanyard hanging from her neck and yoga pants.
Personality

Adachi is deeply devoted to her mother and is willing to go to great lengths to provide her with support. She was willing to heed the commands of a stranger to confront Seiko and seize her power in return for a wish that could benefit her mother. Additionally, she was willingly to subject herself to humiliation by donning a provocative bunny outfit for Murakami, aiming to earn money from him to facilitate her mother's placement in a home.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Onbusuman Arc

While seated at her desk in the faculty office, Adachi greets a mysterious man occupying Murakami's desk. She feels both charmed and puzzled by his presence as he introduces himself as Sanjome. Murakami then walks in puzzled about where his desk is and looks to Adachi for help, only for the woman to discover that she is just as confused. When Murakami finally notices Sanjome's presence, he is convinced of the man's claim to the seat after Sanjome states his name, leading Murakami to identify him as the deputy head teacher.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

At some point, Adachi affiliated herself with a mysterious person who was willingly to grant her a wish in exchange for her helping him collect yokai powers using Asura knives. Upon accepting, Adachi was partnered up with a working man to target Seiko Ayase at Juicy Gyoza Manufactory Dandadan. Before leaving, she interacted with female student Kouki Yukishiro.

After tracking down Seiko, Adachi deployed her jiangshi to engage the spirit medium while remotely controlling them from a distance outside the restaurant. When the confrontation ended in her partner's defeat, Adachi wasted no time fleeing the scene and heading back to Kami High. Upon her return, she was intercepted by Murakami, who questioned her whereabouts. Adachi smoothly covered her absence by claiming she had been taking care of her mother. Murakami then extended an invitation for her to join the staff at a basketball singles mixer, but she respectfully declined. Once she distanced herself from him, Adachi takes out her phone to check the message she had sent to the orchestrator, informing them of her failure to complete the mission, and summons her jiangshi behind her.

Later, Adachi is offered by Murakami financial support for her mother in exchange for accompanying him to his apartment. After accepting, Adachi finds herself coerced into wearing a provocative bunny outfit to satisfy her coworker's inappropriate desires, leaving her deeply humiliated. Despite complying with his demands, Murakami chastises her for her somber expression, warning that he will withhold his support unless she adjusts her demeanor. As he returns to his training, Adachi discreetly clutches a talisman behind her back, concealing her true intentions. Later, Murakami pushes her on the couch to indulge in his fantasies, however Adachi is determined and secretly manifests the jiangshi behind him. She offers to buy as much time as possible so the creatures can strike when his guard is lowered due to him possessing an unknown power. A fly interferes in the plan and Murakami turns around, noticing both the jiangshi and the swarm of bugs unconsciously controlled by Kouki while they are fighting his Severed Head Dribblers. The flies engulf him and forcefully enter his body from every orifice. Adachi is shocked but doesn't waste time and pulls out a black kozuka knife and demands him to yield. He initially hesitates but he grabs the knife and admits defeat, leading to his powers getting stripped. He falls to the ground and asks for help so Adachi and the jiangshi intervene out of pity to save the man from the swarm when he's suddenly launched out of the window and brought to the gym of Kami High where Kouki, Mai, Rin and Aira were just fighting in.

Adachi, now in possession of Murakami's powers, contacts the Orchestrator and she's instructed to meet a subordinate of theirs at the embankment under the overpass. She meets a strange looking businessman and she quickly gets anxious. She suddenly receives a call from the Orchestrator who informs her that even though she had been working hard, Murakami was on their side and they did not classify him as a target. They question why she attacked him and she states that she had felt his spiritual energy and believed he had powers of his own too. They informed her that the Lord of the Flies power user did all the job and they order Adachi to hand in the kozuka knife to the man in front of her, in addition to the powers she were given previously. Adachi begs to keep them when the mastermind affirms that to steal a power, the surrender of the enemy must come deep within their heart which is especially undecipherable and mysterious. Because they are targeting a very strong person who is likely in possession of an ID Cosmos, they would have to ambush and hurt the people close to them like friends and relatives to make their heart tremble. The Orchestrator is aware that Adachi wouldn't willingly commit those acts and as she keeps begging to keep contributing to the mastermind's schemes in order to cure her ill mother, the businessman pushes her down and repeatedly strikes her with his luggage, demanding her to admit defeat. She gets rescued by Bega and the subordinate suddenly manifests Fairy-Tale Card to possess him. The yokai recognizes him from the incident and he realizes he cannot brainwash him so he opts to control Adachi, launching her towards the cop who easily puts her down. In this brief window of time, the power user flees the scene.

Abilities and Powers

Supernatural Abilities

Jiangshi Control [v · e]
Adachi possess the power to summon and control jiangshi. Due to her association with the orchestrator who is in possession of Asura knives, it can be implied that she acquired this power through them.
Adachi's Jiangshi manipulation
Strengths and Weaknesses
This power allows Adachi to summon an army of jiangshi and command them to fight on her behalf using kung fu. The jiangshi disappear when Adachi deactivates her power but loyally follow her wherever she goes while invisible. It is unclear whether this constant presence is a deliberate act by Adachi, an inherent trait of the jiangshi, or a manifestation of her power perpetually at work.
Usage
Adachi has the jiangshi engage in battle while she remains at a safe distance, watching and controlling from a secure vantage point.

Miko (ミーコ, Mīko?) is a recurring character of the Dandadan series. Along with Muko, she is the best friend and classmate of Momo Ayase at high school.

Appearance

Miko is a young girl of average height with hair preferably stylized in a small bun. She is mainly seen wearing her school uniform: a long sleeve sweater on top of a white undershirt with a loose bow, a skirt, baggy socks, and sandals. By the Evil Eye Arc, she has started wearing a jacket on top of her uniform.
Personality

Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Turbo Granny Arc

After Momo breaks up with her arrogant boyfriend, she returns to class and informs Miko and Muko, who previously told her she shouldn't date him. Ayase affirms she only went out with him because he looked like the actor Ken Takakura, annoying Miko who tells her that hard-boiled tough guys like her favorite actor are a thing of the past.

Miko and Muko later wander through the hallways and spot Momo bickering with a nerd from Class 2-C, leading them to believe she has ditched her Ken Takakura for the geek type, however Miko doesn't care about his looks and she's okay with it.

Acrobatic Silky

Miko and Muko notice Ayase has been really quiet lately and the fact that she hasn't responded to Miko's messages and that she was absent from school the previous day makes her very suspicious. Muko theorizes she ran back to her ex-boyfriend but got dumped again and broke her phone in a fit, to which Miko agrees. They both stare at Momo screaming and collapsing, secretly wanting to meet with Okarun and talk to him about aliens.

At the end of school's lunch, Ayase and Takakura accidentally crash into each other and kiss, however Miko and Muko were already there and they are surprised by Momo finding a new boyfriend just a few days after she broke up with her ex, reason why she was so weird and quiet earlier. The two lovebirds insult each other to avoid further embarassment and leave, though this just reassures Momo's friends that they are really close. In class, Miko tells her classmates that she made out with a geek and points him when he enters the room. She keeps teasing Ayase about their relationship despite her denying what happened. After Momo asks Okarun to shut up and leave, Miko is perplexed by her rudeness and tells her she didn't have to reject him so harshly. She points out that if the geek was just a friend she wouldn't have reacted that way and she states that she has never seen her act like that before.

The next day, Momo reveals to Miko that Okarun has been avoiding her lately, so her friend affirms that he's a good guy who, according from someone in class 2-C, fought a student who was badmouthing Ayase because of recent rumors about her. Still, Ayase can't comprehend why he's keeping his distance from her.

Serpo Arc

Since Okarun is apparently busy with his school report, Momo informs her friends about him and proposes to have lunch together. Still, she has a bad feeling on the overall situation and the thought of him going out with Shiratori flashes through her mind. She decides to go buy a drink and so Miko asks for one too. Ayase returns, having spotted Okarun standing over Aira behind the school, tells Miko that she gave the drinks to the ground, which the two interpret as a joke and slams her head on the desk, explaining that she's thinking about something. Later in biology class, Momo observes the mantis shrimp inside its tank and synthonizes with its destructive feelings, making her punch herself multiple times in the face while rethinking about Takakura and Shiratori. Miko and Muko are shocked by her behavior and can only assume she has been possessed by the spirit of the mantis shrimp.

With the defeat of the Serpo Dover Demon Nessie, Momo, Okarun and Aira exit Empty Space while being almost naked in front of the whole school. They escape and hide in Queen's nursery and as Ayase is just about to express what she's feeling to Ken, Miko and Muko rush their way in and explain that she had disappeared in the middle of class according to their friend Kana who also spotted her hugging Okarun while they were both naked in front of class D. Momo doesn't even try to escape the absurd situation they found themselves in, so Miko squeezes her brain juices and determines that she and Shiratori, who form a love triangle with Takakura, had nude gladatorial combat to claim him. She points out that earlier Momo was studying how to punch by observing the mantis shrimp so she could beat Aira. Miko keeps screaming out that Ayase has been acting weird lately because she's jealous over Okarun, so Momo forces her to shut her mouth to avoid embarrasing herself further in front of Ken.

Cursed House Arc

Jin Enjoji enters Kami High in Momo'ìs class and sits next to her friend group, who initially find him annoying because he's a playboy. Jiji says to Miko that he's honored being insulted by such a beauty, so she gives in and tells Ayase that he's a good dude after all. Miko asks Momo who he actually is but she can't find the right words, so Jiji stands up and reveals that they him and Ayase are living together, shocking Miko and the entire class.

Evil Eye Arc

Momo announces to Miko and Muko that she's going to get a part-time job. Miko wants to know why and she explains she has to gather enough money to fix her house, which is currently being damaged by the Evil Eye's shenanigans, however she would like her to buy a new phone so they can stay in contact as she can't believe her house is seriously that cold at the moment. Muko brings up Ririna's looking for help at her job and Miko remembers she's working at a restaurant. Ayase immediately wants to start but Miko fears she won't last long due to her rebellious personality and finds it hard to recommend her to Ririna if she's just going to call it quits after a bit, however Momo insists she's a grown up now. Miko and Muko smile at each other, realizing that Momo has accepted to work in a maid restaurant without knowing.

Miko and Muko go to class 2-C and inform Okarun of Ayase's absence. He understands and gets up to leave when he's suddenly jumped on by the two girls who force him to hangout with them despite him refusing. Outside of school, Okarun tells the girls that he doesn't go out on dates but they specify it isn't yet he keeps considering it that. Miko wonders if he also thinks Jiji and Momo having tea together would be a date which he denies, infuriating her because of his inconsistency. They lead him to the Moe Moe Kikoho and he refuses to drink, so Miko annoyingly says she's fine with it and the two bring him inside. Upon noticing Ayase in a maid outfit, Okarun's face becomes all red while Miko asks her to serve him. Momo doesn't greet them and just tells them follow her, so Miko calls the other worker to reprimand her for her bad attitude.

At their table, Miko asks again for Okarun if he wants anything to drink as they have to order and this time he agrees since Momo is working so hard for them, however this just ticks her off since he said otherwise a few minutes earlier. Momo performs a chant while pouring down the tea although Miko forces her to put more love into it as she's not concentrated and has to put her mind into it, infuriating Ayase. In the end, everyone performs the Moe Moe Tri-Beam while posing for a group picture. Momo promises to get back at them for what they did, but Miko and Muko laugh and leave as they have already taken enough pictures of her in her maid outfit. Surprisingly, Okarun declares he wants to stay and the two girls blush, realizing what he wants to do, and wish the two lovers to have fun.

Kaiju Arc

Miko and Muko are briefly seen in class while the Evil Eye takes over Jiji and announces he's going to kill all humans, although no one takes him seriously. Later, the two girls ask Momo if he's serious since he's very consistent about it. Muko theorizes he's possessed by the apartment-complex ghost and might have the golden ball, surprising Ayase. Miko understands her shock since she doesn't have a phone and shows her their group chat which has been recently only talking about the apartment-complex specter.

Space Globalists Arc

Kinta Sakata is wondering around the school since he wants to show off to his friends his made up injuries, however he cannot find them anywhere and Miko, Muko and Ririna are briefly seen chatting in class 2-C.

Minehisa has a really tall and buff body compared to his schoolmates even when he's hunched over. He wears the school's gakuran, he has two knife-like earrings and a sort of jewel placed on the bridge of his nose. He keeps his hair slicked back in a voluminous helmet-like shape. He has a very intimidating appearance, always looking angry, also emphatized by his completely white eyes.
Personality

Despite appearing furious and intimidating most of the time, he cares a lot about girls, as seen when he forced his classmate to apologize to Momo, when he and his friends defended Momo from the enemy troops and when he tried to protect Rin during the fight against the Fairy-Tale Card. He says that people who make girls will not be tolerated and his class abides to this ideology. Because the Fairy-Tale Card managed to possess him, it might indicate he has experienced trauma and the yokai took advantage of it.
ADVERTISEMENT

Synopsis

Momo and Okarun approached Class B to ask about Unji Zuma but Reo touched her hair so she called him a creep. Minehisa saw this and appeared in front of them, scaring the duo as they thought he was Unji, and he asked to apologize. Momo stood her ground but he was actually talking to Reo, shouting that he can't just touch a girl's hair. He said sorry to Minehisa but he forced him to say it to Momo and Okarun. He then explained that anyone who makes a girl sad won't be tolerated in their class and they all stand by it. He informed the duo that they are in a middle of a dispute and they are waiting for their turn, accumulating murderuous rage, so he apologizes for the trouble they caused them. He tells them that Unji Zuma is from Class D, grade 10 but Momo at first glance believes that they won't even understand her, so Minehisa offers to accompany them and she appreciates it, although they all immediately start to insult and threaten each other.

Toriumi exclaims that she has no clue where Unji is, so Minehisa clarifies to Momo that he's not Unji but Toriumi who's ranked third in Class D. He gets mad hearing his placement as he deems it to be too low for him. Minehisa again asks him where Unji is and Toriumi finally tells them what he knows. Minehisa stares as Toriumi runs away from Okarun in his Turbo Granny form, reminding him of Unji.

Minehisa and all the other students of Renjaku High along Unji's gang entered the cursed trunk and they arrive just in time to defend Momo and Zuma from the enemy troops. He runs with his classmates in front of Momo, protecting her from projectiles with their giant shields so she genuinely thanks him.

He runs away from the unsealed Fairy-Tale Card but later returns with all the other delinquents led by Turbo Granny. Thanks to Rin's singing and Mai's work, he and everyone else is lifted into the sky. They finally reach Zuma up above, surprising the Fairy-Tale Card, and they then reappear on Earth where he succesfully lands and prepares to fight the yokai. However, the spirit uses his powers to split their forces and makes them fight against each other. Minehisa manages to block two mind controlled students and instructs everyone still conscious to protect Rin. Suddenly, his will submits to the yokai and he punches many people out of his way, with Daiki barely dodging his attack. His body rushes towards Rin but he gets sent flying out of nowhere, later revealed that it was Count Saint-Germain's doing. The count, assisted by Okarun, Bega, Unji and Rokuro, defeats the Fairy-Tale Card, freeing Minehisa from his mind control and he watches the beam of light emitted from the spirit.

The Minotaur refers to the subordinate of an unknown individual who was sent, along with Adachi, to confront Seiko Ayase at the Juicy Gyoza Manufactory Dandadan to steal her powers using an Asura knife.

In Dandadan, he serves as a minor antagonist during the Kozuka Knives Arc.

He is a large, muscular bipedal bull with eyes containing concentric circles, human hands, and a black metallic luster of iron skin. The only piece of clothing he wears are briefs.[1]
Personality

In a fight, the Minotaur is shown to be very respectful and civil towards his opponents, such as complimenting their skill in fighting.[2] However, he can become so caught up in the fight that he may resort to throwing forceful attacks at them.[3]
Synopsis

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Minotaur attacks Seiko
The Minotaur attacks Seiko.
Noticing the jiangshi struggling to pin down Seiko, the Minotaur steps in to attack Seiko by cannonballing himself towards her, causing her to be knocked back into a pillar. Following this, he takes a stance and praises Seiko for her impressive movements against the jiganshi, only for Seiko to humbly tell him she is simply old, much to his amusement. The Minotaur then makes his next move with an axe kick. Seiko moves out of the way of his attack and discovers that the Minotaur has a harden body after a kick aimed at this groin and a swing with a piece of wood empowered by the Power of Words did not faze him. The Minotaur appreciates Seiko taking note of his tough hide and reveals to her that his body is made of iron and that her attacks will only make his body stronger. After striking himself around his legs, he kicks Seiko into a wall and follows up with a barrage of punches, all while telling her that it is futile fighting against him. After defeating Seiko, the Minotaur takes out a knife from his briefs and offers to spare her life in exchange for her admitting defeat. Before he is given the chance, the Minotaur is struck with a powerful double blow by Payase and Kashimoto who prepare to fight the Minotaur and the jiangshi as their next opponents.[4]

Seiko defeats the Minotaur
The Minotaur defeated by Seiko.
The Minotaur revels in the presence of three formidable opponents, his excitement manifesting in a series of bizarre exclamations about his groin heating up. As the jiangshi charge forward, they are effortlessly stopped by Payase and Kashimoto's combined abilities. Impressed by Payase's powers, the Minotaur expresses his desire to wield them himself, only to be denied by the man. After his iron body withstands being pierced from below by Payase's shadow, the Minotaur seizes and hurls Payase aside. Kashimoto retaliates with a flurry of spirit-enhanced punches, managing to land significant blows. However, the Minotaur counters with a devastating jab to his chest and demands to receive more punishment. Amid the chaos, the Minotaur spots Seiko chasing after her purse and viciously kicks her against a wall, suspecting trickery within the bag. Kashimoto attempts a sneak attack but is sent flying by the Minotaur’s sheer strength. After he declares to have achieved a state of Ultimate Hotness, the Minotaur punches Payase as he tries to toss Seiko her bag and grabs the woman in a bear hug. Just as he demands for her to concede the fight, Kashimoto strikes again. The Minotaur suggests for Kashimoto to cease, telling his opponent that his attacks against him will only backfire on Seiko as it will go through him and affect her, as well as make him stronger. Despite her injuries, Seiko urges Kashimoto to continue. Just as the Minotaur seems invincible, Payase unexpectedly severs his arms, freeing Seiko. Shocked, the Minotaur is left grappling with this outcome, questioning how his supposedly invulnerable body failed him. Payase explains that intense light casts deeper shadows, making him stronger as a result, while Kashimoto elaborates that his Ice Flame had cooled the Minotaur's iron body, making it brittle and vulnerable. As the Minotaur attempts to divulge critical information about their true pursuers, Seiko pulls a talisman from her purse and destroys his form, cutting short the bull's final words.

The Minotaur crumbles down to reveal a salaryman who immediately begs for mercy. Seiko asks him the motive of his attack, to which he shows a message on his phone given to him by an orchestrator describing Seiko as the target and giving away her position. She runs towards the window and spots a mysterious person which Payase believes to be the one who was controlling the Jiangshi. Kashimoto demands the man to call his friend back but he explains how he has no idea about his identity since they all get contacted by the orchestrator and sometimes multiple people appear to bring down the same target. He gets mad and shows off his Aphoom-Zhah powers, so the scared man pulls out three knives, one being white and the other two blacks. Payase shockingly looks at Seiko who recognizes them as Kozuka Knives, which accompanied the powerful sword Asura, able to use the power of yokai and curses the wielder to kill others until his life runs out. It had been sealed by an organization of magi, however someone stole it five years ago. The man explains how their job is to gather the power of yokais and the ones who get the most will have their wishes come true. Payase threatens him for this nonsensical and dirty quest, but he sadly reveals that his wife has only one year left to live. Ever since he was young he had trouble talking to girls and he thought he was destined to live alone forever, until she showed up and patiently waited for him. Because of this, if there's a chance of saving her, even the most miniscule, he's going to take it. Seiko asks him about how he got contacted to which he says he got introduced to him by a colleague which could help his wife's situation. However, it appears that this colleague never existed since no one knew about him and he did not appear in the company register, despite him remembering the two worked for a long time together.

Masamichi Bega questions the worker about the clients inside the restaurant and he points out the middle-aged salaryman, though he recalls Seiko, Payase and Kashimoto paying their bill before leaving.

ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Skill Set

Master Hand-to-Hand Combatant: The Minotaur has proven to be a formidable close-combat fighter, having briefly beaten Seiko, a highly capable hand-to-hand combatant herself, in a one-on-one encounter. His fighting style emphasizes his remarkable durability, employing not just powerful punches and kicks but also leveraging his entire body weight. A particularly fighting stance he takes resembles a horse stance, with his muscular body hunched forward and his fist firmly extended (the left fist above his head, the right fist below), pointing directly at his opponent.[1]

Supernatural Abilities

Minotaur Form [v · e]
The man is able to take on the form of a large, muscular bipedal bull with eyes containing concentric circles, human hands, and a black metallic luster of iron skin. The only piece of clothing he wears are briefs.
Due his association with the orchestrator who is in possession of Asura knives, it can be implied that he acquired this power through them.
Minotaur's stance
Enhanced Strength
The Minotaur possesses incredible physical strength from the density of his iron body, being able to deliver powerful punches and kicks that were enough to put down a strong fighter like Seiko.
Enhanced Durability
Due to his body being made out of iron, the Minotaur possesses incredible durability. During his confrontation with Seiko, he was undeterred by her kick targeting his groin and did not even incur any harm from a strike with a piece of wood augmented by the Power of Words. Taking advantage of his body's density, the Minotaur could launch himself like a cannonball as an attack and put his whole weight on his opponent once he has got them down, all while receiving no consequences.
Strengths and Weaknesses
In addition to being impervious to harm, the Minotaur, owing to the nature of iron, experiences an increase in strength whenever his body is hit with considerable force, leading to the heating of the impacted area and the emission of steam. As a result, he has proven to be a difficult opponent to defeat, as his body gets stronger with each strike his opponent makes or with each strike he makes to his opponent. If not this, he also uses the tactic of striking himself.
ADVERTISEMENT

Equipment

Asura [v · e]
The Minotaur has in his possession at least three Asuras that were given to him by the Orchestrator for the purpose of gathering yokai powers.
Minotaur's Asura (Knife)
Capabilities
Power Absorption and Bestowal
Like its parent, the Asuras are capable of extracting powers from individuals, under the condition that the wielder's target admits defeat before being cut, and bestow the power onto themselves or someone else by cutting themselves.
Usage
The Minotaur attempted to use an Asura on Seiko after briefly putting her down in their fight.
Current Saga

[v · e · ?]
Kozuka Knives Arc
ADVERTISEMENT
Trivia

In line with the jiangshi being rooted to Chinese folklore, the Minotaur may be a reference to Ox-Head, one of the two wardens, alongside Horse-Face, who are positioned at the entrance to Diyu, the Chinese representation of Hell.
The Minotaur's tendency to shout "HOT, HOT!" regarding his groin is a reference to the gag used by Japanese comedian Takashi Fujii.
In Chapter 178, the Minotaur is erroneously depicted with human feet around the time he states his interest in acquiring Payase's power.[5]
