Peeny-Weeny (ぺニーチンコス, Penīchinkosu?), also referred to as Mr. Mantis Shrimp (シャコさん, Shako-san?) by Momo and Okarun, is a

Mr. Mantis Shrimp's Race
and a UMA known as the Dover Demon (ドーバーデーモン, Dōbādēmon?). In Dandadan, he was once a supporting antagonist during the Serpo Arc, having previously worked as a hired fighter for the Serpo in their mission to capture Okarun, in order to earn

Mr. Mantis Shrimp money
(money) for his son's blood transfusion. Since then, he has become a supporting character after Seiko helped in his son's recovery.

Appearance

As a

Mr. Mantis Shrimp's Race
, Mr. Mantis Shrimp possesses the disk-like head of a crab and a bipedal, muscular humanoid body with dull yellow skin. His eyes are shown to alternate between being crab-like to human-like on occasions. While wearing a variety of outfits throughout the series, he sticks to wearing boxing gloves. While in his human disguise, he resembles a middle aged man with a permanently affixed serious expression who wears a hat in the shape of his own head.

While working for the Serpo, Mr. Mantis Shrimp wore nothing but a speedo and a tie.
Gallery

Mr. Mantis Shrimp Anime Concept Art
Mr. Mantis Shrimp Anime Concept Art
Mr. Mantis Shrimp's human disguise.
Mr. Mantis Shrimp's human disguise.
A close up of Mr. Mantis Shrimp's face as a human.
A close up of Mr. Mantis Shrimp's face as a human.
Mr. Mantis Shrimp's outfit while working for the Serpo.
Mr. Mantis Shrimp's outfit while working for the Serpo.
Personality

Mr. Mantis Shrimp is a rather complex individual. When first met, he was an aggressive yet talkative combatant, regularly singing or boasting about his boosted strength, or sharing verbal exchanges with his opponents. He was also very deferential towards the Serpos who were his employers, frequently apologizing for his less than desirable performance.

Largely as a result of being a weak fighter by his species' standards, Peeny-Weeny has lived a life full of hardships. His wife passed away from a congenital illness, which she also passed on to their son, Chiquitita. Because Chiquitita requires regular blood transfusions due to his illness, Mr. Mantis Shrimp takes on dangerous jobs to fund them. His relative weakness saw him spurned by his people and ridiculed by his employers which upsets him greatly. As such, when the Family attended to his injuries, provided him with a meal to aid in his recovery, and offered a cow for his son's blood transfusion, Mr. Mantis Shrimp was overwhelmed with emotion and vowed to aid them however he could.

While willing to engage in fights for a just cause, Mr. Mantis Shrimp claims to be a pacifist, having refused to teach Okarun how to throw a proper punch because he believes that violence is wrong. However, he admits that he is liable to retaliate if his patience is tested, such as when he is behind the wheel and his passengers complain about his poor driving skills.

He also has the strange habit of saying "deisu" (でいス) after every sentence.
Background

On his home planet, Peeny-Weeny was married and had a child. After his wife eventually died of an illness, Peeny-Weeny desperately needed to earn money for his son's blood transfusion after he attracted the same illness as his mother. Since he was a weak member of his race, Peeny-Weeny had no choice but to engage in dangerous work, which led him to become a subordinate of the Serpo.
Synopsis

Serpo Arc

Aira dodges Dover Demon
The Dover Demon fights Aira.
The Dover Demon, along with Nessie, accompanies the Serpo on their mission to capture Okarun at his school to acquire his supernatural powers. After confronting him, the Dover Demon and the Serpo find themselves dealing with Aira Shiratori, a girl who also has supernatural powers. The Dover Demon fights against Aira but is unable to land a single hit on her due to her enhanced agility and is kicked up into the ceiling where his head becomes stuck. However, after the Serpo use their psychokinesis to suppress her powers, the Dover Demon sends Aira crashing back with a strong punch. He then assaults a restrained Takakaura after he tried to protect Aira, but is sent flying back after Okarun launches himself into his chest, which was made possible after Momo arrives and counteracts the Serpo's psychic powers with her own.

After he is exhausted by Okarun's attack, the Serpo forcibly enhance the Dover Demon so that he may continue fighting (in spite of his objections to being enhanced). Now rejuvenated, the Dover Demon throws a barrage of shockwave punches at Okarun and Aira while they are bound by the Serpo's psychokinesis. However, Momo counters the aliens' powers once more and allows Okarun and Aira to fight back. The Dover Demon manages to hold his own against Aira, since she could not see his attacks coming, but is soon overwhelmed after Okarun helps Aira dodge the Dover Demon's punches since he is able to see them clearly. The conflict between the two sides is interrupted after the water beneath their feet starts to rise from Nessie's sudden arrival.

Serpo Dover Demon Nessie Infobox (Anime)
The Dover Demon after being forcefully fused with a Serpo and Nessie.
As Momo, Okarun, and Aira try to escape after Nessie starts to attack the Serpo, the Dover Demon throws an underwater shockwave punch that sends Aira up into the watery ceiling and continues his assault on Okarun and Momo. However, after being underwater for too long, the Dover Demon quickly swims up to get some air and swims back down to throw more of his strengthen shockwaves punches at Okarun and Momo. He is surprised by Momo's strategy to save Aira from drowning in which she propels Okarun forward with her psychic powers while riding on his back. After commenting on the cleverness of their escape, the Dover Demon turns around to see a Serpo floating in the water and ask for more time in defeating the humans. He is spooked when the head tips over, revealing itself to be severed. Seeing as how the situation has gotten worse with Nessie out of control, a surviving Serpo swims towards the Dover Demon to fuse himself with both creatures.

After the Serpo Dover Demon Nessie is defeated by Okarun, the Dover Demon somehow manages to survive and goes after his enemies for the sake of earning money for his family. He encounters Momo and Aira outside the school and attempts to attack them. However, weakened and bleeding heavily, the Dover Demon falls unconscious in front of them before he can attack. Momo, Aira, and Okarun then decide to take the Dover Demon to Momo's house to help him recover.

Episode 10-4
The Dover Demon expressing his gratitude to the people who helped him.
After waking up from a dream he had about him and his child, the Dover Demon finds himself bandaged up and looked after by Momo, Okarun, Aira, and Seiko. He leaps up and assumes a fighting stance before noticing a plate of curry at his feet, which Momo says they made for him in spite of not knowing what aliens typically eat. Seeing as how it was the first time in his life that he was treated kindly, the Dover Demon becomes emotional and promises that he will no longer try to harm them. After finish having dinner with the group, the Dover Demon tells them about his predicament with not being able to earn enough money to pay for his sick son's constant blood transfusions. Okarun tells the Dover Demon that he is willing to help by offering his genitals but is turned down since the alien did want to cause him and the others any problems as promised. Before showing himself out, Seiko stops him and tells the Dover Demon that she might be able to help after noticing how his blood gave off a familiar scent. After drinking a carton of milk given to him, the Dover Demon notices how the milk is the same as his race's blood. This prompts Seiko to offer the Dover Demon a cow from a dairy farmer she knows to help with his son's blood transfusion. With the cow acquired on his spacecraft, the Dover Demon thanks the humans for their help and tells them that he will never forget the debt he owes them before blasting off into outer space.

At some point, the Dover Demon finds that the cow was not producing any milk and realized that milking the animal would be a problem on his home world due to the planet being filled with a water-like substance, leading to him making the decision to take his son and live on Earth to supply him with a constant intake of milk.

Cursed House Arc

The Dover Demon assists Seiko in helping her meet up with Momo, Okarun, and Jiji using his spaceship and fights the Evil Eye alongside her by the time they arrive. He then guides Chiquitita in using the Tsuchinoko to put out the forest fire as he takes control of the spaceship and helps Momo save Okarun from being stuck down the Tsuchinoko pit.

At the Ayase residence, the Dover Demon and Chiquitita join the others for dinner and informs them of his decision to live with his son on Earth as a farmer. As he prepares to leave, the Dover Demon tells Momo that she is welcomed to call him again if they run into any problems and lets her know that his real name is "Peeny-Weeny" after she asks what it is, only for the girl and her friends to nickname him "Mr. Mantis Shrimp" as a more fitting title.

Evil Eye Arc

While working, Mr. Mantis Shrimp is visited by Okarun for lessons on how to throw a punch but turns him down since he believes violence is wrong.

After learning from Okarun that the Ayase house has been destroyed, Mr. Mantis Shrimp and his son help to repair it by contacting Ludris to acquire his nanoskin, successfully creating an exact replica.

Kaiju Arc

Mr. Mantis Shrimp is visited by Okarun, Jiji, and Kinta for help translating the language of an alien girl named Bamora. He gives them his translator device but sees that it is only able to pick up a few of her words and offers to adjust them when they come back.

Space Globalists Arc

Mr. Mantis Shrimp arrives to save a badly injured Okarun from being captured by a group of suited aliens and takes him, along with one of the aliens Okarun defeated, to the Ayase residence to help him recover. He also does the same for Aira and Jiji after coming across them badly wounded in Kamigoe City. The next day, Mr. Mantis Shrimp becomes relieved to see Momo returning home safe, informs her of Okarun's condition, and watches as she forces Bamora to leave her house since she found out that she is connected to the group of aliens who attacked her and her friends. Shortly after, Mr. Mantis Shrimp treats Momo's wounds as she talks with Aira and Jiji after they had woken up. After Okarun slightly regains conscious from hearing Momo and Jiji arguing, he disconnects his life support long enough to ask that they stop fighting, though Mr. Mantis Shrimp is quick to reattach Okarun's life support once he notices that it's been removed. While doing this, he explains to Momo and Jiji that Okarun cannot rest if his friends fight. Mr. Mantis Shrimp, Aira, and Jiji are then taken outside by Momo to see the Serpo she brought along with her, as the alien and her group now have a common enemy. Hearing the Serpo's speculation of how the alien group will invade Earth in less than five days, Momo decides that their next course of action is to train to prevent this from happening. Using the nanoskin the Ayase house is constructed out of, Mr. Mantis Shrimp helps to rebuild it into a vehicle to have the group relocate to a Serpo hideout. Mr. Mantis Shrimp takes the wheel but becomes displeased when Momo, Aira, and Jiji complain about his reckless driving as he transports them to the hideout.

After arriving and checking the hideout for traps, Mr. Mantis Shrimp trains with the others but performs poorly according to Aira who angrily informs him, Momo, and Jiji of their faults. He then uses the Ayase house to drive back home to Chiquitita. The next day, Mr. Mantis Shrimp returns to the site and wakes up Momo and Jiji to continue with the training. Later, Mr. Mantis Shrimp trains with Aira in a sparring match while Momo and Jiji practice combining their powers.

After finishing their training, Mr. Mantis Shrimp drives the group to the Empty Space where the Kur are summoning their main force, and upon arriving, they are attacked by the Takonoka Ru Patcho, Ta Komeshi, Suda Ko, Ta Kowasa, and Mantis Exosuit Kur. Momo goes ahead of them to close the warp gate. Meanwhile, Mr. Mantis Shrimp, Aira, and Jiji choose to stay behind and fight off the four Kur in their way. Mr. Mantis Shrimp faces the Mantis Exosuit Kur and attacks the Ta Kowasa Kur to free Aira from his restraints. Following Aira's league, Mr. Mantis Shrimp continues to face the Mantis Exosuit Kur but is overwhelmed by his laser blades viciously cutting his body and lies on the ground defeated, soon joined by the defeated Aira and Jiji. During this moment, the three view Bamora's memories through their Serpo communicators after Momo uses attempts to use her powers to close a fatal wound inflicted on Bamora.

Though he manages to get back on his feet, Mr. Mantis Shrimp continues to lose ground to the Mantis Exosuit Kur. He then resorts to entering the river behind him to fight in his natural environment and tells his opponent that, despite not being a lifeform of the planet he is on, he is willing to put his life on the line for the people he owes a debt to. In response, the Mantis Exosuit Kur has his exosuit enter its underwater form and once again gains the advantageous, overwhelming Mr. Mantis Shrimp with his high-speed swimming and strong blows before injecting him with a powerful venom. However, with the exosuit alien close to him as he keeps him bound to a wall, Mr. Mantis Shrimp manages to land a punch on the Kur to damage his exosuit. While the Kur reels, Mr. Mantis Shrimp momentarily shapeshifts into his Dover Demon Strong Style Twenty-Four form to deliver a Jet Punch that completely destroys the Kur's exosuit. He then quickly swims out of the water to catch his breath, notes his species' resilience to venom, and walks back to where Aira and Jiji are, with the Mantis exosuit exploding out of the water behind him as he goes.

Mr. Mantis Shrimp, Aira, and the Evil Eye reunite with Momo, who is with Okarun and Bamora, and fight together against the Kur that have passed through the warp gate. Mr. Mantis Shrimp follows Aira's orders to guard Momo as she and Okarun make their way to the warp gate to close it and are successful. However, after the remain ships of the Kur's main force managed to slip through the gate just in time, Mr. Mantis Shrimp is ordered by Momo to assist Aira in battle as she and Okarun attempt to stop the fleet. After the invasion ends with Reiko Kashima trapping and eliminating the Kur inside her mirror, Mr. Mantis Shrimp drives the Ayase house to pick up Momo and Okarun and leave the city with the rest of the group.

At some point, Mr. Mantis Shrimp brings Chiquitita to the Ayase house as the group are served dinner by Seiko.

Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Physical Prowess

Immense Strength: Mr. Mantis Shrimp has tremendous amount of physical strength, being able to throw powerful punches that are capable of breaking through walls. By his own admission, he's considered a weak fighter by his species' standards.

Skill Set

Boxing: Mr. Mantis Shrimp is a formidable hand-to-hand combatant who uses the style of boxing against his opponents.

Techniques

Jet Punch
Jet Punch.
Jet Punch (ジェットパンチ, Jetto Panchi?): Mr. Mantis Shrimp puts all his strength into throwing a powerful punch that sends his opponent crashing back. This technique was first used against Aira. However, she managed to dodge the technique in time. The force of the punch after striking a wall was shown being carried forward, knocking back anything in its path.

Forms

Dover Demon Strong Style Twenty-Four
(ドーバーデーモンストロングスタイル24, Dōbādēmon Suto Rongu Sutairu 24?) [v · e]
Mr. Mantis Shrimp is able to assume his race's empowered transformation. In this form, his head resembles that of a mantis shrimp, with green, glowing eyes. A second pair of wide eyes, along with antennae extending, act as the top part of his head, which flashes in response to him speaking. Around the neck is a segmented, collar-like structure. His hands change into a mantis shrimp's raptorial appendage with concentric rings of green, red, and orange that are able to open and act as shields. His feet are broad and flat, resembling flippers or the feet of an aquatic creature.
Ironically, despite the change in appearance to resemble the crustacean, along with his strength being more powerful in the environment, this form doesn't offer Mr. Mantis Shrimp gills to allow him to breath underwater. Consequently, he must come up for air at times to prevent himself from drowning. He is also limited to staying in this form for 24 seconds, however, with a special drug, such as a Serpo Energy Drink, his time can be extended to at least 24 hours.
Mantis Shrimp Alien Form (Anime)
Augmented Strength
Mantis Shrimp Alien's strength
This form greatly enhances Mr. Mantis Shrimp's already incredible physical strength.
Strengths and Weaknesses
Mantis Shrimp Alien's underwater strength
The enhanced physical strength Mr. Mantis Shrimp gains in this form increases his punching power and speed to where he is able to generate shockwaves with each thrust. In addition to this allowing him to fight at a distance, these delivered shockwaves proof to be too difficult for his opponents to evade unless they possess extraordinary speed and reflexes. Corresponding to its mantis shrimp likeness, the enhanced strength provided by the Dover Demon Strong Style Twenty-Four form significantly increases for Mr. Mantis Shrimp when he is submerged underwater, with Mr. Mantis Shrimp asserting that his strength multiplies by tenfold.
Usage
In this form, both land and underwater, Mr. Mantis Shrimp transitions his fighting style from close quarters to mid-range by emitting a barrage of powerful shockwaves from his punches towards his opponent.
Techniques
Salary Uppercut
(たいぐアパカツ, Taigu Apakatsu?)

Mr. Mantis Shrimp delivers a swift and strong uppercut that sends his opponent upwards. This technique was first used against Aira, causing her to be temporarily stuck in a ceiling.
Jet Punch
(ジェットパンチ, Jetto Panchi?)
Mr. Mantis Shrimp defeats the Mantis Exosuit Kur
When in his Dover Demon Strong Style Twenty-Four form while submerged underwater, Mr. Mantis Shrimp can use an enhanced version of his Jet Punch. It was first used against the Mantis Exosuit Kur, destroying the alien's exosuit and killing him in the process.

Muko (ムーコ, Mūko?) is a recurring character of the Dandadan series. Along with Miko, she is the best friend and classmate of Momo Ayase at high school.

Appearance

Muko is a young girl with brown skin, brown eyes, and blonde hair styled into pigtails. She is typically depicted in her school uniform, which consists of a white undershirt beneath a long-sleeved sweater adorned with a loose bow, paired with a navy skirt, loose socks, and sandals.

In her introduction, Muko was shown wearing light colored makeup (particularly gyaru makeup of the sub-style known as "Manba"). In addition, she is shown to have bright-blue eyes.
Personality

Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Turbo Granny Arc

Muko and Miko learn from Momo about her distressing breakup with her boyfriend. Muko comments on the humor she found in Momo hurling seafood-themed insults at her boyfriend during their breakup and reminds Momo that she had advised against getting involved with him. She and Miko then become unimpressed with Momo upon learning that her reason for dating her boyfriend was simply because he bore a resemblance to her ideal man, Ken Takakura, remarking that such men are purely fictional. Later on, the pair discovers Momo engaging with a male student in the hallway, leading Kei to remark that Momo seems to have abandoned her search for Ken Takakura in favor of a geeky type of guy.

Acrobatic Silky

During class, Muko and Miko notice Momo daydreaming and speculates that she might have reunited with her ex-boyfriend since she lost her phone and was absent from school yesterday. After lunch, Muko and Miko catch Momo accidently locking lips with Okarun after they accidently bump into each other. The pair then assume that Momo is romantically involved with Okarun and observe them exchanging insults as they attempt to refute the allegation. Despite this, Muko and Miko still become convinced that the two like each other.

Shortly after, Muko and Miko gossip to their female classmates about Momo and Okarun, leading the girls becoming eager to know more from Momo. When Okarun later arrives at their classroom to talk to Momo, the girls quickly cheer him on, with Momo angrily turning him down. After Okarun leaves dejected, Muko points out to Momo her behaviour towards him was out-of-character, leading Momo to reflect.

Naki Kito (鬼き頭とうナキ, Kitō Naki?) is a subterranean who spent over 200 years offering human sacrifices to the Tsuchinoko in order to prevent her village's destruction.

In Dandadan, Naki serves as one of the primary antagonists during the Cursed House Arc, reemerged in the Current Saga during the Kozuka Knives Arc as a major antagonist.

While disguised as a human, Naki appears as a short elderly woman with a large perm and a unibrow. As for attire, she wears a stripe long-sleeve, buttoned shirt, with a large pearl necklace, and harem pants with a flower shape pattern.

As a subterranean, Naki has a wide head with side plating, eyes that have concentric circles and a cross, a long-puckered mouth with dark line markings, and long horns that curve on opposite sides. She has a spring hose body and abnormal feet with toes that resemble fingers.
Gallery

Personality

Naki is devoted to protecting the Kito Family's home village from the Tsuchinoko, being willingly to offer human sacrifices to the Tsuchinoko for 200 years to prevent it from causing the village volcano from erupting. At the same time, she and her family worship the Tsuchinoko, possibly because they believed that it blessed the village with hot springs for appeasing its hunger. Upon being sent to its lair, she conveyed to the creature that it was an honor to be in its presence, as the Kito Family offered Momo, Okarun, and Jiji as the next sacrifices. She found it disgraceful that Momo was using the Tsuchinoko's body as a makeshift hose to cool the lava, even after the enormous worm had previously swallowed her. After the Kito Family were arrested, it was revealed that her allegiance leaned more towards the Tsuchinoko than the protection of the village, as she became frustrated that her 200-year plan to feed the Tsuchinoko until it was big enough was ruined by Momo.

Naki is shown to be very prideful and arrogant, proclaiming that the village is the land of the Kito Family, given the many years they secretly kept it safe, and those who live in it should be grateful to them; especially of the fact that their offerings resulted in the village having hot springs. She also pointed out to Jiji that he would have ended up on the streets if not for her "warmheartedness" allowing him to continue living in his house rent free. Naki's pride as a self-proclaimed protector also could not allow Momo to make a successful attempt at saving the village from the active volcano, believing that an outsider should not dare to take over the Kito Family's role.
ADVERTISEMENT

Background

During the feudal period, Naki led her family into offering village children to a Mongolian Death Worm they praised as the Tsuchinoko in order to prevent the volcano the worm resided in from becoming active and destroying their village. As this ritual continued up to the modern era, the Kito Family constructed a sacrificial house to lure in families, which would lead to the birth of the Evil Eye.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Cursed House Arc

Naki and her relatives spot Jiji, the son of the hospitalized Enjoji Family who are the currently renters of the sacrificial house, inviting over Momo and Okarun to his home. While the male relatives confront Momo after she leaves for the hot springs, Naki and her female relatives invite themselves in to find out from Jiji as to why he recently left without a word and are told that he left to invite Okarun. Naki then questions him on whether he was planning on hiring more spirit mediums as he did before when he suspected that the house was haunted and becomes seemingly hostile after presenting her gun to inform him that she has a hunting license. Upon the male relatives return, Naki asks Jiji when the girl he brought with him would come back and hears him feigning ignorance, resulting in her pointing out that he was lying to her and having her family attack Jiji and Okarun in retaliation.

After Momo returns to the house to find Okarun and Jiji lying on the flying severely beaten, the Kito Family launch an attack on the girl, with Naki sending Momo to the sacrificial room with a strong blow. Naki then lets Momo in on who the Kito Family are and prevents her from escaping the sacrificial room as the floor starts to have her sink down to the Tsuchinoko's lair. However, Naki and the other family members are sent down to the Tsuchinoko's lair as well after Okarun and Jiji regain conscious to push them into the room. After the Tsuchinoko shows itself, Naki and the other family members present themselves as worshippers to inform the Tsuchinoko that they are not the sacrifices, only to end up being swallowed by the Tsuchinoko regardless.

Later, Naki and the other family members are vomited out of the Tsuchinoko's body after Momo manages to kill it. Having killed the Tsuchinoko, Naki starts to blame Momo since the worm's death resulted in the village volcano becoming active. After quoting the village legend leads to Momo using the Tsuchinoko's corpse as a hose to cool down the magma, the Kito Family try to stop her from disrespecting the creature, as well as not wanting her to take credit for protecting the village. The Kito Family are then attacked by Manjiro who has come to defend Momo, as per his master's past phone call instructions to look after her and her friends, and the Evil Eye who has taken over Jiji's body. Naki's right arm is then broken after she tries to block an attack from the Evil Eye and is pulled by Momo from taking on another blow as she did not want the yokai have Jiji responsible for killing anyone. With the Evil Eye targeting both Naki, Momo, and Manjiro, the three go on the defensives and fight alongside each other.

After the events, the Kito Family are arrested after their crimes were finally made known to the authorities. However, Naki manages to hide from her search party and takes off her human disguise in anger, having become furious with Momo for ruining her 200-year plan to grow the Tsuchinoko and declares vengeance on her on behalf of the subterraneans.[1]

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

After three of the detained Kito family members were freed while they were being transported, Naki and her family catch on Momo's scent from the jacket she abandoned during their battle in Daija Town and they slip through the security of the airport where she's currently inside by covering themselves up. Despite the progression of the curse making everybody forget about Momo other than Jiji, the subterraneans still remember her, although they don't see her because of her small size. Naki and her family then happily embark the plane where they'll perform their revenge.

On the plane she secretly gives permission to her four sons to attack the group, leading Bamora to activate Empty Space to avoid civilians getting hurt. They immediately inform Naki who admits that even though she knew they weren't ordinary people, she did not expect them to side with the aliens. As she says this, she removes her disguise and assumes a fighting stance, ready to brawl.

ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Physical Prowess

Jennifer Lopez Anaconda
Naki sending Momo crashing through two walls.
Enhanced Strength: Naki possesses incredibly physical strength, as shown when she sent Momo crashing back through two walls with a pair of simultaneous punches.[2]

Enhanced Speed & Reflexes: Naki demonstrated to be swift and agile, managing to react and evade a television that Momo had hurled towards her from behind.[3]

Enhanced Stamina & Endurance: Naki demonstrated a remarkable tolerance for pain, showing no signs of distress or suffering when the Evil Eye fractured her right arm and proceeded to combat him as though it had no effect on her.[4]

Skill Set

Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Naki favors close-quarters combat, utilizing her powerful punches, kicks, and quick reflexes to overpower her opponents.[2]

Jennifer Lopez Anaconda (ジェニファロペス穴ア根ナコ打ンダ, Jenifāropesu Anakonda?): Naki delivers a double punch to her opponent that is strong enough to send them flying back. She can also perform this attack with one hand. This technique was first used against Momo.[2]

Nessie (ネッシー, Nesshī?), or Kamissie (カミッシー, Kamisshī?) by Okarun since the creature had previously arrived in Kamigoe City, was a cryptid and a disgruntled subordinate of the Serpos.

In Dandadan, it serves as a supporting antagonist during the Serpo Arc.

Appearance

Nessie was a large, roughly 3.5 metre long aquatic reptilian creature resembling a plesiosaur, with a long neck, stout body, long tail and 4 powerful flippers used for swimming. Its reptilian head had numerous ridges and bumps, and it eyes were small and white, with black, piercing pupils. Inside its jaw, it had numerous, jagged teeth and a tongue that was somewhat forked at the tip. The mouth could open rather wide in order to shoot its devastating attack. Its body was patterned and had numerous lines and stripes with a ridge running along its back. Alongside the flanks of the creature, 2 pairs of extremely long gills ran the entire length of its body from directly behind its head all the way to the tail.
Personality

Nessie was animalistic and aggressive, as it attacked anything it came across or sense was nearby. Despite being a subordinate of the Serpos, Nessie did not have the intelligence to follow orders, let alone understand them, and were included in Nessie's rampage.
Background

Ever since 700 AD, the creature had been sighted on multiple accounts but made itself truly known in 1934 at Loch Ness, Scotland after an obstetrician from London captured a photo of it. The creature then went on to become famously known as the Loch Ness Monster (ネス湖の怪獣, Nesu-ko no Kaijū?). While the picture that would then become known as the "surgeon's photograph" exposed the creature's existence, many had doubted its authenticity and believed that it was a hoax.[1] Afterwards, numerous theories have been put down to try to identify what Nessie could actually be, with theories that it could be a massive eel.
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Serpo Arc

Setting their sights on Okarun for his Turbo Granny powers, the aliens brought along Nessie and the hired Dover Demon to capture him at his school. While roaming the halls alone, Nessie becomes spotted by Momo who immediately tries hiding from it. However, after accidently making a sound, Nessie closes in and fires a high-compression water blast that destroys a classroom. It then made its leave but became unaware that the blast missed Momo.

Later, after the Serpos confronts Okarun, Aira, and Momo, Nessie makes its arrival and interrupts the fight by flooding the area and attacking the Serpos. Seeing as how Nessie was uncontrollable, a surviving Serpo makes the decision to merge himself with both Nessie and the Dover Demon to create the Serpo Dover Demon Nessie as a last resort to eliminate Okarun, Aira, and Momo. However, the alien's plan fails after Okarun destroys the creature's body, resulting in Nessie being killed in the process.

The Orchestrator (指示役, Shijiyaku?) is an unknown individual intent on acquiring the abilities of Power Users, including Momo and Seiko Ayase, by enticing individuals with a promise to grant them a wish of their desire if they manage to succeed in doing their bidding.

In Dandadan, they serve as an overarching antagonist during the Kozuka Knives Arc.

Appearance

Orchestrator's Body Double
The orchestrator's body double.
The orchestrator's appearance has yet to be revealed and has only been shown as a silhouette so far.

Using the Fairy-Tale Card's mind control power, the orchestrator employed a man as their body double to confront Adachi. The man had short, dark hair and featureless eyes, a result of the mind control's influence. He was dressed in a long, dark overcoat over a collared shirt, complemented by a dark tie, pants, and shoes. Additionally, he carried a briefcase, which was used to assault Adachi.

Background

Not much of the orchestrator's life has been revealed other than at some point in time they became aware of Momo Ayase and her grandmother Seiko Ayase possessing powers. They then devised an underground pyramid-like scheme in which individuals would be granted a wish upon successfully obtaining abilities from targets selected directly by them and sent out through anonymous group chats. This included providing participants with various kozuka knives crafted from the cursed sword Asura to steal the powers and giving them powers from the aforementioned knives to aid them in their mission. Among these participants were Takeshi Murakami, a teacher at Kami High who blackmailed female student Kouki Yukishiro to do his bidding, a man seeking to use the orchestrator's reward to heal his wife, and Mika Adachi, another teacher at Kami High who wishes to continue providing financial support for her mother.
Synopsis

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

After tracking Seiko down at Juicy Gyoza Manufactory Dandadan, the orchestrator instructed Adachi and the Minotaur to target her at the restaurant.[1] Later, the orchestrator engaged in telepathic communication with the student Hase, urging him to seize Okarun's unique power on their behalf using two Asura kozuka knives: the white kozuka, which held the power of Jumping Crone for Hase to obtain, and the black kozuka, intended for the purpose of stealing the power.[2] The orchestrator soon receives a text message from Adachi that the mission ended in failure due to the spirit medium having backup.[3]

Upon learning from Adachi that she has acquired Murakami's abilities, the orchestrator employs the mind control power of the Fairy-Tale Card to manipulate a man into acting as their body double and instructs Adachi to meet him at the embankment beneath the overpass where they could initiate the transfer. When Adachi arrives, the orchestrator contacts her via phone, praising her efforts. However, they reveal that Murakami was one of their operatives and that her reckless pursuit of an unspecified target, along with the credit for Murakami's defeat attributed to Kouki's Lord of the Flies power, has resulted in her disqualification. The orchestrator then demands that Adachi transfer her kozuka knife and her powers to the man. Despite Adachi's pleas for another opportunity, the orchestrator explains that her lack of resolve, stemming from her compassionate nature, prevents her from defeating and acquiring power from ID Cosmo-type targets. As Adachi continues to resist, the orchestrator controls the man to attack her and force her to relinquish her power. At that moment, Bega intervenes, kicking the man away from Adachi, calls for reinforcements, and confronts him. The orchestrator attempts to exert the Fairy-Tale Card's mind control over Bega, only to discover that it has no effect on the officer, much to their frustration. They then redirect their control to Adachi, having her attack Bega as a diversion for their escape.[4]

Abilities and Powers

Supernatural Abilities

Fairy-Tale Card
(メルへンカルタ, Meruhen Karuta?) [v · e]
The orchestrator possesses the yokai power of the Fairy-Tale Card, particularly his power to corrupt the minds of humans to take control of them.
Orchestrator using Fairy-Tale Card
Strengths and Weaknesses
The primary advantage of this ability lies in the orchestrator's capacity to manipulate their victims' bodies involuntarily, which has the effect of compelling them to confront their deepest traumas in a bid to shatter their mental resilience. Presumably, they are also able to use this power's additional effect of unlocking the victim's full potential; however, this comes at a grave cost, as the victim may ultimately perish due to the continuous strain on their body. Furthermore, there is no restriction on the number of individuals the orchestrator can control simultaneously.

The effectiveness of the Fairy-Tale Card relies on its targets establishing eye contact; if the individual closes their eyes, they will not be influenced. Furthermore, the power does not affect yokai. Interestingly, Masamichi Bega is the sole individual known to be immune to the mind control.
Usage
The orchestrator used the Fairy-Tale Card's power to take control of a man as their body double to meet with Adachi and take back the lent Asura kozuka knife and her power. They later attempted to do the same for Bega after he appeared to help Adachi, only to fail after the officer revealed his immunity. This then led to them redirecting their efforts towards controlling Adachi and inciting her to attack Bega, thereby creating a diversion for the controlled man to escape.

Payase is a man with short, side-parted hair and incredibly dark eye bags. His attire consists of a pale hoodie that's concealed by a dark jacket with pockets located on his biceps, as well as a pale pair of pants. Much like his partner, he also wears a logo consisting of a multi-ringed eye, albeit his doesn't have the triangle background. Due to his curse-collecting hobby, those with the ability to detect auras would notice that his is practically black.
Personality

Payase is an emotional and expressive young man who has a deep fixation for cursed objects. Regardless of the misfortune they bring onto the claimer, he is willingly to acquire them, believing that due to his fixation with them he would be immune to their more negative effects, and calls them "cute".
Synopsis

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

After recently acquiring a cursed painting that causes fires to erupt in his home, Payase, together with Kashimoto, is contacted by Seiko Ayase to convene with her at a restaurant. There, he shares with her about his recent purchase and is asked by Seiko to look after the Fairy-Tale Card's cursed trunk, which he gladly accepts. Just as Kashimoto relays his information on the Uchide-no-kozuchi and where she should go to acquire it, Payase gets knocked back by Kashimoto after a jiangshi kicks him away.[1]

Using their powers, Payase and Kashimoto punch the Minotaur and the horde of jiangshi away from the injured Seiko and prepare to fight the enemies confronting them.[2] Seeing Seiko back on her feet after enduring injuries inflicted by the Minotaur, Payase asks if she is okay. In response, Seiko likens her ordeal to that of the most excruciating osteopathy clinic imaginable, a remark that strikes a chord with Kashimoto while leaving Payase perplexed. After being informed by Seiko that the Minotaur's body is made of iron, and his strength increases every time he is hit, Payase and Kashimoto are instructed by her to handle fighting the Minotaur while she goes to retrieve her bag. While attacks with Aphoom-Zhah, Payase covers Seiko by using his shadow power to disintegrate the jiangshi. This catches the Minotaur's interest in having the power for himself, much to Payase's disapproval. Payase makes an attempt to disintegrate the Minotaur but fails after his shadow spike fails to pierce through his groin, which leaves him open for the Minotaur to grab him out of his shadow and throw him aside. Kashimoto then tries his hand at attacking the Minotaur. Payase believes that his attacks are working but is caution by Seiko to keep his guard. After the Minotaur punches Kashimoto to a wall, Payase expresses worry for his partner's well-being but continues to follow Seiko's orders to focus on covering her from the jiangshi as she reaches for her purse. When the Minotaur kicks Seiko away from her purse and punches Kashimoto after he comes in to attack with Aphoom-Zhah, Payase, as a shadow, throws Seiko's purse her way before the Minotaur strikes him. Thanks to the series of freezing blows delivered by Kashimoto and the light shining from the Minotaur, which darkens his shadow, the Minotaur's iron muscles become sufficiently fragile for Payase to break the creature's arms while hidden in shadow. The Minotaur inquiries about the reason for this occurrence, to which Payase elucidates the relationship between shadow and light. The confrontation then concludes with Seiko affixing a talisman to the Minotaur's head and subsequently delivering a decisive kick that obliterates his head.[3]

ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Powers

Supernatural Abilities

Darkness Form [v · e]
Payase possesses the power to envelope himself in a cloak of darkness. As a result, his form changes into a dark humanoid figure; having a head with horns, a beak mouth, featureless slit eyes, elongated limbs with three talons for his hands and feet, and a slightly hunched back with a small trail of darkness leaking out.
Payase in his cursed form
Shadow Manipulation
Payase manipulating shadows
In his Darkness form, Payase is capable of manipulating his shadow across a surface.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The primary strength of Payase's shadow manipulation is that it enables him to disperse his enemies. He accomplishes this by extending his shadow to intertwine with the shadow of his target and creating a spike that pierces them from their groin to their head. Payase refers to this as "sweeping the darkness". In addition, Payase can enter his own shadow, allowing him to move swiftly around any surfaces and make surprise attacks.

Though he can enter his shadow, Payase remains tangible if a part of his Darkness form extends out from his shadow. If a part of his body is caught while he is mostly within his shadow, Payase risks being dragged out by his opponent and left vulnerable to attack. While Payase's shadow spike can penetrate flesh, it has proven ineffectiveness against harden materials, such as iron. Payase can also be forcibly stripped out of his Darkness cloak, though he shows no problem in reforming it.
Usage
Payase uses the dispersing power of his shadow to eliminate his opponents on the spot, all while merged with his shadow to easily move around his surroundings.
Enhanced Strength
Payase and Kashimoto counterattack
Payase's Darkness form grants him an increase in strength, allowing him to knock back an iron body Minotaur without hurting himself as a consequence. As a shadow in his Darkness form, Payase's strength further increases when exposed to intense light, following the principle that shadows deepen in darkness with increased illumination.

Queen (女じょ王おう, Joō?) is the school nurse of Kami High.

Appearance

Queen full appearance (Anime)
Queen's full appearance.
Queen is a woman with shoulder-length black hair, with a bang that covers the right side of her face, blue eyes, and a beauty mark located under the left side of her mouth. She also wears lipstick and an earring on her left ear. As for her attire, she wears a nurse's cap, a single buttoned-up collar, a loose lab coat that exposes her shoulders, her school I.D. around her neck, and white thigh high boots (black in the anime).

Personality

Queen has a very strict attitude when it comes to the students at Kami High. She possesses zero tolerance for any acts of bullying from any student, viewing those who do as cowards, and is not above reprimanding them physically to address such behavior. Additionally, what she despises most of all are delinquent students who try to play the victim card, which results in her losing her temper. Despite this, Queen has proven herself to be a rational individual, assessing the sensibility of each side of the story before passing judgement, and is empathetic, attentively listening to her students' concerns, whether they relate to insecurities, anxieties, or even spiritual matters. She also has a tendency addressing people as "baldie".
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Serpo Arc

After Momo, Okarun, and Aira are seen in their underwear by the other students out in the halls earlier, Queen questions them about the incident on whether this was an act of bullying. She then receives a message from a colleague, who she berates for not knocking first before entering, about a phone call for her in the staff room and leaves the three students alone to answer.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

Queen slaps Kouki Yukishiro
Queen reprimands Kouki for her misdeeds.
After being sent to Empty Space, Queen observes from outside her office as Kouki is pursued by Kinta on his nanoskin hoverboard. She intervenes with her baton, striking him down under the impression that he, Jiji, and Bamora are bullying her.[1] Queen takes Kouki word in that the members of the History and Culture Research Club assaulted her together and demands for the culprit who hurt her to present themselves. Jiji and Bamora counters Kouki's claim, telling Queen that Kouki was the one who assaulted Momo. While Kouki denies these allegations, Queen examines her injuries and highlights the inconsistencies between her current explanation and her earlier assertion of not knowing Jiji and being outnumbered, despite having the support of the pygmies she is clearly able to see. Queen explains to Kouki that through her student's consulting with her on spiritualism she has come to see spirits and promises not to judge her until she confesses the truth. Touched by Queen's words, Kouki confesses to attacking Momo and offers an apology. Angry with her for pretending to be the victim, Queen becomes prompted to slap Kouki and is held back by Jiji and Bamore from assaulting her any further.[2]

Later, Queen and the History and Culture Research Club listen to Kouki's story about how she had been coerced by a teacher to steal Momo's power in order to keep social media account a secret.[3] She's reminded of a student who admitted he could see a tiny old man and she investigated its existence, finding out that the pygmies were originally people who were emarginated and driven off the surface. They quietly disappeared but their will to be known still remains strong, leading them to gather around a person who can see them and help them in any way they can. She points out how they apparently bring good luck and says that the student she mentioned is still looking for these little old men.

Abilities and Powers

Supernatural Abilities

Spiritual Awareness [v · e]
Queen awakened the ability to see spirits after attending exorcisms and visiting various ominous locations with her students, who sought her guidance on spiritual matters. This also makes her one of the rare few who are able to enter Empty Space.
Equipment

Baton [v · e]
Queen wields a baton as a weapon, which she primarily uses to strike her students if she catches any acts of bullying.

Raiya (雷らい矢や) is a boy who belongs in Unji's gang and he's his right-hand man. He was involved in the Renjaku Apartments Incident and is accompanying the Family to the Izumo Grand Shrine.

Appearance

He wears the Renjaku High's gakuran although he keeps the jacket unbuttoned, revealing a plain white shirt. His blonde hair is slightly parted in the middle and it almost covers his eyebrows. He has three earrings on each ear similar to Unji's and his left cheek is scarred by a knife cut due to a traumatic incident in his youth.
Personality

He's a kindhearted boy who got taken advantage of back when he was younger. He's very devoted to Unji since he rescued him from his aggressors and he's loyal to him. He's also very thankful to him because he accepted him as who he is despite the world pushing them to the side. He's willing to help out Unji in any way, although he doesn't back down from incorporating violence to his missions. He's very thoughtful and passionate, leading him to become the right hand man of Unji and he commands the gang when he isn't around. He's still traumatized from his youth and the times he got hurt, as seen when Fairy-Tale Card's words led him to getting brainwashed.
Background

When Raiya was way younger, he was stripped naked inside a shower by delinquents who beat him up and proceeded to scar his face with a knife. Growing up he continued getting bullied until one day Unji and his gang noticed what they were doing to him and rescued him. He was accepted into Unji's gang and he hung around with them at their hideout, filled with kids who had either trouble with school or their families. Once, a girl was taking dangerous vitamins and Unji kicked them away, ordering Raiya to make sure she doesn't take any more of them. The girl shouted back but he was on Unji's side and tried to calm her down, however she broke down crying because she wasn't as good as the other kids at school and their parents had given up on her, asking why she needed to live. Unji revealed that although he had no idea how to help her, she brought happiness to their friend group unlike anybody else and she should have stayed whenever she felt sad. Raiya admired Unji because of this and their bond grew stronger with Raiya eventually becoming the co-leader of the gang.
Synopsis

Danmara Arc

He and his gang chase after Daiki Hakono when Momo and Okarun suddenly protect the man, the latter showcasing his Turbo Granny powers when Raiya swings his bat against Ayase. The group is shocked as he resembles Unji and Momo asks if they have touched a golden ball and if they are friends with Unji. The boy refuses to answer and threatens to hurt them if they don't hand over the old man. He soon gives up as it's not in his moral code to fight women and brings the three of them to the hideout, where the diorama is found. He explains how Unji is in there and they want to throw Daiki in to bring him back as he was in there in the first place.

Raiya reveals how he actually wanted to swap places with the girl but Unji denied him and everyone else. He also informs Momo that Unji was researching into the diorama as he thought it was a cursed object when he was approached by a mysterious person who gave him the Kintama, claiming it was needed to destroy the world inside the cursed wicker trunk. However, it had been over a week since he entered and tension rises again as they try to force the man back into the diorama. Momo gets accidentally pushed inside and instantly transported in the alternate reality, inducing fear into everyone. Okarun sees Ayase's figurine moving and realizes that it's actually a game, to which Raiya points out they had actually tracked Unji's for a couple of days until it disappeared, leading them to believe he was in serious trouble.

Raiya announces to the gang that they are going to enter the diorama and progress together like Unji and Momo are currently doing but Okarun confronts his decision, claiming it's a cursed object and they might get stuck inside too. He suggests to wait for Seiko's help but Raiya points out Ken's close relationship with Ayase and how he's just going to risk her life by not taking action. Meanwhile, he and his squad are ready to jump in and save Unji's, but he understands Okarun's point of view and lets him do as he wants. The boy calls over the other members to prepare for the mission while Ken activates his power and rushes towards the Ayase Residence.

Unji and Momo almost get overwhelmed during the final battle against the castle's army when Raiya, his gang and the entire Renjaku High School save them from the enemy. They buy enough time for the duo to get inside the castle and destroy the final seal, completing the game. Turbo Granny, who got inside the cursed trunk with Okarun, orders the kids to close their eyes since the now released Fairy-Tale Card has the power to take over anyone who looks at him. The yokai points out how the world he created inside the diorama is way better than the one they came from, where most of the kids are rejected by society and treated like garbage, which makes Raiya remember the time he got assaulted as a kid and scarred with a knife. He opens his eyes and gets possessed by the Fairy-Tale Card who makes him run towards Unji and swing his weapon at him, forcing him to open his eyes too. The yokai is then able to brainwash him and utilize his Umbrella Boy powers to their full potential.

Rin utilizes Mai's gravitational powers outside of the cursed trunk to lift in the air all of the figurines, which applies to them inside the Danmara dimension too. The Fairy-Tale Card is surprised to see them flying next to him and Raiya, along with many others, call out for Unji to take back control. They are finally transported out of the diorama back to Earth but the yokai escapes too, leaving Unji's strained body. The leader and a couple of students assist him who notice he's not breathing and rush to call an ambulance for him. At the end of the fight, he helps an injured Daiki to stand back up.

A couple days later, Raiya and Unji's closest friends visit him in the hospital, happy to see him recover, but he tells them to keep quiet to avoid disturbing the other patients.

Kozuka Knives Arc

The Renjaku High School students block the gate of Kami High in search for Momo Ayase. After Unji reconnects with the girl after all that happened, Raiya accompanies a really old Daiki who's aging at an unnatural speed, hoping to seek for Momo's knowledge of a cure. They decide to consult Seiko and walk home together, despite Jiji and Aira being on bad terms with Unji after they believed he was another pawn of the Orchestrator seeking to hurt Ayase. Inside the Ayase Residence they are introduced to Seiko, who they struggle to believe is a granny, and show her the old man's condition, to which she suggests to come along in their trip to Shimane as Daiki may have been cursed just like Momo.

At the airport, Raiya, who was busy carrying the frail Daiki, notices that Unji's eyesight, which had been affected by the curse already, is now almost completely gone and he shouts to Jiji and Bamora, the former trying to get the latter to see Momo but failing due to the curse's progression, to accompany Unji to the plane. Raiya asks Daiki to remain patient as they make their way to Shimane, however the old man wonders why he's helping him out since the first time they met, he and his gang wanted to beat him up with sticks. He justifies it by saying that he thought it was Daiki's fault for Unji's disappearance so the elderly kid asks why he would do all this for Unji's sake. Raiya affirms that Unji has helped both Daiki and himself, who back in the day used to get bullied until Unji came to his rescue, who despite his aggressive behavior, never left his friends behind. He continues by saying that everyone around Unji were troubled kids and he remembers an episode where his friend was consuming nocive vitamins and Unji ordered him to make sure she doesn't take any more. He tried to reason with her but she broke down and claimed that she couldn't do things that other normal kids could. Raiya admired his friend as he declared the girl's worth to their friend group and so he realizes that all along they wanted to be accepted even though they didn't keep up with the world around them. He finishes by saying that Unji saved them and they'll do anything for him.

On the plane, he and Daiki happily watch Jiji and Unji's bickering, but when the subterraneans try to attack Jiji and Bamora, he stands up to protect her. Unji tells her to hide under the seats, but Bamora suprises the both of them when she reshapes her clothing into her Kaiju exosuit, affirming that she's strong enough to fight. She's asked by Jiji to activate empty space to protect the civilians and they all get transported inside. Raiya is overwhelmed by his opponent, who makes fun of him since he was expecting more of a fight from a youngling, when suddenly the Kito's jacket is held in place by Unji who was hiding under the seats. The man doesn't find it fair for Unji to be hiding while the others are fighting so he repeatedly starts punching him, even when Raiya shouts at him to stop since Unji cannot see. Another Kito kicks Raiya down the corridor, making him shift focus on him while the other pummels Unji. Raiya is amazed by Unji who first lands a jab on the man attacking him, sending him flying, and headbutts the other, taking them both down, before reverting to a normal blind person, getting scared by Bamora's Kaiju. They all then get thrown around by the engine's explosion, caused by a tornado of sharks, possessing an ear, a nose and a mouth, suddenly appearing outside the plane and crashing onto it.

Ranzan and other students of class A get confronted by Toramaru Sodenashi, leader of class C, asking them to submit. This obviously makes a turf war break out and Ranzan covers his classmates by using a pallet as a shield.

With the final seal broken and the Fairy-Tale Card yokai now free who immediately tries to convince them to stay, he looks down, defeated, pondering about the way he's living and reflects if he should stay inside Danmara due to him being treated like garbage in the real world.

A few days after the incident, he's invited to the Goro Stamina Booster by Seiko and he devours his plate while others are too busy staring at Seiko's beauty.

Reiko Kashima (カシマレイコ, Kashima Reiko?), also known as the Slit-Mouthed Woman (口裂け女, Kuchisake-onna?), is a yokai that formerly resided in a ruined area in Kamigoe City. After being bested by Momo, Reiko Kashima harbored a grudge against the girl and vowed to get revenge on her the next time they met. However, after observing her relationship with Okarun, Reiko Kashima let go of her resentment and changed her mind in finding a suitable partner.

In Dandadan, she serves as one of the main antagonists during the Space Globalists Arc.

Appearance

Reiko Kashima is a tall female yokai, easily towering over average size humans, with muscular arms and legs. Her most distinguishing feature, which is where her epithet comes from, is her extremely wide mouth with rows of multiple sharp teeth. She wears a heavy amount of makeup; mascara that accent her round eyes and lipstick for her mouth. Her nails are also colored dark. She has very long, jet black hair, which is kept tied with a bow, and wears a crown on her head. When absent of her makeup, Reiko Kashima's appearance drastically changes. Her head is nicely shaped, and her facial features are revealed to be less prominent to where she looks more human; having normal eyes with long eyelashes and, most noticeably, a normal lipstick mouth. Overall, her face outside of her makeup has been noted to be remarkably beautiful by Momo and Jiji.

For her attire, she wears a collared dress with a bow tie and dress shoes. While seeking revenge on Momo, Reiko Kashima's head of hair became unruly while retaining her long ponytail. Her eyes also became concentric circles. Her dress changed to one that had puffy sleeves with four lines running down to the waist and a different bow tie that is much larger and had a gem at the center. Her shoes also changed to become black dress shoes. After choosing to wear less makeup, Reiko Kashima's dress became slightly altered from when she spent her time searching for Momo, with the only change being the loss of her puffy sleeves. She also lost her crown.

During her lifetime, Reiko Kashima was a young girl with long black hair that was tied with a bow at the end (similar to how her current hairstyle is as a yokai) and wore a dress and a hat. During her final moments, her hair was short and messy, she wore tattered clothes, and was crippled with bandages covering the stump of her legs.
Gallery

Personality

Reiko Kashima traps Bamora
Reiko Kashima trapping Bamora in her mirror for the sole purpose of making her look good in comparison.
Reiko Kashima is a yokai who is vain and narcissistic, as she has an obsession with looking at her own reflection through her mirror and only favors things that are horrid since they only make her look good in comparison, which prompts her to trap them inside her mirror. The only grounds for her being willing to release her victims is if they block her reflection after taking up room and finds it even more dissatisfying when they "defile" her mirror by somehow acting cute. If someone were to offend her by calling her "ugly", and/or steal her mirror, Reiko Kashima loses her composure and breaks out into a highly agitated state at the offender. While she believes that she looks beautiful when she applies on her makeup, she seems to be rather oblivious of the fact that she is naturally beautiful when her true face is exposed.

She is also shown to have a modest side, as she tried keeping her panties from being shown after her attack on Bamora accidently blew her dress up.

Reiko Kashima despises the expulsion spell word "pomade" and immediately attacks anyone who would dare shout it in her presence. She is also extremely bitter and sadistic towards her enemies. After Momo temporarily expelled her from the living world with the word "pomade", Reiko Kashima relentlessly pursued her until she could exact her revenge, having plans to torture her forever within the confines of her mirror as her "plaything".

Stemming from her cause of death, Reiko Kashima hates the sight of aerial bombardment. After the main force of the Kur began their attack inside the Empty Space by dropping bombs, Reiko Kashima responded furiously by using her mirror ability to destroy their main ship and trapping every last one of the Kur inside her mirror where she proceeded to annihilate them in a fit of rage.

After observing Momo's growing relationship with Okarun, that she found frustrating due to the girl not being honest with herself, Reiko Kashima chose to commit herself to finding love as well.
Background

Not much is known about Reiko Kashima's past life when she was alive except that she had a loved one and that she died as a victim in an airplane bombing attack.
Synopsis

Space Globalists Arc

Reiko Kashima disappearing
Reiko Kashima being sent out of the living world by Momo.
Reiko Kashima is met by Momo and Bamora as they attempt to get to school through the ruined area and asks them if she looks pretty. She then attacks Momo in annoyance after hearing her shout out the word "pomade", as she attempted to have the yokai disappear. In response, Bamora uses her exosuit to attack Reiko Kashima with a volley of punches. This becomes ineffective as Reiko Kashima stands unfazed, all the while finding that her exosuit makes her look pretty in comparison, and performs a suplex against her. Hearing Momo attempting to say "pomade" ten times again, Reiko Kashima uses her mirror ability to stop her by hitting her with her fist that emerges from a piece of glass and proceeds to keep her from running away using the other shards on the ground. After being grabbed by Bamora, Reiko Kashima decides to trap her inside her mirror, as she wanted to continue having her look good, and warns Momo not to complete the "pomade" spell since it will end up having Bamora disappear along with her. Momo tells Reiko Kashima that she is not concerned with Bamora's well-being and calls her out as ugly as she prepares to fight her in refusal to lose to her. Reiko Kashima then reacts with rage upon hearing her rude comment and becomes even more furious with Momo after she managed to steal her mirror. Reiko Kashima chases after her as she tries to release Bamora and has her trapped inside as well. However, she soon releases both of them due to the two blocking her reflection and started acting cute. As a consequent to falling for their trickery, Reiko Kashima loses sight of them and disappears after Momo completes the "pomade" spell while using Bamora's exosuit to become invisible.

Reiko Kashima trying to lure out Momo
Reiko Kashima trying to lure Momo out of bed.
After returning back to the living world, Reiko Kashima seeks vengeance against Momo for her actions earlier. At the Ayase house, Reiko Kashima alters her voice to sound like Okarun to lair Momo out of her room but fails after the latter catches on to her act, having mistakenly addressed Jiji the wrong way. Though her trickery was ineffective, Reiko Kashima continued speaking in Okarun's voice for the remainder of the night.

The next day, Reiko Kashima tracks Momo down to a manga cafe and possesses a worker at the front desk to find her. Momo becomes cautious of the worker trying to enter her private room and hides behind the Serpo accompanying her. Reiko Kashima tries to unmask Momo as she talks to the Serpo but has her possession of the worker undone after Momo uses her bandages to cover his mirror.

The Kur defeated
Reiko Kashima eradicates the Kur's main force.
Reiko Kashima finally reunites with Momo at the same moment the main force of the Kur entered the Empty Space and commenced their attack. After she expresses her plans to imprison and torture her inside her mirror, Reiko Kashima sees Momo on her knees in despair between her situation with the yokai in front of her and the alien invasion and wishes to see Seiko again. This scene, along with the bombs being dropped by the Kur, triggers a tragic memory Reiko Kashima had when she was alive, which causes her to furiously destroy the Kur's main ship with her mirror ability for reenacting the same event. She then proceeds to trap every alien inside her mirror to annihilate them all. After being done with this, Reiko Kashima watches as both Okarun and Momo try to protect each other from the former, resulting in her flashbacking to a time in her past life where she was happy with a loved one. This prompts Reiko Kashima to spare Momo and leave the area without a word.

Reiko Kashima threatening Momo
Reiko Kashima demanding to Momo to be honest with her feelings towards Okarun.
Later, Reiko Kashima is met by Momo and her friends as they head off to the market, with the latter being shocked to see the yokai with a different face due to her being without her makeup. Momo becomes confused with her appearance, as she thought that she had attained Nirvana from her mysterious disappearance earlier, and is clarified by Reiko Kashima that this was not possibly since she believes that there is no one who can extinguish her hatred. She also adds that she hates Momo's existence, having secretly observed her interactions with Okarun, during her time seeking vengeance against her, and became annoyed with her inability to be honest with her feelings towards him. On the other hand, she becomes inspired to find love herself and threatens Momo, threatening to take Okarun away from her if she continues to hide her feelings. Reiko Kashima then leaves off to start her search for a man.

Abilities and Powers

Yokai Abilities

Mirror Power [v · e]
Reiko Kashima has the power to control the mirror she carries around with her, allowing her to perform various abilities.
Remote Attacking
Mirror Portal
For attacking her enemies, Reiko Kashima can project parts of her body from her mirror to other mirrors, or shards of glass, within her vicinity as a portal.
Strengths and Weaknesses
Reiko Kashima destroys the Kur battleship
The main strength of Reiko Kashima's remote attacking ability with her mirror is that it allows to fight at a distance and to launch surprise attacks at her opponents by sending her hand through it and remotely striking them from anywhere glass is around. She can also prevent them from escaping from her by grabbing their legs from a piece of glass on the ground. As long as her hand remains inside her mirror, Reiko Kashima can manifest multiple hands from many glasses to overwhelm her opponent. The range of her connection to glass is shown to extend at least a city-wide radius, as Reiko Kashima was capable of manifesting a giant fist to destroy the Kur's main battleship from the multiple shards of glass scattered from the Empty Space Tokyo.

Since Reiko Kashima needs her mirror to perform her abilities, her enemy can steal it from her, if presented with the right opportunity, to prevent her from doing so.
Usage
Reiko Kashima uses her remote attacking ability against anyone who provokes her, such as saying the word "pomade" in an attempt to have her vanish from the living world.
Imprisonment
Momo and Bamora trapped in the mirror
Reiko Kashima can imprison her targets within a pocket dimension that serves as the inside of her mirror by having their reflection shown. The alternate dimension takes on the setting of a dark space with a circular portal at the center that serves as the other side of Reiko Kashima's mirror in the real world.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The main force trapped by Reiko Kashima
The main strength of Reiko Kashima's mirror imprisonment ability is that there is no possible way for anyone on the outside to free a trapped victim from the confines of her mirror, as only Reiko Kashima has the authority to release her targets. Trying will also put the person at risk of being trapped as well if their reflection is shown and Reiko Kashima is nearby to activate her ability. Once inside, Reiko Kashima can do whatever she pleases to her prisoners. This ability is also capable of trapping an entire army. To perform this, Reiko Kashima only needs to have her mirror reflect a partial view of the army, as anything or anyone affiliated with the large group will be instantly sent to the alternate dimension. This gives indication that the alternate dimension is infinite and there is no limit as to how many things Reiko Kashima can store inside her mirror. Those trapped within the mirror are also proportionally small compared to Reiko Kashima if she chooses to send a body part to the dimension.

Since Reiko Kashima needs her mirror to perform her abilities, her enemy can steal it from her, if presented with the right opportunity, to prevent her from doing so. Although it is impossible for her captives to escape from her mirror, they can be cunning enough to exploit her narcissistic personality to force her into releasing them by blocking her reflection and acting cute.
Usage
Using her mirror imprisonment ability, Reiko Kashima traps those who have a horrid appearance to better appreciate how beautiful she views herself compared to them. After trapping those who have annoyed her, she either becomes playful by drawing on their face with her lipstick, torturous where she sees her prisoner as her "plaything", or simply outright kills them by sending her fist inside that is gigantic compared to her enemy.
Possession
Reiko Kashima overshadowing
Reiko Kashima's connection to other mirrors allows her to possess anyone who looks at their own reflection.
Strengths and Weaknesses
With her ability to possess people through their own reflection, Reiko Kashima can get close to her intended target as a form of deception. After possessing someone of her choosing, Reiko Kashima is required to have the mirror that allowed her to take possession of said target on their person at all times to maintain the connection and not have it covered up by something since it will cancel out the possession. Her possession to get close to her targets in secret may prove to be ineffective if her enemy is wary of her attempting to make contact.
Heart Reading
Reiko Kashima's mirror connection also allows her to see into her target's hearts to read their emotions.
Usage
By combining her mirror power to read people's heart and her yokai ability to perfectly mimic a person's voice, Reiko Kashima can deceive her enemies into thinking that they are talking to an ally. After peeking into Momo's heart, Reiko Kashima discovered that she had feelings for Okarun and exploited this in an attempt to have her come out of her bedroom by perfectly mimicking his voice, which had almost worked in her favor if not for her incorrectly addressing Jiji's name the wrong way.
Surveillance
Reiko Kashima spying on Momo
Reiko Kashima can use her mirror to spy on the current activities of her targets, allowing her to know where they are at all times to confront them at the perfect opportunity.
Vocal Replication
As a yokai, Reiko Kashima is able to perfectly mimic a person's voice to deceive her enemies. This becomes even more effective when combined with her mirror ability to sense people's emotions, as she can voice a person who her enemy has feelings for. However, this can only work if she is communicating to her enemy away from their line of sight. Also, in order for her act to be flawless, she must speak in the same way as the person she is imitating.

Rin Sawaki (佐脇 凛, Sawaki Rin?), mainly referred to as Class Rep (委員長, Iinchō?) is one of the main characters of the manga series Dandadan.

She is a student at Kami High who serves as the class representative of Class C. She later became one of Momo and Okarun's main allies whenever the two are faced with the paranormal.

Appearance

Rin is a young girl of average height with brown eyes and long brown hair that she styles into pigtails and has bangs that cover her forehead. She also wears glasses with purple frames. Her common attire is her school uniform; a dark buttoned up blazer with her school emblem located around the left breast, a collared shirt, a bow, a dark short skirt, long socks, and sandals.
Gallery

Rin's full appearance.
Rin's full appearance.
Rin as a child.
Rin as a child.
Personality

Rin is a kind, caring, thoughtful, respectful and dutiful young girl. As Class C's representative, she has her classmates' best interest at heart and hopes that they can confide in her with any problems they may have. She is also not above being confrontational if it concerns the well-being of her classmates. Rin's caring and selflessness dates all the way back to her childhood, being willing to look after her bedridden grandmother and doing chores around the house to take some of the burden off of her mother who was out working, even at the cost of her social life with friends.

Rin has a passion for vampire romance fiction and dreams of one day writing her own story as a novelist. In addition, she also possesses an over-active imagination and has a tendency of getting lost in her thoughts when thinking of implausible scenarios that are vampire related, which comedically leads to her subconsciously saying everything in her head out loud. When made aware of this by someone nearby, Rin automatically assumes in embarrassment that they can read minds and it is confirmation that they are a vampire. This side of hers mainly occurs whenever she is faced with something unexpected, such as her meeting the talking stuffed cat Turbo Granny for the first time, even mistaking her for a male partially due to her crude language. She also has a tendency to swoon for many of these "vampires."
Background

As a child, Rin was put in charge of taking care of her bedridden grandmother while her mother was out working. While in elementary school, Rin made a great impression on her classmates after showcasing her talent for singing, catching the eye of a girl named Mai Kawabanga who believed that together they have what it takes to become idols. Rin complied with Mai to practice for an upcoming junior idol audition, however, after her mother made her aware of how dependent she is of her to look after her grandmother when she is away, Rin unfortunately told Mai and her friends that she would have to skip out on the auditions to continue her duties at home. With Mai's friends interpreting this as a lie and her mother being lazy, Rin makes a statement saying that she believes that there is no worth in them becoming idols, leading to her friendship with Mai ending as the girl viewed her as a traitor.
Abilities and Powers

Natural Abilities

Skill Set

Singing Talent: Rin is a talented singer with a beautiful singing voice.

Supernatural Abilities

Mai Kawabanga's Powers [v · e]
Rin can harness Mai's Onbusuman abilities by merging with the yokai. Once merged, Rin is compelled to wear a bikini-style idol costume, consisting of a pair of fundoshi underwear with ruffles and a turtle shell-theme bra, knee, and shoulder pads. A large turtle shell with spikes on the sides is noticeably strapped to Rin's back as well. The ensemble is then complete with Mai's bow atop her head, triangle-shaped earrings, a small tie with a collar, thigh-high boots, and long gloves, as well as Mai in the form of a microphone. Additionally, Rin's pigtail hairstyle becomes elongated and turns white.
Fused Rin Form
Gravity Manipulation
Rin using gravity manipulation
Through singing (as stipulated by Mai), Rin gains the ability to wield Mai's Onbusuman power to control gravity.
Strengths and Weaknesses
The primary strength of this ability lies in Rin's capacity to manipulate both living things and inanimate objects.

Due to Rin needing to sing in order to control gravity, this ability can be neutralized if an enemy manages to impede her singing in any manner, such as the Fairy-Tale Card's power to erase her mouth.
Usage
Rin utilized this ability to bring the captives trapped in Danmara back to the real world by levitating their figurines out of the cursed trunk.

Ririna (リリナ, Ririna?) is a student at Kami High and an employee of Moe Moe Kikoho.

Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Acrobatic Silky Arc

After Momo had an incident with Okarun where she accidently locked lips with him at school, Ririna and a few other female schoolmates crowded Momo in eagerness to learn more about the incident after hearing it from Miko and Muko.

Evil Eye Arc

Ririna is brought up by Miko and Muko after Momo decides to go look for a part-time job to earn money for house repairs, being mentioned that her place of work, Moe Moe Kikoho, is looking for hire and is later asked by the two friends to put in a good word for Momo.

Space Globalists Arc

Kinta spots her happily talking to Muko and Miko in Class 2-C as he's searching for his friends who, unbeknownst to him, are preparing for the incoming alien invasion.

Rokuro Serpo (セルポ 6郎, Serupo 6rō?) is a Serpo who allied himself with Momo and her allies to destroy the data the Kur stole from his brethren and to stop their invasion on Earth. Following this event, Rokuro was deemed a defect by the Serpos and was banished, leading to him becoming an independent clone.

In Dandadan, he serves as a major supporting character.

Appearance

While identical to his fellow Serpo, Rokuro is the only one among his clones who possesses eyes that makes him distinguishable. He also possesses two thick vertical scars that run down both sides of his face and across his eyes, inflicted on him after the Kur attacked the Serpo.
Gallery

Rokuro face close-up.
