Music Room Portraits

Main article: Music Room Portraits
Okarun and Aira vs the Music Room Portraits
the Music Room Portraits appearing after summoning them.
Music Room Portraits (音楽室の肖像画, Ongakushitsu no Shōzōga?) The Beethoven Portrait Mystery, also known as the Portrait Beethoven Mystery in Japan, is a part of the famous “Seven School Mysteries” that are passed down in schools across Japan. This urban legend revolves around the belief that if one visits the music room at night, the portraits of famous classical musicians on the walls, including Beethoven, come to life in various eerie ways. The legend suggests that the eyes of the portraits may glow red, follow observers around the room, or even change expressions when not being directly observed. Additionally, there are claims that these spirits might play the pianos in the music room when nobody is present, with the sound serving as an omen of impending misfortune.

Tiny Old Man

Main article: Tiny Old Man
Tiny Old Man Infobox
The Tiny Old Man's full appearance.
The Tiny Old Men (ちいさい おじさん Chiisai Ojisan) are fairy-like creatures in the Japanese Folklore which bestow good luck upon those who spot them. They generally appear to children and cheer them but they can also show themselves to adults who have become overworked or have fallen ill and also to celebrities. They are also incredibly fast and disappear quickly so it's impossible to get a clear photo of them. Kashimoto allegedly spotted it multiple times and is now researching it, leading him to also study the Pygmies' nature.

Pygmy

Main article: Pygmy
Pygmy Portrait
The Pygmies without their war masks.
The Pygmies (小人 Kobito?) are invisible miniscule creatures who, according to Queen, are from a folklore of an unspecified region and they were originally people who were driven off the surface and forgotten by others and the world itself. They quietly disappeared, also losing their own memories of their identities and transformed into the little pygmies, however their desire to be acknowleged is still strong and this causes them to gather around any person who can actually see them, using all their forces to help them. Because their powers were contained in a Kozuka knife, Kouki Yukishiro became the main focus of the pygmies, despite wanting to return to her normal life.

Jiangshi

Main article: Jiangshi
Jiangshi Infobox
Jiangshis ready to attack.
The Jiangshi is a legendary creature from Chinese folklore. The origins of the Jiangshi can be traced back to the Han Dynasty (206 BCE - 220 CE), where it was believed to be a reanimated corpse created through dark magic or sorcery.

Severed Head Dribblers

Main article: Severed Head Dribblers
Severed Head Dribblers Infobox
Severed Head Dribblers picking up their heads.
Severed Head Dribblers (生首ドリブル, Namakubi Doriburu?) The Severed Head Dribblers it is inspired by the urban legend Headless Soccer.

Headless Soccer is a Japanese urban legend that tells the story of a group of high school students who played soccer with a headless ghost. According to the legend, the students were practicing soccer late at night when they encountered a mysterious figure wearing a soccer uniform but lacking a head. Despite their initial shock, the students decided to continue playing with the ghostly figure, who displayed remarkable skills on the field. The legend goes on to describe how the headless ghost led the team to victory in a series of matches before disappearing into the night.

Tome (トメ, Tome?) is a Sumerian and a fighter, alongside her allies Banga, Aja, and Bamora, against the Kur who have invaded her planet.

Appearance

Like all the other Sumerians, she possesses two antennas on top of her head and she wears the standard metal armor for their army. She keeps her hair in a bun and her hair is parted to the right side of the face. She has two scars, one on the bottom left of her jaw and one on her right cheek. Her left cheek is also disfigured and has multiple bruises.

While on the spaceship, her right eye is fully covered by a bandage that diagonally covers her head. There's also a tiny band aid applied below her left eye.
Personality

She's pretty cheerful but also mature, since we are told she has participated in many fights against the Space Globalists. Still, she jokes around a lot with her friend Aja and tries to be optimistic despite their situation. She gets nervous when they don't find any sumerians at the meeting point and she shows her bravery while she protects Banga and Bamora during their escape. Instead of waiting to pass away in a cave, her infallible determination leads her to advance against the Kur to see the ocean, which she has never seen because she lived in a small mountain town. Her strong mental fortitude makes her refuse to die without seeing it even when the odds are stacked against her. Like Aja, she acts a sort of aunt to Bamora, willing to throw away her own life for the last sumerian child. She's also seen smoking as a way to deal with stress.
Background

Past

Tome was born and raised in a poor mountain town on her home planet Sumer.

Invasion of Sumer

Upon the alien invasion initiated by the globalists dubbed as the Kur, Tome joined an all-female resistance group to fight against them, with her main partners during the war being Banga and Aja. After Banga complains having to clean up after Bamora, a girl she had rescued off from the battlefield, Tome insists that she take care of her as her savior and suspects Bamora very well ending up being the last child of their race.

Years later, Tome, Banga, Aja, and Bamora set forth with their regiment towards the West to rendezvous with a faction of Sumerian survivors. Upon their arrival, however, they discovered that their destination was a trap orchestrated by the Kur, who launched an ambush on the group. Ultimately, Tome, Banga, Aja, and Bamora emerged as the only survivors, managing to escape the chaos and find refuge in a nearby cave. Desiring to see the ocean before facing her inevitable demise, Tome journeyed with Aja to make a final stand against the Kur until they reached their goal. Later, Banga and Bamora joined them after Banga had a revelation, realizing they could utilize the Sumerian transportation pyramid to relocate to the Sumerians' second home, Idea. Although they successfully arrived at the site, turmoil erupted when a male Sumerian freed by Bamora was shot by the Kur, inciting panic among the other male Sumerians. Faced with no alternative, the four were compelled to fight their way to the pyramid. During the struggle, Banga was incapacitated by missiles while attempting to shield Bamora, prompting Tome and Aja to cover for her. However, they soon found themselves overwhelmed by the Kur. Following Banga's activation of a Sumerian god exosuit, which inspired the enslaved male Sumerians to join the fight, Tome and Aja provided cover for Bamora, ensuring her safe passage to the pyramid. As she did so, Tome took joy in engaging in battle with the ocean's beauty in her view.

Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Space Globalists Arc

After acquiring a ship, Tome, Banga, Aja, and two male Sumerians fight off the Kur in the sky and depart from Sumer, setting course for Idea to reunite with Bamora.

He has a very muscular body and he wears a tank top with a jaguar-like pattern, white shorts and white shoes. He has earings and wears a chain around his neck. His blonde hair is messy and either stands up or falls to the side. Because of the dark beard and some dark parts of his hair, there's a chance he dyed his hair. He usually has a very intimidating face which gives an aggressive vibe.
Personality

He's hotheaded and as the leader of Class C, he believes he's the strongest student at Renjaku and as such his class is superior to others, since the first time we see him he asks Class A to submit to them. He loses his cool multiple times as we see in Danmara when he screams to find Zuma and when he ignores Momo's tips to fight their respective counterparts. He's so confident in his skill and is rarely scared that he even personally threatens the Fairy-Tale Card, saying he would beat him up once they returned to Earth. This doesn't mean that he doesn't care for others as he's seen defending Rin from the controlled aggressors and offers to assist Zuma in his quest to save Daiki from his curse, although he maintains his intimidating and aggressive vibe.
ADVERTISEMENT

Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Danmara Arc

Class C and class A are at a tense standoff and Toramaru pushes it to the edge when he asks the students to accept their fate as inferiors and to submit to them. Benzou, leader of class A, doesn't waste time and runs forward, planting Toramaru's face on his knee. Others follow immediately after and a huge turf war breaks out to determine which class is the strongest.

He and the entire Renjaku High School along with Zuma's gang get transported inside Danmara to save Unji. When they arrive to the battlefield, he screams out, demanding to know where Zuma is. Despite Momo's warnings about fighting the respective enemy classes depending on their own, Toramaru and many others charge in, punching the warriors and defeating them.

Due to Momo and Zuma breaking the final seal and freeing the Fairy-Tale Card, he gets immediately concerned about the force of nature who just appeared in front of them. This escalates when he possesses Umbrella Boy and Momo warns him and others to utilize Medusa's card to turn into stone and survive the deadly blasts.

He returns with the delinquents after the Fairy-Tale Card escapes skyward, screaming, enraged that Zuma's now under control of that evil yokai. Thanks to Rin and Mai's endeavours, the delinquents levitate into the sky and Toramaru soon approaches the spirit, threatening to beat him to a pulp once they return to Earth. The yokai is bewildered by this and questions how he's able to fly, although the other delinquents soon reach him and join forces before reappearing back in the real world. He's one of the few who try to seize the Fairy-Tale Card tentacles but his sheer size makes this task impossible and he retreats. He also did not get affected by any of the spirit's powers when Count Saint-Germain arrived on the scene, so he resorted to defend Rin from the controlled delinquents. He's both scared and intrigued when he sees the defeated yokai burst beams of light into the night.

Days after the incident, he's invited to the Goro Stamina Booster by Seiko and he quickly devours his plate.

Current Saga

Kozuka Knives Arc

The Renjaku High classes decide to set their differences aside to lend a hand to the cursed Daiki Hakono who's aging at an unnatural speed. Toramaru and other delinquents stand in front of Kami High's gate to look for Momo under request of Zuma. The students of the school are frightened by them and Okarun, accompanied by Bamora and a shrunk down Momo, volunteers to approach them since he already met some of them. When Okarun asks them kindly to leave because it was causing problems, Toramaru immediately gets mad and stares him down to intimidate him. Later, when Aira and Jiji see Momo in Zuma's hands and believing he's another pawn of the blackmailer like Kouki, they manifest their powers and attack him, taking Momo away from him. In the background, Toramaru screams out, concerned about Zuma and ready to inflict pain to his attackers.

The Tsuchinoko (ツチノコ, Tsuchinoko?) was the name of a kuragari, or Mongolian Death Worm, that had been revered by the people of Jiji's village, especially the Kito Family, as the Great Snake (大蛇様, Orochi-sama?), believed to be the cryptid tsuchinoko.

In Dandadan, the Tsuchinoko serves as one of the primary antagonists during the Cursed House Arc.

Appearance

The Tsuchinoko is an enormous worm with a spotted pattern serpent body and a tentacle ringed gaping mouth that has multiple rows of teeth. Okarun had noted that the Tsuchinoko was much larger than the average Mongolian Death Worm, which are about 1.5 to 2 meters long in length.
Background

During the feudal period, the Mongolian Death Worm resided inside a village volcano where it became revered as the Tsuchinoko by the villagers due to it causing the volcano to become active whenever hungry. In order to keep the village safe from the volcano's magma, the Kito Family appeased the Tsuchinoko by offering a child from their village as a sacrifice for it to eat and continued on this ritual for 200 years, with one of the rituals resulting in the birth of the Evil Eye.
Synopsis

Cursed House Arc

After the Kito Family has the Enjoji family move into the sacrificial house, the Tsuchinoko causes the parents to succumb to its suicidal psychic influence and end up hospitalized. Believing that the house is cursed based on this event and the appearance of the Evil Eye, the son of the Enjoji family, Jiji, receives help from Momo and Okarun to exorcise the house. This then leads to the trio, along with the Kito Family, being sent deep underground the house where the Tsuchinoko resides. Despite the Kito Family presenting themselves as worshippers, the Tsuchinoko eats them and goes after Momo, Okarun, and Jiji next. While the Tsuchinoko has Momo and Okarun fall victim to its suicidal psychic influence, the worm chases after Jiji as he struggles keeping the two from killing themselves. Just as the Tsuchinoko confronts Jiji with nowhere else left to run, the Evil Eye appears to use his powers to clash with the Tsuchinoko's, which ends up canceling out the mind control on Momo and Okarun. The Tsuchinoko is then decapitated by Okarun in his transformed state but regenerates from the damage and chases after him. After Okarun reaches his limit, the Tsuchinoko releases electricity that shocks Momo, Jiji, and the Turbo Granny down at the lower level and spews out phlegm to bind them as it dives down to swallow them. However, the Tsuchinoko is stopped after being punched by Jiji who becomes possessed by the Evil Eye. The Evil Eye then further damages the Tsuchinoko by continuously attacking it with a grudge form ball, causing the worm to have no other option but to retreat within the ground. At the same time, the Tsuchinoko creates a spore to poison its enemies who continue to remain in its layer.

Later, the Tsuchinoko is forced to come up to the surface after Momo came up with the plan to have the village firemen hose down the sacrificial house after setting it on fire, realizing earlier that worms are unable to remain underground if its soaked with water and will end up drying up once exposed to sunlight, which starts to happen to the Tsuchinoko. The Tsuchinoko then takes cover behind the sacrificial house to prevent itself from completely drying up, however, using her psychokinesis, Momo destroys the house by throwing a fire truck and successfully kills the Tsuchinoko. After Momo checks to see if the Tsuchinoko is really dead by kicking its stomach, the Tsuchinoko's corpse reacts by vomiting out the Kito Family who managed to stay alive.

Though she managed to stop the threat of the Tsuchinoko, Momo now becomes faced with the problem of stopping the active village volcano from destroying the village due to it being linked to the Tsuchinoko. Having figured out the true message to the village legend, Momo uses the Tsuchinoko's corpse as a hose to cool down the magma in the forest with its phlegm as water from the hot springs starts to pump it. However, her plan is soon hindered with the Kito Family not wanting her to take credit for protecting the village and the Evil Eye damaging the Tsuchinoko's corpse. Later, after the arrival of Seiko, Taro, the Dover Demon, and Chiquitita, the Tsuchinoko's corpse is once again used to cool down the magma with the help of Chiquitita controlling it with his father's spacecraft and is also used to save Okarun and the Turbo Granny who were still trapped within the Tsuchinoko's layer.

Kuragari Abilities

Suicidal Psychic Waves [v · e]
The Tsuchinoko is able to release psychic waves to manipulate others into committing suicide. While effective against normal humans or special ones, such as espers or yokai ability users, this power has no effect against yokai themselves or those who possess incredible spiritual power.
Regeneration
Tsuchinoko regenerating
The Tsuchinoko is able to heal completely from nearly any fatal injury. While in its lair, the Tsuchinoko regenerated its head after being decapitated by a full body launch attack from Okarun and survived being pierced from multiple directions by the Evil Eye's grudge ball attack. Due to worm biology, however, the Tsuchinoko is unable handle sunlight exposure and will die as a result of being dried up.
Electrokinesis
Tsuchinoko's electrokinesis
As a Mongolian Death Worm, the Tsuchinoko possesses the natural ability to discharge a large amount of electricity from the tips of its tentacles to attack any nearby enemies.
Phlegm
Tsuchinoko's phlegm
The Tsuchinoko is able to expel a sticky substance that will inhibit its target's mobility. Once trapped, the Tsuchinoko is given the chance to swallow its enemies as they are left helpless. The sticky substance also acts as an effective cooling agent, as Momo used the mucus emitting from the Tsuchinoko's corpse to hose down the magma flowing from the village volcano.
Venom
Tsuchinoko Venom
As a Mongolian Death Worm, the Tsuchinoko possesses the natural ability to create spores that releases a toxic venom to weaken its enemies.


Trivia

The Tsuchinoko is a Japanese cryptid that resembles a snake with a short, stumpy body. It features regularly in popular media throughout Japan.
The Mongolian death worm is a cryptid that supposedly lives in the Gobi Desert, and kills by spraying venom or via electrical discharge.
In Volume 5, the Tsuchinoko's (Mongolian Death Worm) profile extra page suggests that it could have been Minhocão, an Brazilian creature that is variously claimed to be a large fish or to resemble a worm measuring 20 to 50 m (65 to 165 feet), even up to 80 m (260 feet) in length.

Tsuru (つる, Tsuru?) is a police officer at Daija Town and an acquaintance of the Kito Family.[1]

Appearance

Tsuru is a man with pronounced facial features. He wears the standard uniform for a Daija Town police officer, which includes a cap.[1]
Synopsis

Kintama Hunt Saga

Cursed House Arc

After the male members of the Kito family were chased away from Hot Springs Manju by indignant members of the chamber of commerce, officer Tsuru intervened to cover for them and escorted them back to Jiji's house to reunite with the rest of their family.[1]

He returns to the house, now on fire, and asks Momo if she was the arsonist, which she confirms although she immediately shifts the topic to the Kitos who had done human sacrifices for centuries. Tsuru assumes she's talking about the Enjoji family, frustrating Momo, however he orders her to enter the police car so she can get interrogated at the police station. Just as he asks if her parents at home, Momo notices the sunset and she tries to run, shouting to spray more water on the ground to lure out the Mongolian Death Worm, so Tsuru and another cop block her. Just then, the Great Serpent's emerging shakes the ground and Tsuru instructs everyone to stand still, but when it pops out, he and the other civilians run away in fear.

Spirits (霊, Rei?) are deceased humans who have not crossed over to the afterlife and instead roam around amongst the living.


ADVERTISEMENT
Overview


00:00

41:20

Naturally, spirits cannot be seen by humans who are not spiritually aware. Like the living and non-living, spirits possess auras that hold their existence, and without it, the spirit will crumble away into nothingness and will be forgotten by both the dead and the living. Spirits are attracted to things that possess great amounts of life force energy.
Relationship Amongst the Living

As a general rule, Spirit Mediums believe that the dead should not attack the living and that the living should not disrespect the dead, which is why they feel that it is necessary to use force in order to have spirits pass over to the afterlife. Though this was the case, spirits do not believe or follow such things set by human standards.

Classifications

Earthbound Spirits

Earthbound Spirits (地縛霊, Jibakurei?) are spirits who are unable to pass on into the afterlife due to having a strong attachment to a certain place. It is said to be impossible for a Spirit Medium to exorcise a earthbound spirit while they remain in their bound territory since their connection to that place makes them the strongest.

Yokai

Main article: Yokai
Yokai (妖怪, Yōkai?, Literally meaning: Apparition), or Evil Spirits (悪霊, Akuryō?), are spirits who are hostile towards the living. These kinds of spirits have made themselves well-known amongst the living and are given aliases as a result so that humans become wary of their existence.

Guardian Spirit

A Guardian Spirit (護霊, Mamorurei?) is a term referred to by Seiko. While not much of this term has been elaborated on, it is implied, based on Mai Kawabanga, that it is a spirit who is bound to a human due to a desire they wish to have them fulfill before allowing themselves to pass over to the afterlife. While bound, the guardian spirit can offer their spiritual power to them.

Immense Physical Capabilities: Spirits possess inhuman strength, speed and endurance. The Turbo Granny can run at a speed of 100 km/hr, while Acrobatic Silky's reflexes and agility allowed her to avoid being touched by Takakura in his Turbo Granny form.

Fusion: Two spirits can merge together to become one form if they form a pact.
Weaknesses and Termination

Since they can make physical contact with anything in the living world, spirits can be harmed by humans, objects, or substances. Aside from this, the only way to truly harm a spirit, or to have them exterminated, is through the use of spiritual items that causes them to be exorcised to the afterlife.

Aliens (宇宙人, Uchūjin?) is a term that refers to the various extraterrestrial beings existing in outer space (excluding humans inhabiting the planet Earth). It is also a classification for beings who have entered a foreign planet. According to Rokuro Serpo, there are approximately 666 known alien species within the galactic system.

They act as one of the central antagonists in Dandadan, along with yokai.


ADVERTISEMENT
Overview


1/2


While the various races of aliens within the galactic system have made themselves known amongst each other, humanity remains the only known species who are foreign to their existence, with only a few humans who believe that they are real based off a series of conspiracy theories. Three reasons for this are the occurrences of Empty Space, a dimension casted by aliens that conceals their activity to humans, with the exception of those who are spiritually aware, aliens choosing to keep extra-terrestrial life a secret by blending in with their kind using disguises and huge cover-ups mandated by the government, as seen for the Daija Town Incident for example.

Aliens are technologically more advanced than what humans are capable of achieving, such as possessing spaceships, teleportation devices, and nanoskin.

The Serpo Aliens (セルポ星人, Serupo Seijin?) are an entirely identical male race native to Planet Serpo who possess psychokinesis, cybernetic tools installed in their groins, and specialize in advanced technology. While their true appearance are slug-like bipedal creatures, they choose to wear human male disguises.

who have the heads of crabs and strong bipedal humanoid bodies. As a warrior race their bodies are suitable for fighting, possessing immense strength and an immunity to venom. They are capable of fighting on both land and underwater, with the latter environment being where their strength is amplified, however, since they don't possess gills, their time spent underwater is limited by their breathing capacity.

Mr. Mantis Shrimp's Race
are also capable of shapeshifting into a heightened form where their strength is greatly increased.

Kur

Main article: Kur
Takonoka Ru Patcho Kur's appearance
The Kur.
The Kur (深淵クの者ル, Kuru?), a term dubbed by the Serpo, are a race of exosuit wearing octopus aliens who reside in the farthest reaches of space. They are invaders who are hell-bent on conquering numerous planets throughout the cosmos for the purpose of mass producing exosuits through the process of feeding a planet's inhabitants to Big Mamas.

Sumerians

Main article: Sumerians
Sumerians Infobox
The Sumerians.
The Sumerians (シュメール人, Shumēru Hito?) are a race native to Planet Sumer who heavily resemble the human race on Earth, with their sole unique feature being antennas adorning their heads. After Sumer was invaded by the Kur, the Sumerians ended up being on the verge of extinction, with Bamora being the sole surviving child of the race.

Jet Booster Exosuit Kur's Species

Main article: Jet Booster Exosuit Kur
Jet Booster Exosuit Kur's Planet
The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur and her husband on their planet.
They heavily resemble the human race on Earth, with their sole unique feature being their pointy ears. Her species was presumably wiped out when the Kur invaded the planet, forcing her to join their army for survival and she sought to climb the ranks and reach the Emperor, assassinating him and thus avenging her husband and species.



ADVERTISEMENT

Theories

Because the Flatwoods monster activated the chime for evil spirits, Okarun stated that studies revealed a likelihood of spiritually sensitive people also seeing UFOs, meaning spirits and aliens have some points in common. Since the Flatwoods monster got lit on fire, it might mean it appeared as a curse similar to Okarun's Turbo Granny curse.

Knowing that they possess highly advanced science and technology, humans have questioned as to why aliens haven't taken the opportunity to invade Earth. Upon his confrontation with the Serpo, who targeted him for his yokai powers, Okarun theorized that aliens are unable to commence an invasion due to the existence of the yokai all over the world who have powers that surpass their science and technology. Since this is supposedly the case, Okarun also believes that aliens seek to capture humans who somehow came in possession of yokai powers and study them to develop the science needed to combat against the yokai themselves.

It is unknown if aliens possess auras other than species being genetically related to humans, such as Sumerians and more specifically, Bamora.

The Invasion of Sumer was an attack on the planet Sumer by the Kur invaders.


ADVERTISEMENT
Prelude

The sumerian people believed war wouldn't happen in their day and age and decided to shrink down and limit the powers of the government. Unfortunately for them, the Hastur Kur, his right hand Jet Booster Exosuit Kur and the Advance Unit were eventually ordered by the Emperor to prepare the planet Sumer for the incoming invasion.
First Contact

Upon their arrival, the sumerian men who were totally unprepared ended up losing most of the conflicts against the enemy, leading to countless deaths while the survivors were enslaved to produce exosuits by feeding them to Big Mamas. The women who put trust in them were forced to form their own army for survival and because of their scarse numbers, even the elderly were drafted in the conflict. Every day they prayed to their god who would save them on the brink of disaster, although he never seemed to appear.

Planet Idea
Idea, the name given to Earth by the Sumerians.
It is unknown if the Royal Family resorted to escape the planet by warping to their second homeland Idea or if they perished before they could but Banga, one of the chefs who cooked food for the intellectuals visiting the palace, had to leave and enroll in the female army where she met Aja and Tome and they became close, although she avoided putting her trust in others entirely as the devastating outcome of the war was caused by relying on others.
ADVERTISEMENT

Event

Banga rescues Bamora
Banga rescuing a young Bamora in the middle of a battlefield.
The trio fought together until one day Banga spotted an abandoned child in the middle of a battlefield, Bamora, and had a sudden change of heart, resulting in her saving the girl and bringing her to safety. She immediately regrets her decision and she has to clean her clothes while Aja and Tome make fun of her. The latter had rarely seen children since the start of the war and believed that Bamora might be the last sumerian child. This only irritated Banga further because of the incompetent men who had led them in that situation and declared that if someone cannot look after themselves especially in those moments, they might as well die. Bamora started crying and the two ladies stared at Banga to see if she was going to stick by what she said. The frustrated granny brought Bamora along during their fights and they grew up together, teaching her to write, showing her how to cook and clean and forcing her to pray in front of the sumerian god. She told her how they pray every day for God to come and save them but she was certain that it was just a bunch of lies. Yet, she would feel sick if she didn't venerate him as a result of the brainwashing traditions. She explained how they got to that point because they had relied on weak and coward people, even God, so she declared that she would survive the conflict even if it meant sacrificing those around her.

Banga raising Bamora
Banga raising Bamora throughout the years.
Several years passed and Bamora grew up in a vibrant girl who recognized Banga as her mother. She refused to be called like that although Bamora didn't listen to her. Tome and Aja were happy to see her now big and strong compared to when she was a child and they considered her the child of all sumerians, much to Banga's disdain. The leader of their platoon then informed them on the reunion with another pack of about three thousand sumerians. Everyone was excited by the news as they could win the war with those numbers although Banga was unsure of their survival. While traversing the jungle, they bumped into an alien squad feeding captured soldiers to the Big Mama, producing exosuits which were then transferred to the Kur's main base. Between the exosuits, one popped out that closely resembled the sumerian god, which Banga justified by claiming they were praying to God as they died and their hate was embodied in that weapon. Bamora pleaded to save them but when she's told that they might end up like them if they don't reunite with the other soldiers as soon as possible, she returns to the formation.

After a long journey to the West, the platoon reached a opening where they should have met with the other soldiers who were unexpectedly missing. Everyone was frightened until Banga, who maintained her focus, noticed a hologram and screamed out to the others. The Kur's ambush worked and they opened fire while the soldiers were forced to retreat to the forest where another group of aliens were waiting for them. As they got decimated, Bamora's backpack was hit and she had a panic attack before Banga picked her up and screamed at her to focus on surviving. Tome and Aja found an escape route and they covered each other while they made their way out of the battlefield. The night fell and only Banga, Bamora, Tome and Aja were the survivors of the ambush who had to find shelter in a cave nearby. Banga was bleeding out and Bamora rushed to apply a bandaid despite her refusing. She kicked her away and Bamora couldn't understand why she was doing this, to which she stated that they weren't family but strangers even though they spent all those years together, and she reminded her that they lost the war because they had put their trust in others, so Bamora would need to save the bandaids for herself.

Chapter 103
Banga, Bamora, Tome and Aja following the ambush of the Kur who decimated their army.
Realizing that there's no way they can defeat the aliens now, Tome revealed that she lived in a small mountain town and never had the chance to see the ocean. She stood up and joked around with Aja who decided to accompany her in their last mission. The two smiled as they seemingly looked at Banga and Bamora's faces for the final time before leaving. Bamora crawled into Banga's lap and the granny questioned what she was doing, to which she informed she was going to die right there because Banga was the one who had picked her up all those years ago. The girl pleaded her mother to kill her because she was fine with dying by the hands of her instead of the aliens. Banga initially agreed to the request and pointed the rifle to the child's head when she was suddenly hit with a wave of guilt and sadness as she revealed she was a chef in the royal palace who used her hands to prepare wonderful dishes and never wanted to point guns towards others. She burst into tears and Bamora followed soon after, embracing each other for a small and desperate moment. Banga suddenly recalled the myth of the second homeland Idea while she worked as a chef in the royal palace, so she regained her distant composure and suggested Bamora to put everything they had left to hopefully escape the planet. They assisted Tome and Aja who couldn't traverse the jungle due to Kur soldiers blocking their path and they reunited to reach the pyramid which functioned as a warp gate to Idea.

Chapter 104
The group sneaking their way into the Kur's base to escape to Idea using the pyramid.
The four snuck their way into the camp surveilled by the Kur in front of the pyramid. Bamora noticed all the male prisoners, who she had never seen since she was a baby and Banga was surprised to see them as she believed they had been decimated years ago. The girl immediately wishes to free the men but Tome refuses as they were there to flee Sumer in the first place. Banga quickly realized they would need more numbers to have a shot in breaking into the pyramid and using the warp gate, so Bamora rushed in the crowd to undo their restraints while hiding from the guards. The grannies were surprised by this strong course of action but they followed her since Bamora had always wanted to save others and she became confident enough to do just that, compared to the many battles they fought before in which she trembled and panicked. The child began saving one of the men and instructed them to keep looking forward, but once freed, the man started running away, blowing their cover. One of the Kurs shot the trespasser and Bamora barely dodged the shot before taking down the enemy. All the other aliens began opening fire and the grannies had to throw their remaining smokes to make their way through. The Takonoka Ru Patcho Kur from the Kur Advance Unit sent out a barrage of missiles towards Bamora but Banga pushed her out of the way just in time, although she was severely hurt in the process. Bamora couldn't believe it and she begged for her mother to get up before trying to carry her away. Aja seized her away from Banga and explained they had to reach the pyramid by all means necessary, even by leaving behind the wounded Banga, since Bamora was the last sumerian child and she must live for their species' sake. Unbeknownst to them, Banga survived and she was mad due to the girl calling her her mother again when an explosion suddenly revealed the exosuit which resembled the sumerian god.

Sumerian rebellion
Banga succesfully instigating the sumerian men into a massive rebellion against the invaders.
Bamora rushed to the pyramid although she kept crying because of her mother's death when she reached the Big Mama who menacingly stared at her. She turned around and noticed the Ta Kowasa Kur and the Ta Komeshi Kur, two other members of the Advance Unit, pinning down Tome and Aja while doing serious damage to her bodies. Bamora, now surrounded by countless enemies, called out to her mother as the Big Mama thrust forward to eat her alive. Out of nowhere, the giant sumerian god punched and totally annihilated the creature, saving Bamora, leaving her dazzled. The god then swung her tail around and freed Aja and Tome from their captors. The sumerian men couldn't believe their god finally appeared and begged to be saved from the aliens. Suddenly, Banga's voice emanated through the sumerian god exosuit, claiming that she didn't care about their survival. She continued by saying that they did not attempt to protect the child who tried to rescue them in the first place, stating that Bamora was the last sumerian child and her future rested on her shoulders. She instigated the men by pointing out that their families and their planet were now stolen while they counted on someone else to save them. She screamed to get angry at their invaders, to use any means necessary to recover what was theirs and to defend Bamora for their species' sake.

Bamora and Banga separate
Banga declaring her love to Bamora while she's warped towards Idea.
With numbers now on their side, the sumerians easily overwhelm the Kur and kill lots of aliens through sheer strength. Aja quickly recovered and deployed support fire for Bamora while Tome, on a high platform of the camp, shot many enemies and got to see the ocean for the very first time. With the tides of the fight now turned, Bamora was able to enter into the pyramid and reached the warp gate, although the slab was barely comprehensible and she did not know how to activate it. Suddenly, Banga appeared behind her, heavily wounded, and succesfully calibrated the warp gate to Idea. She then gave Bamora the exosuit, explaining that the gate has enough energy for only one person. She obviously refused since Banga needed medical attention and she declared she would find a way to escape too when out of nowhere, Banga punched her into the gate, sealing her inside. Bamora kept trying to force her way out while the granny instructed her to start a new life on Idea, where she would experience lots of love and eventually marry someone. Because she never understood men, Banga suggested to marry a strong man to make strong kids and pass down the blood of the sumerians, claiming it's the least solace there can be for those who died in the war. Bamora screamed out and called her mother again, causing her to burst into tears due to the maternal feelings she kept inside her for all this time. She couldn't handle it in anymore as Bamora was so much precious to her and everyone else, so she crawled towards the wall and put her hand on the barrier, declaring she truly loved Bamora like her daughter just as she was transported away to Idea.
ADVERTISEMENT

Post-Bamora's Escape

Chapter 106
The Hastur Kur approaching Banga after Bamora escaped with their suit.
The Hastur Kur and other members of the Advance Unit breached into the pyramid, holding Aja captive, and approached Banga, with their leader revealing they had never seen a Big Mama produce a suit of such capabilities. With the name "Bamora" echoing through their minds as the thief who stole their most powerful exosuit, he declared they are going to chase her down through the universe and eventually adorn the top of the pyramid they were in with her head. The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur tried to decipher the slab in vain, claiming it could only be activated by a sumerian. Banga affirms they never will since she won't cooperate, however she needs to take a decision when the Hastur Kur holds Aja and slightly pierces her with the suit's nails, asking if lower life-forms like Banga knew about mental programming and threatens to torture her if she doesn't reveal the inner workings of the slab.

Banga, Tome, and Aja leave Sumer
Banga, Tome and Aja making their way to Idea after they pushed back the invaders.
It is not revealed how Banga got out of this deadlock, however the Kur Advance Unit eventually made their way to Earth while following Bamora's footsteps to reclaim their suit. Banga, Tome and Aja, with the dangerous Advance Unit members now away from Sumer and with the help of the sumerian men who finally acted to save their planet, together they pushed back the alien invaders and soon got controls of spaceships. In one of them, a couple men are seen shooting at the Kur with cannons along with Tome while Aja repaired the ship's wiring. Banga, who was manuevering the ship into space, affirmed they were going to Idea despite not knowing how many light years away it was. She excitingly declared to Bamora that they were now staring a space odyssey and make their way to Bamora to see each other again.
Aftermath

Jet Booster Exosuit Kur Infobox 2
The Jet Booster Exosuit Kur's real form.
The Invasion of Sumer is likely still ongoing, with the sumerians now in the lead against the invaders. Still, the escape of Bamora to Earth caused the events of the Kaiju Arc and the Space Globalists Arc, leading to the defeat of the Kur Advance Unit and their main fleet. Only one of them survived, the Jet Booster Exosuit Kur, secretly not a Kur who snuck in the army to rise through the ranks to murder the emperor.
